chapters.title: Chapter 8: Opening of the Trading House, Goblin Archer
paragraphs: As long as Leon was the one who contributed the most to a battle, it seemed his talent would always activate without fail. That much was clear now.

Whether it required him to land the finishing blow was something he still needed to test. He wondered if striking a monster once and letting others kill it would count, or if the system was stricter than that.
Either way, those details could wait. What mattered now were the rewards.
Leon opened his storage space and looked through the items he had obtained from the mutated goblin.
[Eternal Coins x10]
[Mutated Small Goblin Essence: Consuming will increase strength by 3.]
[Goblin Machete +2 (Common): +15 Attack, +6 Strength.]
He stared at the list for a moment, then let out a quiet breath.
"I guess it doesn’t change much if the mutated monster doesn’t have many differences," he muttered.
In the end, that creature had still been a goblin. Taller, more aggressive, and stronger than usual, yes, but not fundamentally different.
Mutations raised stats, not rarity. Bosses were the ones that truly warped the rules.

Without hesitating, Leon consumed the essence first. A warm sensation spread through his body, flowing into his muscles and settling there, familiar by now. Strength rose, and with it, his overall stability in combat.
Next, he pulled out the machete. He already had one identical to it in his storage. There was no reason to keep both separate.
Fwish!
[You have consumed two identical equipments... enhancement successful!]
When the light faded, Leon now had two [Goblin Machete +3] with him. One was already equipped. The other sat unused, sharp and heavy, its stats noticeably higher than before.
’Maybe I could give it to David or one of his teammates,’ Leon thought briefly. ’But they’ll be fine, I think.’
David and Aaron were competent, and more importantly, cautious. They wouldn’t die anytime soon if they kept playing it smart.

Still, Leon couldn’t ignore the thought that his presence here, his interference compared to his past life, might cause a snowball effect. Even small changes could eventually spiral into something unpredictable.
He pushed the thought aside and kept moving.
The deeper he went into the [Wild Forest], the more monsters he encountered. Demonized rats scurried between roots and rocks, their red eyes glowing faintly in the dim light beneath the canopy.
Leon killed them without hesitation, fireballs bursting through their bodies or his machete cleaving them apart in a single swing.

At one point, he encountered a mutated demonized rat. Larger than the others, its muscles swollen unnaturally, its movements erratic and aggressive. It lunged at him with surprising speed, but Leon met it head-on, crushing it without mercy.
Fwish!
[Demonized Rat Essence: Consuming will increase constitution by 2.]
Leon consumed it immediately. His body felt heavier, sturdier, as if his bones and organs had been reinforced from within.
He checked his status again, eyes narrowing slightly as the numbers updated.
[Combat Power: 190 (+124)]
Leon let out a low whistle.
His combat power had officially surpassed 300. That meant level 4 monsters would no longer pose a real threat to him. He could fight them cleanly, without needing to gamble his life.
A wide grin spread across his face.
"I’m not far from level 3 either," he said to himself. "Once I reach it, I’ll be able to unlock the [Level Ranking]."
Rankings were more than just bragging rights. In the future, they shaped reputation, drew attention, and influenced how gods and factions viewed players from all races.
Leon knew better than anyone how dangerous that could be, but he also knew how powerful it was to stand at the top early.
Just as he was about to keep moving forward, a familiar sound echoed in his ears.
Ding!

Voices immediately erupted across the system channels.

"What kind of junk is this? They’re selling novice machetes for five Eternal Coins. Are they trying to scam people?"

Fireball!
A demonized rat exploded in flames. Leon dashed forward, cutting down a small goblin before narrowly avoiding an arrow that whistled past his head.

[Archer Goblin]
[Level: 3]
[Combat Power: 220]
[Details: A goblin that wields a bow and fires arrows. Becomes defenseless once at close range.]

Fwish!

Ding!
[You have killed "Goblin Archer" and gained 15 experience points.]
[You have killed...]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered. Items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
The system messages stacked rapidly, and then—
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 3!]
[You have gained 5 points in all attributes, and 5 free points to distribute.]
Leon exhaled slowly.
’Perfect.’
His growth was steady, efficient. Exactly how he wanted it.
Without hesitation, he allocated the five free points into [Spirit]. Now that he had spells, his spell efficiency mattered far more than raw physical stats alone.
After that, he equipped the necklace he had been waiting to use.
[Purple Jade Necklace (Rare): +15 Spirit, +20 Constitution. Comes with the "Purple Jade" defensive skill. Requirement: Level 3.]
The moment he equipped it, a faint protective sensation wrapped around his body, subtle but reassuring. His stats surged again, and Leon immediately checked his combat power.
[Combat Power: 240 (+194)]
"Haha!" Leon laughed openly this time. "Incredible."
He clenched his fist, feeling the strength and stability coursing through him.
"I might actually be able to complete that quest sooner than expected now."
And with that thought firmly in mind, Leon turned his gaze deeper into the forest, already planning his next move.

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Unlocking The Level Leaderboard, Heading to The Secret Quest
paragraphs: At the same time Leon reached level three, not too far away, near a wide clearing deep inside the forest, another fight had just ended.
Fwish!
The massive body of a giant blue frog collapsed onto the ground, its thick blood seeping into the dirt and staining the grass beneath it. The creature twitched once, then went completely still.
Standing around the corpse were four exhausted but excited players: David’s team.
David wiped the sweat from his brow and looked down at the weapon in his hands, his grip tightening around the handle of his machete. His face slowly broke into a wide grin.
"This [Goblin Machete +3] is insane," he said, unable to hide his excitement. "We can even take down a boss with this thing now."
Aaron laughed as he leaned on his shield, nodding in agreement.
The fight had been smoother than expected, and the damage David had dealt was on a completely different level compared to before.
"Good," Eleonore said with a grin of her own, lowering her bow slightly. "At least I’m not the one dealing the most damage anymore."
Even though she fought from long range, her arrows were still terrifyingly strong.
More than once, she had killed monsters in a single shot, and only David’s enhanced weapon had finally taken that role away from her.
"Fifty experience points," Aaron said cheerfully, checking his panel. "That boss was worth it. You all got the same, right?"
"Yep~"
"I did too."
David let out a satisfied breath and straightened his posture. "I’m almost level three now," he said, clearly pleased. "If we keep going like this, we might be the first team to reach it."
But the moment those words left his mouth, a familiar sound echoed through the clearing.
Ding!
A system announcement rang clearly, cutting through the atmosphere and drawing everyone’s attention.
[Player "Leon Rykard" in "Novice Village #1" has successfully advanced to Level 3, unlocking the Level Leaderboard.]
[It will constantly show the level ranking of the top 25 players above Level 3.]
David froze.
"What?" His jaw dropped slightly as he stared at the floating text. "I thought I was fast, but... he beat me to it?"
Aaron scratched his chin, his expression thoughtful rather than shocked. "That’s Leon. The guy we saw earlier," he said slowly. "The one who sold you the goblin machete."
He paused for a moment before adding, "Looks like he really was strong enough to go solo."
Almost instantly, players all across the novice village opened the new panel that had just unlocked.
[Level Leaderboard:]
[1. Leon Skyward: Level 3]
Since no one else had reached level three yet, Leon’s name stood alone at the top of the leaderboard.
That single fact alone made waves.

His name was already spreading far faster than it ever had in his past life. Back then, even with an S-Level Talent, Leon had never once appeared in the top twenty-five. He had always lagged behind, cautious and underprepared.
This time was different. And there was a reason for that.
’Itshould happen soon,’ Leon thought calmly as he continued moving through the forest. ’Now that the Trading House is open, it won’t take long.’
Before he could dwell further on that thought, more system panels appeared, one after another, visible to every player.
Ding!
[Level promotions will be rewarded.]
[The first to reach Level 10 will be rewarded with a Legendary Treasure Chest.]
[The 2nd-3rd to reach Level 10 will be rewarded with an Epic Treasure Chest.]
[The 4th-10th will be rewarded with an Elite Treasure Chest.]
[The 11th-25th will be rewarded with a Rare Treasure Chest.]
[All remaining players will receive a Uncommon Treasure Chest upon reaching Level 10.]
Leon’s eyes narrowed slightly as he read through the list. In his past life, he had only ever received an [Uncommon Treasure Chest].
He remembered that disappointment clearly. By the time he reached level ten back then, the rewards that truly mattered were already gone.
But this time? This time, it would be different.
With his current talent, aiming for the legendary chest wasn’t just possible, it was logical.
Getting every single item inside a Legendary Treasure Chest would completely change his early trajectory.
It would give him a massive advantage that could carry him far beyond the novice stage.
Ding!
Another panel appeared.
[Since you are the first to reach Level 3, you have been rewarded with 10 Reputation Points.]
[When Reputation Points reach certain thresholds, rewards can be obtained.]
"Oh," Leon muttered softly.

Reputation points were rare and valuable, especially this early. They affected how systems, NPCs, and even certain quests responded to a player. Getting ten of them right away was a significant boost.
When the announcements finally ended, the entire novice village was buzzing.
"How the hell is he leveling that fast?"
"Overpowered talent, probably."
"Figures..."
Even experienced players were shaken. David and his team exchanged looks, their excitement turning into renewed determination.
"Alright," David said firmly. "No slacking off. If we can’t get the legendary chest, we’ll at least aim for the epic ones."
"Yeah!"
Back in the forest, Leon checked everything one last time and confirmed that his status was stable. There was no reason to stop now.
Then the notifications came.
Ding! Ding! Ding!
[You have received a friend request from "Oscar Daniels."]
[You have received a friend request from...]
[You have received...]
The requests flooded in rapidly. Dozens of them. Leon frowned slightly and muted the notifications without hesitation.
He had no interest in accepting random players. Connections were important, but only the right ones. Blind trust was a luxury he couldn’t afford.
Instead, he opened the map that had been unlocked through his [Appraisal] skill and began scanning it carefully.
"The secret quest should still be available," he murmured. "No one else could’ve found it yet."
His eyes moved slowly across the terrain markers, paths, and shaded regions. Then, after only a few seconds, they stopped.
Leon’s gaze sharpened. There it was.
A small, almost unnoticeable opening tucked between uneven terrain, barely visible unless someone knew exactly where to look. It was the entrance to a cave.
Exactly where he remembered it.
Without the map, finding it would’ve been nearly impossible. Even back in his past life, he had only stumbled across it by accident, and far too late.
Leon didn’t waste another second. He moved quickly toward the location, pushing his pace despite the rising danger around him.
The area surrounding the cave was home to level four and five monsters, far stronger than what most players could handle right now.
But Leon didn’t slow down.
After roughly ten minutes of careful but swift movement, he finally reached the cave entrance.
This was the place. A quest that no one had ever completed in his past life.
The reason was simple. It was time-based. If players didn’t complete it within a few hours of entering [Eternal Ascension], it disappeared forever.
The first time Leon had entered this cave, all he had found was a corpse.
This time—
"H-Hello?" a weak voice echoed from within.
Leon stepped inside and immediately spotted a woman leaning against the cave wall. Her breathing was shallow, her body trembling.
"P-Please... I need your help..."
"Bingo," Leon said quietly, a grin forming. "I wasn’t late."
The woman had pale, beautiful skin and pointed elf ears.
She wore a robe and clutched a scepter tightly in one hand. But her condition was terrible. Blood stained her lips, and she coughed violently, her life force visibly fading.
"My name is Emilia," she said weakly. "I-I was attacked by [Poison Snakes]... I don’t think I can last much longer..."
Ding!
[You have triggered the S-Level Novice Village Quest: "Save the Poisoned Elf."]
[Time Limit: 1 Hour 14 Minutes.]
Leon’s expression turned serious.
Emilia had died quickly in his past life. No one had reached her in time. By the time players discovered this cave back then, it was already too late.
But now? Now there was a chance.
"I-I think some of the snakes may drop an antidote," Emilia continued, her voice barely above a whisper. "But... I don’t think you’ll have enough time..."
She coughed again, her body sagging further against the wall.
[Quest Objective: Bring the antidote to Emilia to save her from her cruel fate.]
[Reward: Elite Treasure Chest and 500 Eternal Coins.]
Leon clenched his fist.
’Yeah,’ he thought firmly. ’There’s no way I’m letting this slip.’
This time, he would change the outcome.

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Emilia Verdant, The Poison Cave
paragraphs: "T-The poison snakes are deeper inside the cave," Emilia said weakly, her voice trembling as she leaned against the cold stone wall. "Please... I need to return to my own instance..."
Leon frowned slightly as he looked at her. "How did you even get here in the first place?" he asked calmly. "Races should be separated at the start of [Eternal Ascension]."
At those words, Emilia’s eyes widened in visible shock. "Wait... how do you even—"
"No matter," Leon interrupted before she could finish, his tone firm. "I’ll get you the antidote."
She stared at him for a moment, clearly confused, but then slowly nodded. "...Alright. Thank you."
Before turning away, Leon activated [Appraisal] on her, wanting to at least get a clearer idea of who he was trying to save.
[Name: Emilia Verdant]
[Level: 8]
[Talent: ???]
[Skills: ???]
[Combat Power: ???]
[Status: Poisoned.]
Leon narrowed his eyes slightly. He still couldn’t see most of her information, but at least her name was now clear.
’Verdant...’ he thought, rubbing his chin lightly. ’That family name...’

In his past life, Emilia had died too quickly for anyone to learn anything about her. She never played any role afterward, never influenced the world in any way. She had simply vanished, another forgotten casualty of the early game.
But this time was different. If he saved her, things could change.
And so, without wasting another second, Leon turned and headed deeper into the cave, his steps steady and his focus sharp.

As he descended further, the air around him slowly changed. It became damp and heavy, carrying a faint stench that irritated his nose. The walls narrowed slightly, and faint, unsettling sounds echoed from somewhere ahead.
Then a system panel appeared in front of his vision.
Ding!
[You have entered the Level 5 Zone: "Poison Cave."]
"Expected," Leon muttered.
[Eternal Ascension] was filled with zones like this, special areas layered with danger, resources, and challenges. Some held powerful monsters, others rare items or hidden quests.
But one thing was always the same: entering them meant risking your life.
Since players only had one chance, many avoided zones entirely, choosing safer paths instead.
Leon didn’t have that luxury. He needed the antidote.
He continued forward, descending deeper into the cave until it finally opened into a wide chamber. The faint glow of bioluminescent moss illuminated the area just enough for him to see clearly.
And what he saw made him tense slightly.
Several long, dark shapes slithered across the stone floor.
[Poison Snake]
[Level: 5]
[Combat Power: 400]
[Details: Extremely fast. Their venom will slowly kill the victim after being bitten.]
"Damn," Leon muttered.
Each of these snakes had combat power close to his own. One mistake would be enough to poison him, and that poison would not be something he could easily deal with.
Leon quickly scanned the area.
’I don’t see a boss,’ he thought. ’But it has to be nearby.’

Emilia had said that the snakes carried the antidote, but Leon knew better. Normal monsters rarely held quest-critical items. If there was an antidote, it would almost certainly drop from a stronger variant, or a boss.

That was why no one had completed this quest in his past life. Even if someone found Emilia in time, risking everything to fight a boss-level poison monster was not a decision many were willing to make.
Fireball!
Leon launched a fireball toward the nearest snake. Flames exploded on impact, scorching its scales and sending it crashing against the cave wall.
But it didn’t die. Instead, the snake twisted its body and lifted its head, locking its cold eyes onto Leon.
Hiss!
A low, sharp hiss echoed through the chamber. In response, the other snakes slowly turned toward him as well.
One by one, they began slithering forward. Six of them. Leon didn’t move.
"Well," he said calmly, a faint grin forming, "guess I’ll just kill you all and see what you drop."
Fwish!
The moment the snakes lunged, Leon rushed forward instead of retreating.
Vision Enhancement!
The world around him shifted instantly. Every movement became clearer, slower, easier to read. The snapping jaws of the snakes looked almost sluggish under his enhanced vision.
He twisted his body, narrowly dodging two strikes, then slashed downward with his machete.
Crunch!
Steel met flesh as one snake’s tail was severed cleanly.
HIIISSS!
The creature thrashed violently, its body slamming against the stone floor.
Leon didn’t hesitate. He knew that with similar combat power, brute force wouldn’t be enough. He had to fight smart.
Snake-type monsters almost always shared the same weakness: their tails.
Another snake lunged toward his arm, its fangs inches away from his skin. Leon leaned back just in time, then swung his machete in a clean arc.
Slash!
The snake’s head separated from its body, rolling across the stone floor.
Fireball!
Leon immediately followed up, launching another fireball at the snake he had injured earlier. Already weakened, it couldn’t withstand the impact and collapsed lifelessly. Three down.
The remaining snakes didn’t retreat. Instead, they circled him, striking again and again, trying to exploit even the smallest opening.
Leon stayed calm.
He dodged, blocked, and countered, relying on his enhanced vision and agility. Every movement was deliberate. Every strike was calculated.
By the time the thirty seconds of [Vision Enhancement] ended, the chamber was silent. All six poison snakes lay dead on the ground.
Ding!
[You have killed x6 "Poison Snake" and gained 120 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered. Items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
"Perfect," Leon said quietly.
He immediately checked the items he had obtained.
[Eternal Coins x30]
[Skill Stone x2]
[Poison Fang Dagger x3 (Common): +10 Attack. Applies "Poison."]
[Poison Snake Essence x6: Consuming will increase Agility by 3.]
Leon frowned slightly.
As expected, there was no antidote.
Even with his [100% Drop Rate] talent, nothing appeared. That meant none of these snakes carried it.
Without hesitation, Leon consumed all six essences. A familiar warmth spread through his body as his agility increased by eighteen points.
Then his attention shifted to the skill stones.
"Hm."
He summoned them into his hands and crushed them without hesitation, focusing on his existing abilities.
Ding!
[Congratulations! "Fireball (Level 1)" has been upgraded to "Fireball (Level 2)."]
Ding!
[Congratulations! "Vision Enhancement (Level 1)" has been upgraded to "Vision Enhancement (Level 2)."]
[Vision Enhancement (Level 2): Consumes Spirit to enhance dynamic vision for 45 seconds. Cooldown: 2 minutes.]
[Fireball (Level 2): Condense your spirit into a larger fireball with increased power.]
Leon exhaled slowly.
Both skills had improved, which meant his overall combat ability had risen again.
’Perfect,’ he thought.
Next, he looked at the three [Poison Fang Daggers]. They were decent weapons, especially with the poison effect, but they were still weaker than his fully enhanced goblin machete.
’Maybe I can improve them.’
Leon selected two of the daggers and initiated enhancement.
Fwish!
[You have consumed two identical equipments... Enhancement failed.]
Crack!
The daggers shattered in his hands, dissolving into fragments of light.
Leon sighed. "Guess I’ll need more."
Then—
Ding!
[Quest Warning: Only 1 Hour Remains.]
"Shit," Leon muttered. "Gotta move fast."
Time was becoming the biggest problem. Finding the antidote wasn’t enough. He still had to return to Emilia before the timer ran out.
If he went too far or wasted time, the quest would fail no matter what.
Leon immediately rushed forward, pushing deeper into the cave.
Soon, he encountered another group of monsters. But this time, one of them stood out.
It was larger than the others, its scales darker, its presence far more oppressive.
[Poison Snake (Mutated)]
[Level: 5]
[Combat Power: 500]
[Details: A mutated poison snake. Its venom causes instant death upon biting.]
Leon stared at it, his expression tightening.
"Ah shit," he sighed quietly. "That thing’s combat power is higher than mine."
And yet, he didn’t turn back.

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Defeating Monsters, Poisonous Mushroom Leader
paragraphs: Fireball!
Leon summoned another fireball, but this time it was clearly different from the ones before.
The condensed flames burned brighter, denser, and carried far more heat as his improved skill poured extra power into it.
BOOM!
The fireball slammed directly into the mutated poison snake, erupting in a violent explosion of flame.
The monster screeched as its scales cracked and burned, its body thrown back several meters.
One of the regular poison snakes beside it wasn’t nearly as lucky, it was caught in the blast and reduced to a charred corpse almost instantly.
’Amazing,’ Leon thought, his eyes narrowing slightly.
This was the true difference that leveled skills made. The increase wasn’t subtle. A single level turned something usable into something genuinely deadly.
HISSS!
The mutated poison snake let out a sharp, furious hiss, its yellow eyes locking onto Leon as it ordered the remaining snakes to attack.
The creatures lunged forward in unison, their bodies low and fast as they attempted to overwhelm him with numbers.
But after only a few seconds, it became clear that they stood no chance.
Slash!
Leon stepped forward and cut one down cleanly, his movements sharp and controlled.
Another snake tried to coil around his leg, but he twisted his body and drove his blade down, splitting its head open.
One by one, the poison snakes fell, their speed no longer enough to threaten him.
Soon, only the mutated monster remained.
Monsters’ [Combat Power] wasn’t just a flat number. It was calculated based on attributes, skills, and sometimes even equipment-like traits.
In the case of this mutated poison snake, the reason its combat power was so high was simple: its speed was absurd.
Before Leon could fully reposition himself, the snake suddenly vanished from where it stood, its body blurring as it shot forward.
In the next instant, its jaws were already clamped down on Leon’s arm.
Leon reacted immediately, but not fast enough to stop the bite outright.
Purple Jade! Fwoosh!
A violet glow burst to life around Leon’s arm as the defensive skill from his [Purple Jade Necklace] activated.
A translucent layer of jade-like energy formed at the exact point of impact, blocking the snake’s fangs before they could pierce his flesh.
"Hiss?"
The mutated poison snake recoiled slightly, clearly confused by the sudden resistance.
That hesitation was all Leon needed.
Slash!
Leon swung his weapon upward, carving a deep wound across the snake’s neck. Before it could even scream, he followed up with a spell.
Fireball!
The flames detonated at point-blank range, engulfing the snake entirely.
Ding!
[You have killed x4 "Poison Snake" and gained 80 experience points.]
[You have killed "Poison Snake (Mutated)" and gained 50 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered, items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
Leon exhaled slowly and opened his storage space almost immediately.
But once again... there was no antidote.
He didn’t dwell on it for long. Instead, he consumed the essences dropped by the snakes, feeling his body grow lighter and more responsive as his agility increased by another sixteen points.
Then another system message appeared.
Ding!
[You have consumed two identical equipments... enhancement successful!]
Leon’s lips curled into a grin.
"Nice."
[Poison Fang Dagger +2 (Common): +30 Attack, +10 Strength. Applies "Poison" on target.]
The dagger’s stats now rivaled his [Goblin Machete +3], and on top of that, it carried a poison effect. Against living enemies, that alone made it extremely dangerous.
Leon didn’t hesitate.
Fwish!
He equipped the [Poison Fang Dagger +2], feeling its balance settle perfectly into his hand. Immediately after, he opened the [Trading House].
He listed his [Goblin Machete +3] for sale, this time pricing it at 50 Eternal Coins.
And almost instantly—
Ding!
[Your "Goblin Machete +3" has been sold.]
Leon raised an eyebrow, amused.
’I guess people are really watching me now.’

He didn’t care much either way. If anything, it worked in his favor. As long as he kept moving forward and killing monsters, he could continuously supply powerful equipment to other players and profit from it.
To everyone else, the items he sold were absurdly strong. To Leon, they were just extras.
Among the other drops, one item stood out.
[Poison Potion (Uncommon): Drink to be poisoned.]
"...No thank you."
Leon shook his head and tossed it back into storage. He had no intention of using it now, though he made a mental note that it might be useful later.
’I’ll only really be able to move forward after Level 10,’ Leon thought as he pushed deeper into the cave. ’Only then does the real [Eternal Ascension] begin.’
Everything before that was little more than a brutal tutorial.
After reaching Level 10, players would be transported to the [Novice Divine Temple] for their first assessment. That was when things truly started to separate the strong from the weak.
But Leon wasn’t there yet. So he focused on what was in front of him.
He continued slaughtering [Poison Snakes], cutting through [Poison Archers], and clearing chamber after chamber.
Time passed quickly as his movements grew smoother and more efficient.
By the time he reached the deepest part of the cave, his agility had increased even further, and he had collected enough [Poison Fang Daggers] to enhance his own weapon again.
Fwish!
[Poison Fang Dagger +3 (Common): +50 Attack, +25 Strength. Applies "Poison" on target.]
Leon examined the blade for a moment, satisfied.
Then he stepped forward. And finally... he saw it. At the very end of the cave stood the boss.
[Poisonous Mushroom Leader (Boss)]
[Level: 5]
[Combat Power: 650]
[Details: A mutated mushroom that releases toxic spores into the air.]
"Damn," Leon muttered.
The creature was massive, its body resembling a grotesque mushroom with thick roots anchoring it to the ground.
A gaping mouth split its stem, lined with jagged growths, while yellow, unblinking eyes stared directly at Leon.
Around it were several [Poison Snakes], one of them mutated, as well as multiple [Poison Archers] perched along the cave walls.
The moment Leon stepped into the chamber, the battle began.
Fireball!
Leon launched his spell without hesitation. The fireball struck the boss directly, flames spreading rapidly across its fungal body.
’I mean... it’s a mushroom,’ Leon thought with a faint grin. ’Of course it’s weak to fire.’
Vision Enhancement!
He activated his skill immediately as the poison snakes lunged and the poison archers fired their arrows. The world slowed, every attack becoming easy to read.
Leon moved through the chaos, dodging arrows, cutting down snakes, and repositioning with ease.
But the boss wasn’t idle.
Poisonous Spores!
The [Poisonous Mushroom Leader] shook violently, releasing a thick green haze that spread throughout the cave.
’Can’t breathe that,’ Leon thought sharply.
He closed his mouth and held his breath, but even then—
Ding!
[You have been afflicted with "Poison."]
"...Figures," Leon muttered.
Even standing near the thing was enough. He knew he had to finish the fight fast.
Within twenty seconds, most of the monsters were dead. Only the mutated poison snake and a few archers remained.
Fireball!
Leon incinerated the archers in one blast, then rushed forward and cut down the mutated snake.
And just like that, only the boss remained.
Fueled by his now monstrous agility, over one hundred, he dashed forward in a blur and stopped right in front of the [Poisonous Mushroom Leader].
"Give me that antidote," Leon said calmly.
Slash!
He drove his dagger deep into the boss’s body. The poison effect didn’t activate, as expected, but the damage was severe.
Leon leapt back and raised his arm.
Fireball!
BOOM!
The explosion tore through the boss, flames consuming it entirely. Its body blackened and collapsed, its life force fading rapidly.
Ding!
[You have killed "Poisonous Mushroom Leader" and gained 400 experience points.]
[You have killed "Poison Snake (Mutated)" and gained 50 experience points.]
[You have killed...]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered, items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
"Perfect."
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 4!]
[You have gained 5 points in all attributes and 5 free points to distribute.]
Leon let out a slow breath.
Only then did he fully realize just how much he had done while still technically being a low-level player.
Without wasting time, he opened his storage space, eyes sharp as he searched for the one thing that mattered most.

Around it were several [Poison Snakes], one of them mutated, as well as multiple [Poison Archers] perched along the cave walls.
The moment Leon stepped into the chamber, the battle began.
Fireball!
Leon launched his spell without hesitation.
The fireball struck the boss directly, flames spreading rapidly across its fungal body.
’I mean... it’s a mushroom,’ Leon thought with a faint grin. ’Of course it’s weak to fire.’
Vision Enhancement!
He activated his skill immediately as the poison snakes lunged and the poison archers fired their arrows.
The world slowed, every attack becoming easy to read.
Leon moved through the chaos, dodging arrows, cutting down snakes, and repositioning with ease.
But the boss wasn’t idle.
Poisonous Spores!
The [Poisonous Mushroom Leader] shook violently, releasing a thick green haze that spread throughout the cave.
’Can’t breathe that,’ Leon thought sharply.
He closed his mouth and held his breath, but even then—
Ding!
[You have been afflicted with "Poison."]
"...Figures," Leon muttered.
Even standing near the thing was enough.
He knew he had to finish the fight fast.
Within twenty seconds, most of the monsters were dead.
Only the mutated poison snake and a few archers remained.
Fireball!
Leon incinerated the archers in one blast, then rushed forward and cut down the mutated snake.
And just like that, only the boss remained.
Fueled by his now monstrous agility, over one hundred, he dashed forward in a blur and stopped right in front of the [Poisonous Mushroom Leader].
"Give me that antidote," Leon said calmly.
Slash!
He drove his dagger deep into the boss’s body.
The poison effect didn’t activate, as expected, but the damage was severe.
Leon leapt back and raised his arm.
Fireball!
BOOM!
The explosion tore through the boss, flames consuming it entirely.
Its body blackened and collapsed, its life force fading rapidly.
Ding!
[You have killed "Poisonous Mushroom Leader" and gained 400 experience points.]
[You have killed "Poison Snake (Mutated)" and gained 50 experience points.]
[You have killed...]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered, items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
"Perfect."
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 4!]
[You have gained 5 points in all attributes and 5 free points to distribute.]
Leon let out a slow breath.
Only then did he fully realize just how much he had done while still technically being a low-level player.
Without wasting time, he opened his storage space, eyes sharp as he searched for the one thing that mattered most.

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Acquiring the Poison Antidote, Curing Emilia and Completing the Quest
paragraphs: Leon placed the five free points he had just gained into [Spirit] without hesitation, then opened his storage space to review everything he had obtained from the battle.
The first items were exactly what he expected.
[Poison Snake Essence x5]
[Poison Archer Essence x4]
[Poison Fang Dagger x2]
[Mutated Poison Snake Essence x1]

These were all drops from the regular monsters he had hunted throughout the cave. There was nothing surprising about them. He had killed dozens of snakes and archers on his way down, so these rewards made sense.
What really mattered came next.
The remaining items were clearly from the boss.
[Poison Antidote x3: Drink to heal any kind of poison.]
[Poisonous Mushroom Leader Essence: Consuming will increase constitution by 7 and strength by 4.]
[Poison Mushroom Armor (Uncommon): +30 Constitution, +15 Strength, +10 Agility. Protect from "Poison".]
Leon stared at the three [Poison Antidote] for a second, then let out a long breath he didn’t realize he had been holding.
Relief washed over him.
"So it really dropped," he muttered.

He didn’t waste even a second. The poison spores were still lingering in the cave, and even though his body was holding up for now, he had no intention of pushing his luck. Leon immediately pulled one of the antidotes from storage and drank it.
Ding!
[You have been cured from "Poison"]
The uncomfortable sensation in his chest vanished almost instantly. His breathing became steady again, and the faint dizziness he hadn’t noticed until now completely disappeared.
"Much better."
Leon straightened up, but he didn’t linger at the bottom of the cave.
Ding!
[Quest Warning: 30 Minutes Remain.]
His expression turned serious.
"Gotta go back to Emilia," Leon muttered before turning around and sprinting toward the exit.

He estimated it would take him around fifteen minutes to climb back up if he maintained a good pace. That left very little room for error. If he delayed for even a few minutes, Emilia might not survive.
As he moved upward through the winding tunnels of the [Poison Cave], Leon used the time efficiently.
One by one, he consumed all the essences he had collected.
The familiar warm sensation spread through his body as his attributes increased.
Agility rose sharply as the snake essences took effect. His muscles felt lighter, more responsive. His balance improved, and every step felt more precise than the last.
Then came the essence from the [Poisonous Mushroom Leader].
A heavier warmth settled into his body this time. His frame felt sturdier, his breathing deeper. His strength followed shortly after, his grip tightening instinctively around his weapon.
By the time he finished, the changes were complete.
Leon then fused the two [Poison Fang Dagger] together.
Ding!
[You have consumed two identical equipment... enhancement successful!]
The weapon in his hand became denser, its blade sharper and darker than before.
[Poison Fang Dagger +2]
Finally, Leon equipped the [Poisonous Mushroom Armor].

The armor settled comfortably over his body, surprisingly light despite its durability. The faint green patterns across its surface pulsed once before going still, signaling its poison resistance effect.
"Phew," Leon said quietly. "That should be enough."
Before continuing, he quickly checked his combat power to make sure everything had updated correctly.
[Combat Power: 478 (+350)]
Leon froze. His eyes widened as he stared at the number.
"...What?"
He checked it again to make sure he hadn’t misread it. 478 base. Plus 350. That put him well over 800 total combat power.
"Holy hell."
He had gone from struggling against mutated monsters to standing at a level that most players wouldn’t reach for some time.
To be absolutely certain, Leon opened his status panel and checked his attributes directly.
[Constitution: 35 (+60)]
[Strength: 47 (+40)]
Everything matched.
His agility, in particular, stood out. It was absurdly high compared to his other stats, far beyond what a level 4 player should normally possess.
That speed made the rest of the climb trivial.

Leon moved through the cave like a blur, his steps light and controlled, barely slowing down even on steep slopes. Where he had been cautious on the way down, now he simply flowed through the tunnels.
Less than ten minutes later, he arrived at the cave entrance.
Cough!
The sound made his head snap to the side.
"Emilia!"
Leon rushed forward and dropped to one knee beside her.
Her condition was worse than he expected.
Her eyes were bloodshot, unfocused, and blood slowly seeped from the corners of her eyes, mouth, and ears. Her breathing was shallow, and her body trembled faintly.
It was clear she barely registered his presence.
"...Damn," Leon muttered under his breath.
If he had been even a few minutes later...
Leon didn’t want to imagine what would have happened.
He crouched closer, quickly pulling out one of the remaining [Poison Antidote] and bringing it to her lips.
"Drink this," he said firmly, supporting her head.
Emilia weakly followed his instruction.
The moment the potion took effect, the change was visible.
Ding!
[Target has been cured from "Poison"]
Her breathing steadied. The bleeding slowed, then stopped entirely. The dried blood remained, but fresh wounds no longer appeared. Color slowly returned to her face, and her eyes regained focus.
Leon let out a quiet breath of relief.
So this was what prolonged poisoning did to someone.
If he hadn’t cured himself earlier, he might have ended up in the same state without even realizing it.
As Emilia slowly recovered, Leon’s thoughts drifted. An elf. In a novice village meant for humans.
[Eternal Ascension] wasn’t limited to Earth or the human race. Thousands of worlds and races were dragged into the system, some earlier, some later. However, they were separated at the beginning.
Which meant Emilia didn’t end up here by accident.
Someone had used a special method. A rare item. Or a forced transfer.
And that meant one thing: someone really wanted her dead.
Leon didn’t know the reason, but he could guess it wasn’t something simple.
"H-Haha..." Emilia finally let out a weak laugh as she looked up at him. "You actually did it. I didn’t expect that.
She slowly pushed herself up, grabbing her scepter for support before standing fully upright.
Her legs shook slightly, but she remained standing.
"I guess I should give you those rewards..." she said quietly, opening her storage space. "Here."
Ding!
[You have received 500 Eternal Coins from "Emilia Verdant"]
At the same time, an [Elite Treasure Chest] materialized in front of Leon, resting quietly on the ground.
Leon glanced at the coins notification, then focused on the chest.
Before opening it, he looked back at Emilia.
"How did you end up here?" he asked. "You shouldn’t be in this village."
Emilia’s expression darkened.
"...They tried to kill me," she said calmly, though her clenched hand betrayed her anger. "But thanks to you, I think I’ll be able to avenge myself."
Leon studied her silently.
She was strong. Stronger than most players he had seen at this stage.
But revenge now would be reckless.
"Maybe you should grow stronger first," Leon said after a moment. "Don’t risk your life twice for no reason."
Emilia went quiet. She stared at the ground, then slowly nodded.
"...Maybe you’re right," she admitted. "I still want revenge. I’ll prepare properly."
As she spoke, her body began to glow faintly.
Ding!
Blue particles started forming around her legs, slowly traveling upward.
"I guess I’m returning to my own [Novice Village]," Emilia said with a gentle smile. "I hope we meet again, human."
"Sure," Leon replied with a shrug. "See you."
Fwish!
Her body fully dissolved into blue particles and vanished.
Leon stared at the empty spot for a few seconds.
Would they meet again? Maybe. But for now, that wasn’t important.
He turned back to the [Elite Treasure Chest] in front of him.
Just as he reached for it—
Ding!
[Since you are the first to complete a secret quest, you have been rewarded with 10 Reputation Points.]
"Oh, right," Leon muttered, nodding in satisfaction.
That was a valuable reward. Reputation opened many doors later on.
Without wasting another second, he focused on the chest.
[Elite Treasure Chest: May contain skill stones, enhancement stones, a special pill, items or a skill.]
Elite chests were on a completely different level compared to common or rare ones. The rewards could be absurd, but the odds were usually terrible.
Some items had drop rates as low as 0.001% in the strongest chests.
Normally, players would be nervous. Leon wasn’t.
He reached out and opened the chest without hesitation.
Ding!
[100% Drop Rate has triggered, all items inside of the treasure chest have been placed into storage space.]
Ten new items appeared inside his storage space at once.
Leon’s grin widened.
"...Let’s see what I got."

chapters.title: Chapter 13: Level 3 Strong Fireball, The First Event is Here!
paragraphs: Leon opened the chest and stared at the items that appeared inside his [Storage Space].
[Eternal Coins x400]
[Beginner All-Attributes Pill: Increases all attributes by 15.]
[Skill Stone x3]
[Enhancement Stone x3]
[Night Vision Goggles (Uncommon): Allows to see in the dark. Requirement: 50 Agility.]
[Poison Arrows (Skill Book): Allows its user to launch arrows that deal "Poison" when hitting a target.]
"...Damn."
That was the only word that came to his mind.
The rewards were far better than he had expected, even for an [Elite Treasure Chest].
The coins alone were already generous, but the rest pushed it into absurd territory.
The [Beginner All-Attributes Pill] especially stood out. Items that boosted all attributes at once were rare even later into the game, let alone at this stage.
The goggles were also useful. Darkness was common in many zones, and vision-related equipment was always in demand. As for the skill book...
Leon glanced at it for a moment, then shook his head.
"I’m not switching to a bow."
He had no intention of becoming an archer. His build was already set, and splitting focus now would only weaken him. Still, the skill book wasn’t useless.
’Eleonoe is the strongest archer in the [Novice Village], maybe even among all humans,’ Leon thought. ’Selling it to her would be better.’
Someone like her could make full use of it, and in return, he could gain favors or resources later. For now, he stored it away.
Next, Leon took out the [Beginner All-Attributes Pill].
The pill was smooth and faintly warm in his hand, with a subtle glow pulsing beneath its surface. Without hesitating, he swallowed it whole.
Nom! Ding!
[You have consumed the "Beginner All-Attributes Pill" and all your attributes have increased by 15.]
The effect was immediate.
A powerful surge spread through his body, far stronger than any essence he had consumed so far.
It wasn’t focused on one area, everything improved at once. His muscles felt denser, his movements sharper, his breathing steadier, and his mind clearer.
At the same time, his combat power jumped sharply. Just like that, it increased by another 120.
Leon exhaled slowly, steadying himself.
"That pill alone is worth more than the entire cave," he muttered.
For most players, this would have been a once-in-a-lifetime reward. For him, it was guaranteed.
After that, Leon moved on to the stones.
He pulled out two [Enhancement Stone] and focused on his armor.
Ding!
[You have successfully enhanced your "Poison Mushroom Armor"]
The armor glowed faintly, the patterns on its surface becoming sharper and more pronounced. Leon frowned slightly.
"It still took two."
The armor was only level 1 before, but its rank made enhancement harder. Higher-rank equipment always required more stones. That was the trade-off for stronger base stats.
If he wanted to avoid that, he’d need to find an identical piece and gamble on fusion instead. That was easier said than done.
The enhancement finished a moment later.
[Poison Mushroom Armor +2 (Uncommon): +60 Constitution, +40 Strength, +25 Agility. Protects from "Poison".]
Leon nodded.
"That’s solid."
The stat increase was massive. With armor like this, even prolonged poison exposure wouldn’t be much of a threat anymore.
He checked his remaining stones. One [Enhancement Stone] left.
Unfortunately, it wasn’t enough for anything else. His [Purple Jade Necklace] was rare-rank, and it needed three stones just for the first enhancement. There was no point wasting it.
That left the [Skill Stones]. Leon didn’t hesitate.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have upgraded "Fireball (Level 2)" to "Strong Fireball (Level 3)"]
"Nice."
He had used two stones, and the skill didn’t just grow stronger, it evolved.
[Strong Fireball (Level 3): Focus your Spirit and condense it into a strong fireball that hits a target.]
Leon read the description carefully.
As skills grew stronger, their requirements often increased as well. Some players found themselves unable to use upgraded skills because their attributes lagged behind.
Leon checked his [Spirit]. Still more than enough.
"No problem," he said quietly.
With everything sorted, Leon didn’t linger near the cave any longer. He turned and headed back into the [Wild Forest].
Once he was clear of the cave entrance, he opened his status panel.
[Name: Leon Rykard]
[Talent: 100% Drop Rate (SSS)]
[Constitution: 50 (+90)]
[Strength: 62 (+65)]
[Skills: Appraisal (Lv.3), Vision Enhancement (Lv.2), Strong Fireball (Lv.3)]
[Combat Power: 598 (+490)]
[Eternal Coins: 1358]
[Reputation Points: 20]
Leon looked over the numbers slowly. His total combat power was now well over 1,000.
At this point, he could comfortably fight level 6 or even level 7 monsters. That was ridiculous for someone who had only been in [Eternal Ascension] for a few hours.
Most players were still struggling against level 2 enemies.
Leon then glanced at the upper right corner of the panel.
His eyes narrowed. In just two hours, 753 players had already died.
And it wouldn’t slow down. If anything, it would get worse as time passed.
Leon knew this reality well. This was why so many races, including humans, eventually chose to submit to gods, demons, or higher beings. Survival alone pushed people to desperate choices.
Many would think, if only there was another way. Leon knew the answer: absolute strength.
If he became strong enough, he wouldn’t need to bow to anyone. He wouldn’t need protection. He would tear through whatever stood in his way.
With that thought in mind, Leon prepared to move deeper into the forest to continue hunting monsters. He needed more essences. More levels.
But then—
Tick! Tick! Tick!
A strange sound echoed through the air. Leon froze.
The two-hour mark since their arrival in [Eternal Ascension] had just passed.
"Oh god," Leon muttered, his expression turning grim. "The first event."
And at that moment...
Ding!
[It has been two hours, meaning that it is time for your first event!]
"What?"
"Come on..."
[All 10,000 Novice Villages will now face against each other in aforcedevent.]
[Each Novice Village will have another as their opponent, with only one being able to claim victory.]
[Event: Challenge Tokens]
[Be the first Novice Village to gather 50 Challenge Tokens to win.]
[The winning side of the event will be spared, while the losing side will have their experience and resources halved for 12 hours.]
[The person that contributes the most "Challenge Tokens" in this event will be granted 25 free attribute points and an "Epic Treasure Chest".]
"Holy shit, what?"
"I guess it really is a game. There are events too..."
"But wait, that means we’ll have to fight another [Novice Village]?"
"There’s not even a real reward for winning!"
Voices erupted around the place as players reacted in shock.
Leon stayed silent, his eyes fixed on the panels. This event. He remembered it very well.
This was one of the first moments where [Eternal Ascension] showed its true nature.
They were being forced to compete against other humans. Not monsters. But other players just like them.
And there was no real reward for winning. Victory only meant avoiding punishment.
Losing meant having half of their experience and resources cut for twelve hours, a devastating setback early on.
Leon eagerly kept looking at the panels, waiting to see who their opponents were.
Because if they were the same as is in his past life... he’d do anything to annihilate them.
And...
Ding!
[Novice Village #1 will battle against Novice Village #5]
Leon stared at the text. Then, slowly, a wide grin spread across his face.
"...Yeah," he said quietly. "I’m not letting them even breathe."
Novice Village #5. He remembered them clearly.
That village was filled with sadistic players. People who joined the gods, betrayed others, or caused chaos just to survive.
Not everyone there was evil, but most of the decent ones didn’t last long.
In his past life, [Novice Village #1] was completely crushed during this event. Even with strong players and powerful talents, they were overwhelmed.
Back then, no one knew what kinds of talents existed in other villages. Some players were monsters in human skin.
But this time was different. Leon wouldn’t accept that outcome again.
Ding!
[Challenge Tokens can be obtained by killing monsters. May the strongest Novice Village win.]
That meant every village was fighting at the same time. There was no hesitation in Leon’s movements.
Fwoosh!
Fueled by his overwhelming agility, Leon shot forward, rushing deeper into the [Wild Forest].
Monsters were waiting. And this time, every kill mattered.

At the same time, his combat power jumped sharply.
Just like that, it increased by another 120.
Leon exhaled slowly, steadying himself.
"That pill alone is worth more than the entire cave," he muttered.
For most players, this would have been a once-in-a-lifetime reward.
For him, it was guaranteed.
After that, Leon moved on to the stones.
He pulled out two [Enhancement Stone] and focused on his armor.
Ding!
[You have successfully enhanced your "Poison Mushroom Armor"]
The armor glowed faintly, the patterns on its surface becoming sharper and more pronounced.
Leon frowned slightly.
"It still took two."
The armor was only level 1 before, but its rank made enhancement harder.
Higher-rank equipment always required more stones.
That was the trade-off for stronger base stats.
If he wanted to avoid that, he’d need to find an identical piece and gamble on fusion instead.
That was easier said than done.
The enhancement finished a moment later.
[Poison Mushroom Armor +2 (Uncommon): +60 Constitution, +40 Strength, +25 Agility.
Protects from "Poison".]
Leon nodded.
"That’s solid."
The stat increase was massive.
With armor like this, even prolonged poison exposure wouldn’t be much of a threat anymore.
He checked his remaining stones.
One [Enhancement Stone] left.
Unfortunately, it wasn’t enough for anything else.
His [Purple Jade Necklace] was rare-rank, and it needed three stones just for the first enhancement.
There was no point wasting it.
That left the [Skill Stones].
Leon didn’t hesitate.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have upgraded "Fireball (Level 2)" to "Strong Fireball (Level 3)"]
"Nice."
He had used two stones, and the skill didn’t just grow stronger, it evolved.
[Strong Fireball (Level 3): Focus your Spirit and condense it into a strong fireball that hits a target.]
Leon read the description carefully.
As skills grew stronger, their requirements often increased as well.
Some players found themselves unable to use upgraded skills because their attributes lagged behind.
Leon checked his [Spirit].
Still more than enough.
"No problem," he said quietly.
With everything sorted, Leon didn’t linger near the cave any longer.
He turned and headed back into the [Wild Forest].
Once he was clear of the cave entrance, he opened his status panel.
[Name: Leon Rykard]
[Talent: 100% Drop Rate (SSS)]
[Constitution: 50 (+90)]
[Strength: 62 (+65)]
[Skills: Appraisal (Lv.3), Vision Enhancement (Lv.2), Strong Fireball (Lv.3)]
[Combat Power: 598 (+490)]
[Eternal Coins: 1358]
[Reputation Points: 20]
Leon looked over the numbers slowly.
His total combat power was now well over 1,000.
At this point, he could comfortably fight level 6 or even level 7 monsters.
That was ridiculous for someone who had only been in [Eternal Ascension] for a few hours.
Most players were still struggling against level 2 enemies.
Leon then glanced at the upper right corner of the panel.
His eyes narrowed.
In just two hours, 753 players had already died.
And it wouldn’t slow down.
If anything, it would get worse as time passed.
Leon knew this reality well.
This was why so many races, including humans, eventually chose to submit to gods, demons, or higher beings.
Survival alone pushed people to desperate choices.
Many would think, if only there was another way.
Leon knew the answer: absolute strength.
If he became strong enough, he wouldn’t need to bow to anyone.
He wouldn’t need protection.
He would tear through whatever stood in his way.
With that thought in mind, Leon prepared to move deeper into the forest to continue hunting monsters.
He needed more essences.
More levels.
But then—
Tick!
Tick!
Tick!
A strange sound echoed through the air.
Leon froze.
The two-hour mark since their arrival in [Eternal Ascension] had just passed.
"Oh god," Leon muttered, his expression turning grim.
"The first event."
And at that moment...
Ding!
[It has been two hours, meaning that it is time for your first event!]
"What?"
"Come on..."
[All 10,000 Novice Villages will now face against each other in aforcedevent.]
[Each Novice Village will have another as their opponent, with only one being able to claim victory.]
[Event: Challenge Tokens]
[Be the first Novice Village to gather 50 Challenge Tokens to win.]
[The winning side of the event will be spared, while the losing side will have their experience and resources halved for 12 hours.]
[The person that contributes the most "Challenge Tokens" in this event will be granted 25 free attribute points and an "Epic Treasure Chest".]
"Holy shit, what?"
"I guess it really is a game.
There are events too..."
"But wait, that means we’ll have to fight another [Novice Village]?"
"There’s not even a real reward for winning!"
Voices erupted around the place as players reacted in shock.
Leon stayed silent, his eyes fixed on the panels.
This event.
He remembered it very well.
This was one of the first moments where [Eternal Ascension] showed its true nature.
They were being forced to compete against other humans.
Not monsters.
But other players just like them.
And there was no real reward for winning.
Victory only meant avoiding punishment.
Losing meant having half of their experience and resources cut for twelve hours, a devastating setback early on.
Leon eagerly kept looking at the panels, waiting to see who their opponents were.
Because if they were the same as is in his past life... he’d do anything to annihilate them.
And...
Ding!
[Novice Village #1 will battle against Novice Village #5]
Leon stared at the text.
Then, slowly, a wide grin spread across his face.
"...Yeah," he said quietly.
"I’m not letting them even breathe."
Novice Village #5.
He remembered them clearly.
That village was filled with sadistic players.
People who joined the gods, betrayed others, or caused chaos just to survive.
Not everyone there was evil, but most of the decent ones didn’t last long.
In his past life, [Novice Village #1] was completely crushed during this event.
Even with strong players and powerful talents, they were overwhelmed.
Back then, no one knew what kinds of talents existed in other villages.
Some players were monsters in human skin.
But this time was different.
Leon wouldn’t accept that outcome again.
Ding!
[Challenge Tokens can be obtained by killing monsters.
May the strongest Novice Village win.]
That meant every village was fighting at the same time.
There was no hesitation in Leon’s movements.
Fwoosh!
Fueled by his overwhelming agility, Leon shot forward, rushing deeper into the [Wild Forest].
Monsters were waiting.
And this time, every kill mattered.

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Dark Trees and Howler Wolves, Collecting Challenge Tokens
paragraphs: Slash!
Leon pushed deeper into the level 6 area of the [Wild Forest], his movements fast and precise.
The air here felt heavier, the trees thicker, their shadows stretching unnaturally across the ground. It didn’t take long before he sensed something was wrong.
Then he saw it.
[Dark Tree]
[Level: 6]
[Combat Power: 500]
[Details: A monster tree that tries to act as a normal one to ambush victims.]
To an untrained eye, it looked like any other tree, dark bark, twisted branches, roots half-buried in the soil. But Leon knew better.
The moment his gaze lingered on it, he acted.
Strong Fireball!
A blazing sphere of condensed flames shot forward.
BOOM!

The fireball slammed directly into the trunk, igniting it instantly. The tree didn’t even have time to react before it cracked apart, blackened wood collapsing inward as the monster let out a shrill screech and died on the spot.
"One-shot," Leon muttered.
Against physical attacks, [Dark Trees] were annoying. Their bark was tough, and their vines could restrain careless players. But they had one glaring weakness: fire.
For warriors, elemental weaknesses didn’t always matter. A sword was a sword. But for mages, elements were everything. And Leon was both.
As a [Magical Swordsman], he needed to understand every advantage his skills could offer. Fire against wood was as simple as it got.
The moment the first [Dark Tree] fell, two more revealed themselves nearby. Their trunks split open, massive dark eyes opening where bark had once been.
Slash!
Leon spun on his heel and rushed forward, his dagger flashing. He slashed straight into the exposed eye of the nearest tree, dark sap spraying outward as it recoiled.
Thud! Thud!
Roots burst from the ground, thick vines snapping toward Leon’s legs and torso, trying to restrain him.
But it was pointless. Leon’s agility was far too high.
He stepped lightly between the vines, movements sharp and clean, then struck again.
Slash! Slash!
His blade carved through bark and flesh alike. In seconds, both trees collapsed, their bodies splitting apart as their life force faded.
Ding!
[You have killed x3 "Dark Tree" and gained 150 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered, items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
Leon barely spared the corpses a glance before checking his storage space. And immediately, his lips curled upward.
[Challenge Token x2: Can be used to increase the novice village’s score by one.]
"Haha," Leon laughed softly.
This was where his talent became truly unfair.
[Challenge Tokens] didn’t drop often. Even when monsters could drop them, the chance was painfully low. Most players would kill dozens of monsters and see nothing.
But Leon? If a monster could drop it, he would get it. Every time. That alone tilted the entire event in their favor.
He brought up the event progress bar, translucent panels appearing in front of his vision.
[Novice Village #1: 1 Challenge Token.]
[Novice Village #5: 3 Challenge Tokens.]
"They’re fast," Leon noted.
It had only been a few minutes since the event started, and [Novice Village #5] was already ahead. There was also a leaderboard showing individual contributions.
[Challenge Token Leaderboard:]
[1. David Windbreak: 1.]
Leon nodded slowly.
"I guess they’re working too. Can’t let them down."
He understood the stakes better than anyone. If their village lost, the punishment would cripple them. Half experience and resources for twelve hours this early was devastating.
And so—
Fwish!
Leon added his two [Challenge Tokens] to the village score.
[Novice Village #1: 3 Challenge Tokens.]
[Novice Village #5: 3 Challenge Tokens.]
Just like that, the gap closed.
Beside the tokens, the [Dark Trees] had also dropped three [Dark Tree Essence], which increased Strength by 3 each, and a [Dark Branch (Uncommon)].
Leon consumed the essences immediately, feeling his muscles tighten slightly as his strength rose.
Then he moved on.
Slash!
Leon didn’t spare a single monster he encountered. Every [Dark Tree] that even hinted at movement was cut down or burned to ash. He cleared the area efficiently, never slowing, never hesitating.
Eventually, the forest shifted again.
The trees grew thinner, the ground rougher. The howls reached his ears before the monsters appeared.
[Howler Wolf]
[Level: 7]
[Combat Power: 650]
[Details: Wolves that roam in the darkness of the forest, waiting for prey.]
Leon narrowed his eyes. Now it was a mix.
[Howler Wolves] roamed in packs, fast and aggressive, while [Dark Trees] still lurked, waiting to ambush careless players.
For most people, this area was a nightmare.
Vision Enhancement!
The world sharpened instantly. Every movement, every shift of shadow, every twitch of muscle stood out clearly.
A wolf lunged from the side.
Slash!
Leon cut its throat mid-leap, blood spraying as the body hit the ground lifeless.
At the same time, he twisted his torso and fired a spell.
Strong Fireball!
Boom!
A [Dark Tree] trying to ambush him was engulfed in flames before its vines could even reach him.
Howlll!
More wolves emerged, their glowing eyes locking onto Leon as they surrounded him.
But they were too slow. Leon moved like a blur, weaving between them, blade flashing again and again.
Slash! Slash!
Heads rolled across the forest floor. Bodies dropped one after another.
The remaining [Dark Trees] panicked as they realized their camouflage wasn’t working.
Vines lashed out wildly. Leon dodged, leapt, and retaliated.
Strong Fireball!
Boom!
The explosion shook the ground, splintering wood and scattering ash. Within minutes, the forest fell silent.
Ding!
[You have killed x8 "Dark Tree" and gained 350 experience points.]
[You have killed x6 "Howler Wolf" and gained 420 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered, items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 5!]
[You have gained 5 points in all attributes, and 5 free points to distribute.]
Leon exhaled slowly.
"Phew."
His combat power now far surpassed anything in this area. That was why he could fight so freely, chain kills together, and level up without slowing down.
He quickly checked the loot.
[Eternal Coins x170]
[Dark Tree Essence x8: Consuming will increase strength by 3.]
[Howler Wolf Essence x6: Consuming will increase agility by 4.]
[Dark Tree Branch x4 (Uncommon): Can be used to forge a weapon.]
[Howled Wolf Claw x3 (Rare): Can be used to create a powerful dagger.]
[Challenge Tokens x7]
"Nice."
Leon immediately consumed all the essences.
His strength surged by 24 and his agility surged by another 24.
Just like that, his combat power climbed past 1,200.
But Leon didn’t add the seven [Challenge Tokens] right away.
"I should head back," he muttered. "Winning fast matters more."
Since any monster could potentially drop tokens, there was no reason to linger here. He could always return later to grind.
And so Leon retraced his steps, killing monsters along the way while keeping an eye on the event.
[Novice Village #1: 6 Challenge Tokens.]
[Novice Village #5: 8 Challenge Tokens.]
If he added his tokens now, their village would jump far ahead.
But Leon shook his head, a grin forming.
’Nah. Just like they did to us before... I’ll let them think they can win.’
Five minutes passed. Leon continued hunting, moving efficiently, collecting more drops.
By the time he slowed, he had gained five more [Challenge Tokens].
And then—
"Got one more!"
"Nice!"
Leon recognized the voices instantly.
He rushed forward and saw David, Aaron, Eleonore, and their other teammate standing over a fallen monster.
David wiped sweat from his brow, grinning.
"Perfect timing," Leon thought as he stepped out from the trees.
