chapters.title: Chapter 15: Giving Items to Aaron and Eleonore, Dominating the Event
paragraphs: Leon already knew how this would turn out.
In the entire Novice Village, the number of people who could actually contribute to the event was painfully small.
Most players simply couldn’t do it.
Some were too scared. The idea of risking their lives for something as uncertain as [Challenge Tokens] was enough to make them stay inside the village.
Others did try, but reality hit them fast: they weren’t strong enough to handle the monsters outside for long.
A few bad encounters, some close calls, and they retreated, shaken and empty-handed.
No matter the reason, the result was the same. Only a handful of groups were actively trying to win the event.
David’s team was one of those groups.
Leon remembered them clearly from his past life. Among everyone in the village, they had been the ones who gathered the most [Challenge Tokens].
They weren’t the strongest, nor the luckiest, but they kept pushing forward while others hesitated. That alone set them apart.
Slash!
The sound rang out sharply as David brought down his weapon.
The [Goblin Machete +3] flashed through the air and split a level 4 monster cleanly.
The creature barely had time to react before its body collapsed to the ground.
Leon watched from a distance as he approached the group.
That machete was something Leon himself had sold to David earlier. Seeing it now, stained with monster blood and being put to proper use, only confirmed Leon’s judgment. David wasn’t wasting it.
While walking toward them, Leon briefly opened the level leaderboard.
There was no real need to check it, he already knew what it would show, but habit made him glance anyway.
[Level Leaderboard:]
[1. Leon Skyward: Level 5]
[2. Eleonore Starlight: Level 3]
[3. David Windbreak: Level 3]
[4. Aaron Godfield: Level 3]
[5. Alice Evicton: Level 3]
The list went on, but nothing changed.
Everyone else in the top twenty-five was still level 3. Not a single one had reached level 4 yet.
Leon closed the leaderboard. The gap was obvious. He was far ahead.
To the others, reaching level 4 felt like a wall. To Leon, it had already become a distant memory.
His experience, his stats, his combat sense, everything placed him in a completely different category.

"I hope you’re helping with the event," Eleonore said as she noticed Leon approaching. She wore a grin, but there was clear frustration beneath it. "I feel like these other guys are way luckier than us."
David wiped his blade and let out a long sigh. "We only get one [Challenge Token] every dozen monsters," he complained. "At this rate, it’s going to take forever."

"Well, worst case," Aaron said with a shrug, resting his weapon on his shoulder, "we just stay inside the village for the twelve hours. No point risking too much. We don’t even know what the other villages can do."
"Absolutely not," Eleonore replied immediately, shaking her head. Her tone was firm. "We need to grow stronger.
"I’m just saying," Aaron continued calmly, "we have an entire month to reach level 10. At the rate we’re going, it’ll take a few days at most."
Leon understood where Aaron was coming from.
From a normal player’s perspective, that logic made sense. Why rush? Why push so hard when the system gave them time?
But Leon knew better. That mindset killed people.
If you moved too slowly, you fell behind. And once you fell behind, catching up became nearly impossible.
Monsters would grow stronger. Players would grow stronger. And those who hesitated would be crushed between the two.
That was why leaving the Novice Village as soon as possible was always the best choice.
Leon looked at the group in front of him.
They had potential. Not enough to survive on their own forever, but enough to matter.
He opened his [Storage Space] and pulled out two items without hesitation.
"Here."
He tossed a dagger toward Aaron and a glowing book toward Eleonore.
The [Poison Fang Dagger +2] landed neatly in Aaron’s hands. The [Poison Arrows (Skill Book)] was caught by Eleonore almost instinctively.
For a moment, nobody spoke.
Then—
"How the fuck did you get that?" Aaron blurted out, staring at the dagger like it might disappear.
"Seriously..." Alice, the support of their team, said quietly, eyes wide. "We killed so many monsters and barely got anything, and you have all this?"
Eleonore didn’t look away from the skill book in her hands. Her grip tightened slightly.
"What do you want in return?" she asked, finally lifting her gaze to Leon. "We didn’t even get a single skill book."
Leon smiled.
It was the same expression he remembered. Sharp, observant, straight to the point. Even back when she later became a guild leader, Eleonore always thought this way.
"Nothing much," Leon said simply. "When I ask for a favor someday, just help me out."
Eleonore stared down at the skill book again.
She tried to keep her expression cold and composed, but it didn’t fully work. Her eyes sparkled despite her effort to hide it.
"A-Alright," she said after a brief cough. "But I don’t have any experience with anything else..."
David blinked: "?"
Alice tilted her head, "?"
Aaron looked between them, confused, "???"
Even Leon paused for a second, "...?"
All of them looked at each other in confusion: what could Eleonore even be talking about?
But before anyone could ask, Eleonore poured her mana into the skill book.
The light flared, and the book dissolved into particles as the skill engraved itself into her system.
Her presence shifted immediately. It wasn’t dramatic, but it was clear, she was stronger now.
Aaron swung the dagger experimentally, feeling its balance and weight. A wide grin spread across his face.
"Damn," he said. "This feels amazing.
Luckily, neither item had strict requirements. Otherwise, they wouldn’t have been able to use them at all.
"Well," Aaron said, motivation burning in his eyes now, "this definitely gets me moving. Let’s crush Novice Village #5’s ass."
"Well said," David nodded. "We should push into the level 4 area. I’m close to leveling up."
"So am I," Eleonore added. "Even if it’s just us, we have to try."
"See you," Leon said neutrally.
He watched them leave, their pace quicker than before, their resolve clearly strengthened.
He had done what he wanted with them. And so, Leon continued forward.
After all, his goal was clear: he wanted as many [Challenge Tokens] as possible.
Not just to humiliate Novice Village #5, but also to secure the reward for being the biggest contributor.
As he moved deeper into the area, monsters began appearing one after another: [Small Goblins], [Demonized Rats], [Plant Foxes].
They barely had time to register his presence. The moment their eyes locked onto Leon, he was already in front of them.
Slash!
His blade cut through flesh and bone without resistance. The monsters were split apart as if they were made of paper.
His combat power was overwhelming. None of these creatures stood a chance.
Leon didn’t slow down. He moved like a machine, efficiently clearing everything in his path.
Thirty minutes passed, and at some point, Leon realized there were no more level 3 monsters left nearby.
He had killed them all. Without hesitation, he turned back toward the level 4 area.
While Leon was doing this, the players from both villages continued their own struggles.
And eventually, the numbers updated.
[Novice Village #1: 13 Challenge Tokens.]
[Novice Village #5: 21 Challenge Tokens.]
They were losing again. The other village either had players who were more efficient, or simply luckier.
But it didn’t matter. Leon checked his own count.
[Challenge Tokens x34]
In only a few more minutes, he would completely fill the event bar. Victory was inevitable.
As he continued slaughtering monsters, his talent activated several times. Essences flowed into him.
[+25 Strength, +12 Constitution, +15 Agility and +28 Spirit]
His body grew stronger with every kill.
He was also close to leveling up again. Level 6 required 1,500 experience points, and he was nearly there.
On top of that, mutated monsters dropped rewards: two [Skill Stones] and one [Enhancement Stone].
Leon exhaled slowly and smiled.
"Everything’s going way better than before."
But for the other village, that wouldn’t be the case for much longer.

sentences.text: Leon already knew how this would turn out.
In the entire Novice Village, the number of people who could actually contribute to the event was painfully small.
Most players simply couldn’t do it.
Some were too scared.
The idea of risking their lives for something as uncertain as [Challenge Tokens] was enough to make them stay inside the village.
Others did try, but reality hit them fast: they weren’t strong enough to handle the monsters outside for long.
A few bad encounters, some close calls, and they retreated, shaken and empty-handed.
No matter the reason, the result was the same.
Only a handful of groups were actively trying to win the event.
David’s team was one of those groups.
Leon remembered them clearly from his past life.
Among everyone in the village, they had been the ones who gathered the most [Challenge Tokens].
They weren’t the strongest, nor the luckiest, but they kept pushing forward while others hesitated.
That alone set them apart.
Slash!
The sound rang out sharply as David brought down his weapon.
The [Goblin Machete +3] flashed through the air and split a level 4 monster cleanly.
The creature barely had time to react before its body collapsed to the ground.
Leon watched from a distance as he approached the group.
That machete was something Leon himself had sold to David earlier.
Seeing it now, stained with monster blood and being put to proper use, only confirmed Leon’s judgment.
David wasn’t wasting it.
While walking toward them, Leon briefly opened the level leaderboard.
There was no real need to check it, he already knew what it would show, but habit made him glance anyway.
[Level Leaderboard:]
Leon Skyward: Level 5]
Eleonore Starlight: Level 3]
David Windbreak: Level 3]
Aaron Godfield: Level 3]
Alice Evicton: Level 3]
The list went on, but nothing changed.
Everyone else in the top twenty-five was still level 3.
Not a single one had reached level 4 yet.
Leon closed the leaderboard.
The gap was obvious.
He was far ahead.
To the others, reaching level 4 felt like a wall.
To Leon, it had already become a distant memory.
His experience, his stats, his combat sense, everything placed him in a completely different category.
"I hope you’re helping with the event," Eleonore said as she noticed Leon approaching.
She wore a grin, but there was clear frustration beneath it.
"I feel like these other guys are way luckier than us."
David wiped his blade and let out a long sigh.
"We only get one [Challenge Token] every dozen monsters," he complained.
"At this rate, it’s going to take forever."
"Well, worst case," Aaron said with a shrug, resting his weapon on his shoulder, "we just stay inside the village for the twelve hours.
No point risking too much.
We don’t even know what the other villages can do."
"Absolutely not," Eleonore replied immediately, shaking her head.
Her tone was firm.
"We need to grow stronger.
"I’m just saying," Aaron continued calmly, "we have an entire month to reach level 10.
At the rate we’re going, it’ll take a few days at most."
Leon understood where Aaron was coming from.
From a normal player’s perspective, that logic made sense.
Why rush?
Why push so hard when the system gave them time?
But Leon knew better.
That mindset killed people.
If you moved too slowly, you fell behind.
And once you fell behind, catching up became nearly impossible.
Monsters would grow stronger.
Players would grow stronger.
And those who hesitated would be crushed between the two.
That was why leaving the Novice Village as soon as possible was always the best choice.
Leon looked at the group in front of him.
They had potential.
Not enough to survive on their own forever, but enough to matter.
He opened his [Storage Space] and pulled out two items without hesitation.
"Here."
He tossed a dagger toward Aaron and a glowing book toward Eleonore.
The [Poison Fang Dagger +2] landed neatly in Aaron’s hands.
The [Poison Arrows (Skill Book)] was caught by Eleonore almost instinctively.
For a moment, nobody spoke.
Then—
"How the fuck did you get that?" Aaron blurted out, staring at the dagger like it might disappear.
"Seriously..." Alice, the support of their team, said quietly, eyes wide.
"We killed so many monsters and barely got anything, and you have all this?"
Eleonore didn’t look away from the skill book in her hands.
Her grip tightened slightly.
"What do you want in return?" she asked, finally lifting her gaze to Leon.
"We didn’t even get a single skill book."
Leon smiled.
It was the same expression he remembered.
Sharp, observant, straight to the point.
Even back when she later became a guild leader, Eleonore always thought this way.
"Nothing much," Leon said simply.
"When I ask for a favor someday, just help me out."
Eleonore stared down at the skill book again.
She tried to keep her expression cold and composed, but it didn’t fully work.
Her eyes sparkled despite her effort to hide it.
"A-Alright," she said after a brief cough.
"But I don’t have any experience with anything else..."
David blinked: "?"
Alice tilted her head, "?"
Aaron looked between them, confused, "???"
Even Leon paused for a second, "...?"
All of them looked at each other in confusion: what could Eleonore even be talking about?
But before anyone could ask, Eleonore poured her mana into the skill book.
The light flared, and the book dissolved into particles as the skill engraved itself into her system.
Her presence shifted immediately.
It wasn’t dramatic, but it was clear, she was stronger now.
Aaron swung the dagger experimentally, feeling its balance and weight.
A wide grin spread across his face.
"Damn," he said.
"This feels amazing.
Luckily, neither item had strict requirements.
Otherwise, they wouldn’t have been able to use them at all.
"Well," Aaron said, motivation burning in his eyes now, "this definitely gets me moving.
Let’s crush Novice Village #5’s ass."
"Well said," David nodded.
"We should push into the level 4 area.
I’m close to leveling up."
"So am I," Eleonore added.
"Even if it’s just us, we have to try."
"See you," Leon said neutrally.
He watched them leave, their pace quicker than before, their resolve clearly strengthened.
He had done what he wanted with them.
And so, Leon continued forward.
After all, his goal was clear: he wanted as many [Challenge Tokens] as possible.
Not just to humiliate Novice Village #5, but also to secure the reward for being the biggest contributor.
As he moved deeper into the area, monsters began appearing one after another: [Small Goblins], [Demonized Rats], [Plant Foxes].
They barely had time to register his presence.
The moment their eyes locked onto Leon, he was already in front of them.
Slash!
His blade cut through flesh and bone without resistance.
The monsters were split apart as if they were made of paper.
His combat power was overwhelming.
None of these creatures stood a chance.
Leon didn’t slow down.
He moved like a machine, efficiently clearing everything in his path.
Thirty minutes passed, and at some point, Leon realized there were no more level 3 monsters left nearby.
He had killed them all.
Without hesitation, he turned back toward the level 4 area.
While Leon was doing this, the players from both villages continued their own struggles.
And eventually, the numbers updated.
[Novice Village #1: 13 Challenge Tokens.]
[Novice Village #5: 21 Challenge Tokens.]
They were losing again.
The other village either had players who were more efficient, or simply luckier.
But it didn’t matter.
Leon checked his own count.
[Challenge Tokens x34]
In only a few more minutes, he would completely fill the event bar.
Victory was inevitable.
As he continued slaughtering monsters, his talent activated several times.
Essences flowed into him.
[+25 Strength, +12 Constitution, +15 Agility and +28 Spirit]
His body grew stronger with every kill.
He was also close to leveling up again.
Level 6 required 1,500 experience points, and he was nearly there.
On top of that, mutated monsters dropped rewards: two [Skill Stones] and one [Enhancement Stone].
Leon exhaled slowly and smiled.
"Everything’s going way better than before."
But for the other village, that wouldn’t be the case for much longer.

chapters.title: Chapter 16: Event Victory, Damon’s Rage
paragraphs: Meanwhile, in Novice Village #5...
Slash!
A monster fell apart in two clean pieces.
"Here we go," Damon laughed loudly, wiping blood from his machete. "Another [Challenge Token]!"
"Nice one!"
"I got one too," Maki said as she walked over, her own machete still dripping. The metal glinted faintly as she smiled. "That makes two for this fight."
"Perfect," Damon nodded with satisfaction. "Those idiots from [Novice Village #1] are still taking their sweet time."
"They can’t catch up anyway," Maki laughed. "They’ll just lose and get their experience and resources cut in half for twelve hours."
"The weak deserve to die," Damon said coldly. His smile twisted into something cruel. "That’s how this world works now."
Before they were chosen by [Eternal Ascension], Damon and Maki had lived very different lives from most people.
They were gang members. Violence, theft, intimidation, those things were normal to them.
They fought almost daily, took what they wanted, and never cared about consequences.
Deep down, they both knew it couldn’t last forever. If they kept going like that, prison or death was only a matter of time.
But then everything changed. That thing descended on their world. [Eternal Ascension].
In an instant, their old world was gone. They were dragged into this new place filled with monsters, systems, levels, and skills. A world where strength wasn’t just useful—it was everything.
When Damon realized that, he felt something awaken inside him.
A world where the strong ruled. A world where violence wasn’t punished, but rewarded.
From that moment on, Damon swore to himself that he would become stronger than anyone else. He would crush anyone beneath him. No mercy. No hesitation.
And so far, it was working. He was level 4, the highest level in Novice Village #5.
Damon glanced at the event panel floating before his eyes.
[Novice Village #1: 14 Challenge Tokens.]
[Novice Village #5: 25 Challenge Tokens.]
"Hah!" Damon laughed and turned to his group. "We’re already halfway there, and they can barely scrape together anything!"
"Of course, boss!"
"They can’t compare to us!"
"We kill way more monsters than they do!"
The entire group was in high spirits. They moved with confidence, even arrogance. To them, this event was already over. Victory felt guaranteed.
Just as they prepared to charge another group of monsters—
Ding!
A sharp sound echoed through the air. A panel appeared in front of every player’s vision.
[Novice Village #1 was the first to gather 50 Challenge Tokens.]
[Novice Village #5 has failed the challenge.]
Silence.
"What?" Damon muttered.
He stared at the panel, his smile disappearing instantly. A vein popped on his forehead as disbelief twisted his face.
"This... this is a joke, right?"
Beep!
Another panel appeared.
[Novice Village #5’s players will have all experience points and resources halved for the next 12 hours.]
[Novice Village #1 is spared.]
"What the hell!?"
"How is that possible!?"
"We were winning! How did we lose!?"
Shouts erupted all around.
Not just in Novice Village #5, but in both villages. Nobody had expected this outcome. It made no sense.
They were ahead. They had more tokens. So how?
"How could Novice Village #1 suddenly get thirty-six tokens!?" someone yelled.
Confusion quickly turned into disbelief. Then disbelief turned into anger.
Many players immediately opened the event leaderboard, desperate for an explanation.
[Challenge Token Leaderboard:]
[1. Leon Rykard: 37 Challenge Tokens.]
[2. Damon Regicide: 17 Challenge Tokens.]
[3. David Windbreak: 7 Challenge Tokens.]
[4. Maki Dusekaar: 6 Challenge Tokens.]
[5. Eleonore Starlight: 5 Challenge Tokens.]
The rest of the list barely mattered. Most players had one or two tokens at best, earned through sheer luck.
Everyone’s eyes locked onto the name at the very top. Leon Rykard.
Before this, he had only two tokens.
Now? Thirty-seven. In less than an hour.
"That’s impossible..."
"That has to be cheating!"
"How can one person get that many!?"
Whispers spread like wildfire. Fear, jealousy, and resentment mixed together. No one could understand how it was even possible.
Maki slowly walked toward Damon. His entire body was shaking, his teeth clenched so hard it looked painful.
"D-Damon," she said carefully. "Calm down. We can always—"
Slash!
Damon suddenly swung his machete.
The blade crashed into a nearby tree. The trunk split cleanly in half and fell to the ground with a heavy thud.
Silence followed. Damon stood there, breathing heavily. Then he laughed.
"Haha..." He straightened up and wiped his blade slowly. "I see."
His anger faded, replaced by something colder.
"Leon Rykard."
He spoke the name softly, like he was tasting it.
A wide grin spread across his face. The players watching felt chills run down their spines.
’Whoever that Leon guy is... he’s dead.’
’Even I feel bad for him.’
Everyone in Novice Village #5 knew about Damon’s talent.
SS-Rank Talent: [Enraged One].
The angrier Damon became, the stronger he got. The closer he was to death, the more terrifying his power grew. It had no clear limit.
That was how he had cut down a tree like it was nothing.
If he was pushed far enough, Damon could even one-shot a level 5 boss.
And now, Leon’s name was burned deep into his mind.
One day, Damon would find him. And he would make him pay.
Back in [Novice Village #1].
"Oh... we actually won."
"I didn’t even do anything."
"That was way too close."
"I guess we should thank Leon."
Relief spread throughout the village.
Players slumped to the ground, exhaling deeply. Many of them hadn’t even tried to help with the event. They had fully expected to lose.
"Well, I guess we really could count on Leon," David said with a grin. "Good work, everyone."
"Phew..."
"Yeah," Eleonore said quietly, rubbing her chin. A small smile appeared on her lips. "Leon really is strong."
Far away from the village, Leon stood over the corpse of the monster that had given him his final [Challenge Token].
The moment the token entered his inventory, he didn’t hesitate.
He immediately sent all his tokens to the event score.
The event ended instantly. Victory.
This time, unlike his past life, Novice Village #1 won.
"Damon must be furious," Leon said with a grin. "Good."
He absorbed the three essences he had just gained. His [Spirit] increased by 6.
Then a new panel appeared.
Ding!
[Since you contributed the most Challenge Tokens, you are granted 25 free attribute points and an Epic Treasure Chest.]
Clang!
A massive chest materialized in front of Leon. At the same time, his free attribute points increased.
[Free Points to Allocate: 30.]
"Hah," Leon laughed softly. "Put everything into [Spirit]."
His [Strength] and [Agility] were already absurdly high. His [Constitution] was boosted by his equipment.
[Spirit] was the only stat still lacking. And he needed it. Strong spells meant survival.
Without wasting time, Leon reached out and placed his hand on the chest.
An [Epic Treasure Chest]. Better than an elite or rare one.
The current ranking was simple: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Elite, Epic, Legendary.
There were higher ranks beyond Legendary, but that was a problem for the future.
[Epic Treasure Chest: May contain Eternal Coins, an epic-ranked item, skill stones, enhancement stones, or a skill book/spell scroll.]
Leon smiled. This was the reward for his hard work.
And without hesitation, he opened it.

chapters.title: Chapter 17: Epic Treasure Chest Loot, Elemental Bears
paragraphs: Ding!
[100% Drop Rate has triggered. All items inside the treasure chest have been placed into storage space.]
"Nice."
Leon didn’t waste a second. He immediately opened his storage and checked what he had gotten.
[Eternal Coins x700]
[Skill Stone x6]
[Enhancement Stone x5]
[Sage’s Chain (Epic): +100 Spirit, -15% Cooldown Reduction. Requirement: Level 6 and 150 Spirit.]
[Lightning Strike (Elite): Focus your Spirit and condense it into a lightning strike that can hit a target and sometimes stun them. Requirement: 200 Spirit.]
"...Damn."
Leon couldn’t help but mutter that out loud. This haul was absurd.
Even compared to the best chests he had opened in his past life, this one stood out.
But that made sense, this was an epic chest, after all. Epic-ranked items were on an entirely different level compared to elite ones.
The [Sage’s Chain] alone was ridiculous. And then there was the spell. [Lightning Strike].
An elite-ranked offensive spell that could stun. For a mage, or a magical swordsman like Leon, this was huge.
But unfortunately... Leon’s expression shifted slightly as he checked his current stats.
"...So close."
He was missing just a little bit of everything.
A few hundred experience points. A bit more Spirit.
He couldn’t equip the [Sage’s Chain] yet.
And without the chain, there was no way he could reach 200 Spirit to learn [Lightning Strike].
It was frustrating, but Leon didn’t panic.
If there was one thing he had learned from his past life, it was patience mixed with decisiveness.
He knew exactly what to do.
Leon turned around without hesitation and headed straight back toward the deeper areas of the [Wild Forest].
The level 6 and 7 zones.
Fwoosh!
He shot forward at full speed.
No players appeared along the way. That wasn’t surprising, most people were still struggling in level 3 and 4 areas. Going this deep required confidence, power, or recklessness.
Leon had a mix of the three. Eventually, the dense forest opened up into a clearing.
A small lake shimmered under faint light, surrounded by grass and broken stones. Near the water, several massive shapes rested calmly.
Leon narrowed his eyes.
[Elemental Bear]
[Level: 7]
[Combat Power: 700]
[Details: Bears capable of controlling elemental forces. Each one usually masters a single element during childhood.]
Four bears. Each one radiated a different aura.
One had sparks of lightning dancing across its fur.
Another had small flames flickering along its body.
The third had thick roots and patches of earth clinging to its limbs.
And the last one stood partially submerged in the lake, water swirling lazily around it.
Leon observed them quietly.
"Yeah," he muttered. "This should be enough."
He stepped forward.
Strong Fireball!
A blazing fireball formed instantly and shot forward. Leon aimed it straight at the bear covered in roots.
If that one used earth-element abilities, then fire should be its weakness.
BOOM!
The fireball exploded on impact.
Flames engulfed the bear for a split second before its massive body collapsed onto the ground, lifeless. Instant kill.
Leon didn’t slow down.
Unfortunately, fire wasn’t ideal against the other three. He didn’t have spells tailored to each element yet.
So he switched tactics.
Fwish!
Leon closed the distance in an instant, his [Poison Fang Dagger +3] flashing in his hand.
Slash!
He slashed across the flame-type bear’s side.
The blade cut deep, and a sickly green poison immediately spread through the wound. The dagger’s passive activated instantly, eating away at the bear’s vitality.
Roar!
The remaining three bears reacted at once.
The water-type and lightning-type bears roared loudly, elemental energy gathering around them.
Zap! Splash!
A bolt of lightning and a condensed water projectile shot toward Leon.
Leon twisted his body smoothly, dodging both attacks without difficulty.
He dashed forward again.
The flame-type bear was already slowing down. Poison coursed through its body, weakening it rapidly.
Slash!
Before it could even retaliate, Leon ended its life with a clean strike. Two down.
The remaining bears hesitated. Fear flickered in their eyes.
They had seen two of their companions die in seconds.
Strong Fireball!
Leon fired another spell, this time targeting the lightning-type bear.
The bear leapt aside, barely avoiding the explosion. But that was exactly what Leon wanted.
Slash!
In the next instant, Leon was already behind it. The dagger flashed.
The lightning-type bear’s head separated from its body and fell to the ground.
Blood splattered across the grass. Only one remained.
ROOOAR!
The water-type bear roared furiously.
It retreated backward and plunged fully into the lake. Water surged violently as it gathered the surrounding liquid.
The surface of the lake began to churn.
A massive [Water Ball] formed, growing larger and larger until it was the size of a car.
Leon frowned.
’That’s dangerous.’ The water ball shot toward him at terrifying speed, ’But... it’s fine.’
Strong Fireball!
Leon launched a fireball straight into the incoming attack.
The two collided. The water ball slowed for a moment, just enough.
Leon dashed to the side.
BAM!
The water ball smashed into the ground where Leon had been standing, creating a violent explosion of water and force.
Leon raised his arm to shield his face as debris scattered everywhere.
When the water settled, the bear realized something: the human was still alive.
Its movements slowed as a result.
Fwish! Slash!
So Leon closed the distance and ended it.
The bear’s head rolled into the lake. Silence returned to the clearing.
Ding!
[You have killed x4 "Elemental Bears" and gained 400 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered. Items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 6!]
[You have gained 5 points in all attributes and 5 free points to distribute.]
"All free points into [Spirit]," Leon said instantly. Then he checked the drops.
[Elemental Bear Essence x4: Consuming will increase Spirit by 4.]
[Elemental Stone x4: A stone that reacts to a specific element. Currently has no known use.]
Leon raised an eyebrow.
"Hm."
He stored the stones without much thought and consumed the essences.
His Spirit climbed again.
He smiled.
Level requirement met. Spirit requirement, almost.
Next, Leon equipped the [Sage’s Chain].
Beep!
[You already have two necklaces equipped. Please remove one.]
"Oh, right."
Leon glanced at his equipment.
He was currently wearing the [Shadow Necklace +2] and the [Purple Jade Necklace].
After a short pause, he removed the [Shadow Necklace +2].
The necklace vanished.
Thankfully—
[Spirit: 155]
Leon exhaled softly.
If his Spirit had dropped below the requirement after removing it, that would’ve been embarrassing.
It had happened more times than he liked to remember in his past life.
With the [Sage’s Chain] equipped, Leon felt an immediate change.
His mana pool expanded. His thoughts felt clearer. Spellcasting felt... smoother.
Without wasting time, he summoned the spell scroll: [Lightning Strike].
Fwoosh!
Leon poured his mana into it and tore the scroll apart.
Ding!
[You have learned the skill "Lightning Strike."]
"Second spell," Leon said with a grin. He clenched his fist, "And I still have plenty of [Skill Stones] and [Enhancement Stones]."
He had been waiting for this moment.
Now that he had the chain equipped and the spell learned, there was no reason to hold back anymore.
"...Time to get stronger."

sentences.text: Ding!
[100% Drop Rate has triggered.
All items inside the treasure chest have been placed into storage space.]
"Nice."
Leon didn’t waste a second.
He immediately opened his storage and checked what he had gotten.
[Eternal Coins x700]
[Skill Stone x6]
[Enhancement Stone x5]
[Sage’s Chain (Epic): +100 Spirit, -15% Cooldown Reduction.
Requirement: Level 6 and 150 Spirit.]
[Lightning Strike (Elite): Focus your Spirit and condense it into a lightning strike that can hit a target and sometimes stun them.
Requirement: 200 Spirit.]
"...Damn."
Leon couldn’t help but mutter that out loud.
This haul was absurd.
Even compared to the best chests he had opened in his past life, this one stood out.
But that made sense, this was an epic chest, after all.
Epic-ranked items were on an entirely different level compared to elite ones.
The [Sage’s Chain] alone was ridiculous.
And then there was the spell.
[Lightning Strike].
An elite-ranked offensive spell that could stun.
For a mage, or a magical swordsman like Leon, this was huge.
But unfortunately...
Leon’s expression shifted slightly as he checked his current stats.
"...So close."
He was missing just a little bit of everything.
A few hundred experience points.
A bit more Spirit.
He couldn’t equip the [Sage’s Chain] yet.
And without the chain, there was no way he could reach 200 Spirit to learn [Lightning Strike].
It was frustrating, but Leon didn’t panic.
If there was one thing he had learned from his past life, it was patience mixed with decisiveness.
He knew exactly what to do.
Leon turned around without hesitation and headed straight back toward the deeper areas of the [Wild Forest].
The level 6 and 7 zones.
Fwoosh!
He shot forward at full speed.
No players appeared along the way.
That wasn’t surprising, most people were still struggling in level 3 and 4 areas.
Going this deep required confidence, power, or recklessness.
Leon had a mix of the three.
Eventually, the dense forest opened up into a clearing.
A small lake shimmered under faint light, surrounded by grass and broken stones.
Near the water, several massive shapes rested calmly.
Leon narrowed his eyes.
[Elemental Bear]
[Level: 7]
[Combat Power: 700]
[Details: Bears capable of controlling elemental forces.
Each one usually masters a single element during childhood.]
Four bears.
Each one radiated a different aura.
One had sparks of lightning dancing across its fur.
Another had small flames flickering along its body.
The third had thick roots and patches of earth clinging to its limbs.
And the last one stood partially submerged in the lake, water swirling lazily around it.
Leon observed them quietly.
"Yeah," he muttered.
"This should be enough."
He stepped forward.
Strong Fireball!
A blazing fireball formed instantly and shot forward.
Leon aimed it straight at the bear covered in roots.
If that one used earth-element abilities, then fire should be its weakness.
BOOM!
The fireball exploded on impact.
Flames engulfed the bear for a split second before its massive body collapsed onto the ground, lifeless.
Instant kill.
Leon didn’t slow down.
Unfortunately, fire wasn’t ideal against the other three.
He didn’t have spells tailored to each element yet.
So he switched tactics.
Fwish!
Leon closed the distance in an instant, his [Poison Fang Dagger +3] flashing in his hand.
Slash!
He slashed across the flame-type bear’s side.
The blade cut deep, and a sickly green poison immediately spread through the wound.
The dagger’s passive activated instantly, eating away at the bear’s vitality.
Roar!
The remaining three bears reacted at once.
The water-type and lightning-type bears roared loudly, elemental energy gathering around them.
Zap!
Splash!
A bolt of lightning and a condensed water projectile shot toward Leon.
Leon twisted his body smoothly, dodging both attacks without difficulty.
He dashed forward again.
The flame-type bear was already slowing down.
Poison coursed through its body, weakening it rapidly.
Slash!
Before it could even retaliate, Leon ended its life with a clean strike.
Two down.
The remaining bears hesitated.
Fear flickered in their eyes.
They had seen two of their companions die in seconds.
Strong Fireball!
Leon fired another spell, this time targeting the lightning-type bear.
The bear leapt aside, barely avoiding the explosion.
But that was exactly what Leon wanted.
Slash!
In the next instant, Leon was already behind it.
The dagger flashed.
The lightning-type bear’s head separated from its body and fell to the ground.
Blood splattered across the grass.
Only one remained.
ROOOAR!
The water-type bear roared furiously.
It retreated backward and plunged fully into the lake.
Water surged violently as it gathered the surrounding liquid.
The surface of the lake began to churn.
A massive [Water Ball] formed, growing larger and larger until it was the size of a car.
Leon frowned.
’That’s dangerous.’ The water ball shot toward him at terrifying speed, ’But... it’s fine.’
Strong Fireball!
Leon launched a fireball straight into the incoming attack.
The two collided.
The water ball slowed for a moment, just enough.
Leon dashed to the side.
BAM!
The water ball smashed into the ground where Leon had been standing, creating a violent explosion of water and force.
Leon raised his arm to shield his face as debris scattered everywhere.
When the water settled, the bear realized something: the human was still alive.
Its movements slowed as a result.
Fwish!
Slash!
So Leon closed the distance and ended it.
The bear’s head rolled into the lake.
Silence returned to the clearing.
Ding!
[You have killed x4 "Elemental Bears" and gained 400 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered.
Items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 6!]
[You have gained 5 points in all attributes and 5 free points to distribute.]
"All free points into [Spirit]," Leon said instantly.
Then he checked the drops.
[Elemental Bear Essence x4: Consuming will increase Spirit by 4.]
[Elemental Stone x4: A stone that reacts to a specific element.
Currently has no known use.]
Leon raised an eyebrow.
"Hm."
He stored the stones without much thought and consumed the essences.
His Spirit climbed again.
He smiled.
Level requirement met.
Spirit requirement, almost.
Next, Leon equipped the [Sage’s Chain].
Beep!
[You already have two necklaces equipped.
Please remove one.]
"Oh, right."
Leon glanced at his equipment.
He was currently wearing the [Shadow Necklace +2] and the [Purple Jade Necklace].
After a short pause, he removed the [Shadow Necklace +2].
The necklace vanished.
Thankfully—
[Spirit: 155]
Leon exhaled softly.
If his Spirit had dropped below the requirement after removing it, that would’ve been embarrassing.
It had happened more times than he liked to remember in his past life.
With the [Sage’s Chain] equipped, Leon felt an immediate change.
His mana pool expanded.
His thoughts felt clearer.
Spellcasting felt... smoother.
Without wasting time, he summoned the spell scroll: [Lightning Strike].
Fwoosh!
Leon poured his mana into it and tore the scroll apart.
Ding!
[You have learned the skill "Lightning Strike."]
"Second spell," Leon said with a grin.
He clenched his fist, "And I still have plenty of [Skill Stones] and [Enhancement Stones]."
He had been waiting for this moment.
Now that he had the chain equipped and the spell learned, there was no reason to hold back anymore.
"...Time to get stronger."

chapters.title: Chapter 18: Upgrading Skills, Increasing Combat Power
paragraphs: [Skill Stone x10]
[Enhancement Stone x7]
With this many stones, Leon didn’t even need to hesitate.
This wasn’t a small gain anymore, this was a real power spike. Enough to push his skills and equipment far beyond what any normal novice player should be capable of.
And Leon had no intention of saving them. He immediately began using the stones.
First came the skills. He took five [Skill Stones] and focused them on his newest spell: lightning Strike.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have upgraded "Lightning Strike (Level 1)" to "Lightning Strike (Level 2)"]
A surge of power flowed through him, and Leon could immediately feel the difference. The lightning he summoned felt denser, sharper, more obedient.
Next, he used three more stones on his main spell: Strong Fireball.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have upgraded "Strong Fireball (Level 3)" to "Strong Fireball (Level 4)"]
The heat in his core intensified. His fire had always been reliable, but now it felt heavier, like it carried real destructive intent instead of just raw flames.
Finally, he used the last two [Skill Stones] on a utility skill that had saved him more times than he could count: Vision Enhancement.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have upgraded "Vision Enhancement (Level 2)" to "Vision Enhancement (Level 3)"]
Leon opened the description immediately.
[Vision Enhancement (Level 3): Consume a certain amount of Spirit to enhance one’s dynamic vision for 60 seconds, 2-minutes cooldown.]
"Perfect."
A full minute. That meant longer fights, clearer tracking, and far more room for error correction.
In fast-paced combat, especially against stronger monsters or skilled opponents, that extra time was priceless.
Leon closed the panel and shifted his attention to the remaining stones.
Seven [Enhancement Stones]. He didn’t even consider spreading them around.
"All in on [Sage’s Chain]."
An epic-rank item was on a completely different level compared to the rest of his equipment. Upgrading it would give returns that no uncommon or rare item could match.
Leon crushed the stones one by one, focusing all the enhancement energy into the chain around his neck.
Ding!
[You have successfully enhanced your "Sage’s Chain"]
[Sage’s Chain +2 (Epic): +200 Spirit, -20% Cooldown Reduction.]
Leon inhaled sharply.
"Nice."
The increase was massive. His Spirit surged again, flooding his body with a calm, controlled power.
Even better, the cooldown reduction improved further, letting him use his spells more freely in extended battles.
Upgrading it again would take ten enhancement stones, a ridiculous amount, but even at +2, the chain was already absurdly strong.
Leon felt no regret about his choice. He checked his combat power next.
[Combat Power: 1,036 (+740)]
"...Damn."
He let out a quiet laugh.
At level 6, this number was completely unreasonable. Most players at this stage barely scratched a few hundred combat power.
And Leon? He was already nearing what some level 10 players had in his past life.
"I should be able to go even deeper now."
Leon looked ahead, toward the heart of the [Wild Forest].

Normally, players avoided that area entirely. Once someone reached level 10, they were forced to advance to the next stage of [Eternal Ascension], meaning there was very little incentive to risk death by pushing too far early.
But Leon wasn’t normal. And more importantly, this was his second life.
He knew what waited ahead. He knew the races, the factions, the enemies.
And he knew what would happen if he let them grow unchecked.
’Since I’m stronger now,’ Leon thought as he began moving again, ’I can kill them before they become a problem.’

In his past life, many beings from other races allied themselves with gods or higher existences. That single choice allowed them to skyrocket in power, and eventually, they turned that power against everything.
Leon wouldn’t let that happen again.
If he wanted to survive, and protect the few people he actually cared about, then this was necessary.
He pushed forward without slowing down.
Soon, the forest changed.
The air grew heavier. The trees thickened, their trunks darker, their shadows deeper.
Leon had entered the level 8 area.
And the moment he stepped forward—
BOOM!
A spell slammed into him.
Leon was pushed back half a step as a barrier flared around his body, the defensive skill of the [Purple Jade Necklace] activating automatically.
He immediately turned toward the source. An [Elemental Bear].
The bear stared at him, clearly shocked that its attack hadn’t killed the human instantly.
Leon raised an eyebrow.
The bear growled and began gathering energy again.
Leon smiled.
"Perfect timing."
Lightning Strike!
He pointed his arm forward.
In an instant, lightning condensed around his hand, forming a sharp, crackling bolt before launching forward.
Zap!
The lightning struck the bear squarely, electricity coursing through its massive body.
The bear froze mid-motion. Stunned.
Slash!
Leon closed the distance in a blink and cleanly decapitated it before the stun even wore off.
"...Yeah," Leon nodded, satisfied. "This spell’s good."
Ding!
[You have killed "Elemental Bear" and gained 70 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered, items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
Leon noticed the experience gain immediately. Lower than before.
When he had killed these bears at level 5, he earned more.
That was how the system worked.
The stronger you became, the less value weaker monsters provided. [Eternal Ascension] didn’t reward stagnation, it forced growth.
If you wanted to level efficiently, you had to fight monsters at or above your level.
Leon didn’t dislike that. It made sense.
At level 6, he now needed 2,000 experience points to level up. A massive increase compared to before.
He consumed the [Elemental Bear Essence] and continued forward.
On his way deeper into the forest, Leon encountered new monsters.
Among them were level 8 [Dark Turtles].
Thick shells. Slow movement. Extremely high defense.
His fireballs hit them, and did almost nothing.
"...You’ve got to be kidding me."
Leon clicked his tongue.
Magic was nearly useless against them. Thankfully, his strength wasn’t.
He focused his body instead of his spells and stepped in.
Slash!
His blade scraped against the shell at first, but repeated strikes began to crack it.
Slash! Slash!
After a few clean hits, the turtle finally collapsed. The others followed soon after.
Ding!
[You have killed x6 "Dark Turtles" and gained 720 experience points.]
They dropped [Dark Turtle Essence], increasing Constitution by 4, along with several [Dark Shell Shields].
Leon collected them all. After obtaining four shields, he decided to try fusing them.
The first enhancement succeeded. The second failed.
[Dark Shell Shield +2 (Uncommon): +100 Defense, +90 Attack Resistance.]
"Tch."
Leon shrugged. He didn’t use shields anyway. Aaron would probably be happy to buy it later.
After that, Leon kept moving.
The forest grew darker. The pressure increased.
And eventually—
He stepped into a massive clearing. The ground was torn apart, trees broken and scorched.
At the center of it all stood a massive figure. A boss.
Leon slowly lifted his gaze, a grin forming on his face.

chapters.title: Chapter 19: Fire Lizard Boss, Sub-Talents Are Here!
paragraphs: [Fire Lizard (Boss)]
[Level: 9]
[Talent: Constitution Enhancement (F-Level)]
[Combat Power: 1,500]
[Details: a lizard that really likes to burn things, it is its hobby to burn parts of the wild forest.]
As monsters and beasts grew stronger, their [Combat Power] would naturally rise alongside their levels.
This increase wasn’t linear either. Lower-level creatures gained power slowly, but the higher their level became, the more noticeable the jump.
And among all of them, bosses were the most extreme cases.
Some bosses possessed combat power far beyond what their level alone suggested, making them infamous obstacles that wiped out careless players.
Still, Leon felt no pressure at all.
Right now, his own combat power sat at around 1,700.
That already put him comfortably above the [Fire Lizard].
The creature itself was massive, standing close to two meters tall. Its body was covered in thick crimson scales that glowed faintly, as if heat was constantly trapped beneath them.
Flames leaked from between the plates of its armor-like hide, scorching the ground wherever it stepped.
Around it, several trees were already burning, their trunks blackened and cracked as fire crawled upward.
But what truly caught Leon’s attention wasn’t its size or its destructive behavior. It was the talent.
Monsters could possess talents just like players.
Every being had a main talent, something fundamental to their existence. For players, this was the talent they awakened with, something irreplaceable. Monsters were the same in that regard.
However, in addition to their main talent, both players and monsters could sometimes possess something else entirely: [Sub-Talents].
These were secondary abilities that enhanced specific aspects of one’s body or skills. Their effects varied wildly.
Some were weak and barely noticeable, while others were strong enough to rival, or even surpass, a main talent under the right circumstances.
There were even rumors of SS-Level Sub-Talents.
Leon had never seen one personally, but he knew they existed.
As for SSS-Level sub-talents... he had never heard of a single confirmed case.
Because of that, Leon was quite confident that no talent in [Eternal Ascension] could surpass his own.
Looking at the [Fire Lizard], Leon made a decision almost instantly.
There was no point in wasting mana on fire-based attacks.
A creature like this was almost certainly immune to flames, or at least highly resistant. Throwing a fireball at it would be nothing more than a flashy waste of time.
So instead—
Lightning Strike!
Zap!
A bolt of lightning exploded from Leon’s hand, tearing through the air in a straight line. The moment the [Fire Lizard] turned its head toward him, the lightning struck it directly.
The impact was immediate.
Electricity surged across the creature’s scales, its entire body stiffening as the lightning coursed through it. The [Fire Lizard] froze in place, muscles locked, unable to react.
Leon didn’t hesitate. He rushed forward the instant the spell connected.
Slash!
His blade flashed as he swung toward the lizard’s neck. The edge bit into its scales, carving a deep wound, but before Leon could finish the job—
Bam!
The [Fire Lizard] slammed one of its massive legs into the ground.
A violent shockwave spread outward, and with it came an eruption of fire. Flames burst in a wide circle, consuming the grass and turning the clearing into a sea of burning embers.
Leon immediately leaped backward, narrowly escaping the worst of the blast. Heat washed over him, and behind him, the grass was reduced to ash in seconds.
"Tch."
The boss wasn’t going down that easily.
Vision Enhancement!
Leon activated his ability, and the world around him sharpened. Movements slowed in his perception, every detail becoming clearer and more defined.
The [Fire Lizard] inhaled sharply, flames gathering around its mouth as it prepared another attack.
Fwoosh!
Leon surged forward instead.
With his enhanced vision, the creature’s movements were painfully obvious. Its tail tensed, muscles coiling in preparation for a swing.
The tail came sweeping toward him, trailing fire behind it like a blazing whip.
Leon sidestepped calmly.
Even though their combat power values were close, the difference between them was obvious. Leon’s experience, control, and raw strength completely overwhelmed the boss.
Slash!
His blade came down on the tail.
The reinforced scales shattered under the force of the strike, and the tail was severed cleanly in half. The burning appendage crashed to the ground, flames sputtering as it twitched.
ROOAR!
The [Fire Lizard] let out a deafening roar filled with pain and rage. Its body twisted, trying to retaliate, but Leon was already moving.
SLASH!
In a single, fluid motion, Leon cut upward, slicing through the lizard’s neck. He didn’t even bother casting another spell. This was pure physical power.
The massive head fell from the body, hitting the ground with a heavy thud. Flames flared briefly around it before fading away.
The body collapsed moments later, lifeless.
Ding!
[You have killed "Fire Lizard (Level 9 Boss)" and gained 1,000 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered, items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 7!]
[You have gained 5 points in all attributes and 5 free points to distribute.]
"Nice."
Leon let out a satisfied breath.
Boss monsters always gave more experience than regular ones, and since this boss was higher-level than him, the reward was even greater.
With this level-up, every single one of Leon’s attributes had finally surpassed 100.
That alone was a massive milestone.
Without wasting time, Leon opened his storage space and focused on the real prize: the drops.
’I wonder...’ Leon thought, ’if that talent will drop as well.’
Bosses that possessed talents were rare. Even when they did, those talents were usually low-tier, like this F-Level one.
On top of that, the drop rate for talents was abysmally low. Most players were lucky to ever obtain even a single sub-talent in their entire time playing.
Yet as Leon looked at the items now resting in his storage space, a grin slowly spread across his face.
[Eternal Coins x50]
[Fire Lizard Essence: Consuming will increase spirit by 5 and strength by 4.]
[Flame Tail Sword (Rare): +100 Attack, +50 Strength. May apply "Burn" on a target. Requirement: At least one fire-related skill.]
[Sub-Talent Scroll: Constitution Enhancement (F-Level). Requirement: 150 Constitution.]
"Damn."
This was an incredible haul.
Leon immediately added the Eternal Coins to his balance and consumed the essence without hesitation. A warm sensation spread through his body as his spirit and strength increased.
Then his attention shifted to the final two items.
’A new weapon... and a sub-talent. Just as expected.’
Because Leon’s talent allowed him to obtain everything a monster possessed, it meant that whenever he killed a boss with a talent, there was an extremely high chance he would get it.
With that in mind, Leon couldn’t help but imagine his future.
Multiple sub-talents. Permanent enhancements stacking on top of each other.
The thought alone was enough to make his heart race.
Leon unequipped the [Poison Fang Dagger +3] and equipped the [Flame Tail Sword] instead. The blade felt heavier in his hand, but also far more powerful.
Thankfully, he had [Strong Fireball], which fulfilled the requirement.
Even at level 1, the sword’s stats surpassed the dagger’s. There was no reason to keep the old weapon anymore.
Leon immediately listed the dagger on the [Trading House] for 75 Eternal Coins.
It sold almost instantly. Satisfied, Leon turned his attention to the [Sub-Talent Scroll].
These scrolls were absurdly valuable. In the future, they would sell for tens of thousands of Eternal Coins, easily.
Even an F-Level talent was still a permanent bonus, and bonuses like that were priceless. The only real downside was the requirement, which could be absurdly high.
Luckily for Leon, his constitution was more than enough.
Without hesitation, he poured his mana into the scroll and tore it apart.
Fwoosh! Ding!
Golden particles burst from the scroll, swirling around him before engraving themselves into his body.
[Congratulations, you have learned the F-Level Sub-Talent: "Constitution Enhancement"]
[Constitution Enhancement (F-Level): Permanently increase constitution by 10%.]
"Nice."
This was exactly the kind of sub-talent Leon liked.
Simple. Practical. Always active.
A permanent 10% increase in constitution might not sound impressive at first, but as his base stats continued to rise, the value of this talent would grow alongside them.
And its evolutions? They were far stronger.
Satisfied with the results, Leon checked his status once more.
With the level-up, new equipment, and sub-talent, his combat power had officially surpassed 2,000.
That alone placed him far ahead of where he should be at this stage.
After finishing his preparations, Leon didn’t stop.
He continued deeper into the forest.
He was already close to the deepest parts of the wild forest, and turning back now would be pointless.
With his current [Combat Power], level 10 monsters were well within his reach. There was nothing to fear.
After several minutes of steady movement, Leon slowed to a stop.
Something massive loomed ahead. A structure.
"Oh," Leon muttered as he looked up, "I guess I’m back here after so long."
Before him stood the [Wild Ruins]. The most dangerous zone in the entire [Wild Forest].

sentences.text: [Fire Lizard (Boss)]
[Level: 9]
[Talent: Constitution Enhancement (F-Level)]
[Combat Power: 1,500]
[Details: a lizard that really likes to burn things, it is its hobby to burn parts of the wild forest.]
As monsters and beasts grew stronger, their [Combat Power] would naturally rise alongside their levels.
This increase wasn’t linear either.
Lower-level creatures gained power slowly, but the higher their level became, the more noticeable the jump.
And among all of them, bosses were the most extreme cases.
Some bosses possessed combat power far beyond what their level alone suggested, making them infamous obstacles that wiped out careless players.
Still, Leon felt no pressure at all.
Right now, his own combat power sat at around 1,700.
That already put him comfortably above the [Fire Lizard].
The creature itself was massive, standing close to two meters tall.
Its body was covered in thick crimson scales that glowed faintly, as if heat was constantly trapped beneath them.
Flames leaked from between the plates of its armor-like hide, scorching the ground wherever it stepped.
Around it, several trees were already burning, their trunks blackened and cracked as fire crawled upward.
But what truly caught Leon’s attention wasn’t its size or its destructive behavior.
It was the talent.
Monsters could possess talents just like players.
Every being had a main talent, something fundamental to their existence.
For players, this was the talent they awakened with, something irreplaceable.
Monsters were the same in that regard.
However, in addition to their main talent, both players and monsters could sometimes possess something else entirely: [Sub-Talents].
These were secondary abilities that enhanced specific aspects of one’s body or skills.
Their effects varied wildly.
Some were weak and barely noticeable, while others were strong enough to rival, or even surpass, a main talent under the right circumstances.
There were even rumors of SS-Level Sub-Talents.
Leon had never seen one personally, but he knew they existed.
As for SSS-Level sub-talents... he had never heard of a single confirmed case.
Because of that, Leon was quite confident that no talent in [Eternal Ascension] could surpass his own.
Looking at the [Fire Lizard], Leon made a decision almost instantly.
There was no point in wasting mana on fire-based attacks.
A creature like this was almost certainly immune to flames, or at least highly resistant.
Throwing a fireball at it would be nothing more than a flashy waste of time.
So instead—
Lightning Strike!
Zap!
A bolt of lightning exploded from Leon’s hand, tearing through the air in a straight line.
The moment the [Fire Lizard] turned its head toward him, the lightning struck it directly.
The impact was immediate.
Electricity surged across the creature’s scales, its entire body stiffening as the lightning coursed through it.
The [Fire Lizard] froze in place, muscles locked, unable to react.
Leon didn’t hesitate.
He rushed forward the instant the spell connected.
Slash!
His blade flashed as he swung toward the lizard’s neck.
The edge bit into its scales, carving a deep wound, but before Leon could finish the job—
Bam!
The [Fire Lizard] slammed one of its massive legs into the ground.
A violent shockwave spread outward, and with it came an eruption of fire.
Flames burst in a wide circle, consuming the grass and turning the clearing into a sea of burning embers.
Leon immediately leaped backward, narrowly escaping the worst of the blast.
Heat washed over him, and behind him, the grass was reduced to ash in seconds.
"Tch."
The boss wasn’t going down that easily.
Vision Enhancement!
Leon activated his ability, and the world around him sharpened.
Movements slowed in his perception, every detail becoming clearer and more defined.
The [Fire Lizard] inhaled sharply, flames gathering around its mouth as it prepared another attack.
Fwoosh!
Leon surged forward instead.
With his enhanced vision, the creature’s movements were painfully obvious.
Its tail tensed, muscles coiling in preparation for a swing.
The tail came sweeping toward him, trailing fire behind it like a blazing whip.
Leon sidestepped calmly.
Even though their combat power values were close, the difference between them was obvious.
Leon’s experience, control, and raw strength completely overwhelmed the boss.
Slash!
His blade came down on the tail.
The reinforced scales shattered under the force of the strike, and the tail was severed cleanly in half.
The burning appendage crashed to the ground, flames sputtering as it twitched.
ROOAR!
The [Fire Lizard] let out a deafening roar filled with pain and rage.
Its body twisted, trying to retaliate, but Leon was already moving.
SLASH!
In a single, fluid motion, Leon cut upward, slicing through the lizard’s neck.
He didn’t even bother casting another spell.
This was pure physical power.
The massive head fell from the body, hitting the ground with a heavy thud.
Flames flared briefly around it before fading away.
The body collapsed moments later, lifeless.
Ding!
[You have killed "Fire Lizard (Level 9 Boss)" and gained 1,000 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered, items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 7!]
[You have gained 5 points in all attributes and 5 free points to distribute.]
"Nice."
Leon let out a satisfied breath.
Boss monsters always gave more experience than regular ones, and since this boss was higher-level than him, the reward was even greater.
With this level-up, every single one of Leon’s attributes had finally surpassed 100.
That alone was a massive milestone.
Without wasting time, Leon opened his storage space and focused on the real prize: the drops.
’I wonder...’ Leon thought, ’if that talent will drop as well.’
Bosses that possessed talents were rare.
Even when they did, those talents were usually low-tier, like this F-Level one.
On top of that, the drop rate for talents was abysmally low.
Most players were lucky to ever obtain even a single sub-talent in their entire time playing.
Yet as Leon looked at the items now resting in his storage space, a grin slowly spread across his face.
[Eternal Coins x50]
[Fire Lizard Essence: Consuming will increase spirit by 5 and strength by 4.]
[Flame Tail Sword (Rare): +100 Attack, +50 Strength.
May apply "Burn" on a target.
Requirement: At least one fire-related skill.]
[Sub-Talent Scroll: Constitution Enhancement (F-Level).
Requirement: 150 Constitution.]
"Damn."
This was an incredible haul.
Leon immediately added the Eternal Coins to his balance and consumed the essence without hesitation.
A warm sensation spread through his body as his spirit and strength increased.
Then his attention shifted to the final two items.
’A new weapon... and a sub-talent.
Just as expected.’
Because Leon’s talent allowed him to obtain everything a monster possessed, it meant that whenever he killed a boss with a talent, there was an extremely high chance he would get it.
With that in mind, Leon couldn’t help but imagine his future.
Multiple sub-talents.
Permanent enhancements stacking on top of each other.
The thought alone was enough to make his heart race.
Leon unequipped the [Poison Fang Dagger +3] and equipped the [Flame Tail Sword] instead.
The blade felt heavier in his hand, but also far more powerful.
Thankfully, he had [Strong Fireball], which fulfilled the requirement.
Even at level 1, the sword’s stats surpassed the dagger’s.
There was no reason to keep the old weapon anymore.
Leon immediately listed the dagger on the [Trading House] for 75 Eternal Coins.
It sold almost instantly.
Satisfied, Leon turned his attention to the [Sub-Talent Scroll].
These scrolls were absurdly valuable.
In the future, they would sell for tens of thousands of Eternal Coins, easily.
Even an F-Level talent was still a permanent bonus, and bonuses like that were priceless.
The only real downside was the requirement, which could be absurdly high.
Luckily for Leon, his constitution was more than enough.
Without hesitation, he poured his mana into the scroll and tore it apart.
Fwoosh!
Ding!
Golden particles burst from the scroll, swirling around him before engraving themselves into his body.

[Constitution Enhancement (F-Level): Permanently increase constitution by 10%.]

Simple.
Practical.
Always active.

Something massive loomed ahead.
A structure.

Before him stood the [Wild Ruins].
The most dangerous zone in the entire [Wild Forest].

chapters.title: Chapter 20: The Wild Ruins, Hard Difficulty
paragraphs: The [Wild Ruins] was usually the very first dungeon that players encountered on their path toward reaching level 10.
In [Eternal Ascension], dungeons varied greatly in difficulty, structure, and danger.
Some were sprawling labyrinths filled with traps, others were short but brutally intense. Still, among all of them, many players agreed on one thing.
The [Wild Ruins] was considered the easiest dungeon.
Of course, that reputation came with a massive condition: most players chose the easiest difficulty.
Leon slowly approached the entrance of the ruins. The structure itself looked ancient, built from massive stone blocks covered in worn-down runes.
Time had eroded their edges, yet the dungeon still radiated a heavy, oppressive aura.
The moment Leon stepped close enough, a translucent panel appeared in front of him.
[Which difficulty do you wish to choose?]
[Easy] [Normal] [Hard]
Leon stared at the options without moving.
Above [Hard], there technically existed even higher difficulties like [Hell] and [Nightmare].
However, no one could actually challenge them at this stage, and they weren’t even available in this dungeon.
Even in Leon’s past life, no matter how talented or confident someone was, they were forced to choose [Normal] or [Hard]. There simply wasn’t another option.
The dungeon system itself was unforgiving.
The level of the monsters inside the [Wild Ruins] never changed. No matter the difficulty, they were all level 10.
What changed was everything else: their strength, combat power, durability, and more importantly, their intelligence.
On higher difficulties, monsters didn’t just hit harder. They fought smarter. They coordinated, reacted faster, and punished mistakes mercilessly.
Leon knew all of this very well.
He had never once heard of any human clearing the [Hard] difficulty of the [Wild Ruins]. It was simply too overwhelming.
And yet, Leon wanted to be the first.
The rewards would be far better, both in terms of drops and experience. Clearing [Hard] would widen the gap between him and everyone else by an absurd amount.
The usual recommended combat power for entering the [Wild Ruins] on [Easy] difficulty was around 1,000.
For [Normal], it jumped to about 1,500. And for [Hard], 2,500 at the very least.
Leon’s current combat power was slightly above 2,000.
Strictly speaking, he didn’t meet the requirements.
And yet...
"Gotta risk it," Leon grinned.
[Level Leaderboard:]
[1. Leon Skyward: Level 7]
[2. Eleonore Starlight: Level 5]
[3. David Windbreak: Level 5]
[4. Aaron Godfield: Level 5]
[5. Elliot Dusekaar: Level 5]
Leon glanced at the leaderboard.
Many players had already reached level 5 or 4. Compared to his past life, this was incredibly fast.
The reason was simple.
This time around, nobody had suffered the massive penalty that came from losing the opening event.
Without that setback, overall progression skyrocketed.
Still, none of that mattered. Leon was still far ahead of everyone else.
And once he cleared the [Wild Ruins], the gap would only grow wider.
Without hesitating any longer, Leon extended his arm and pressed his finger against the [Hard] option.
Fwoosh!
The panel shimmered briefly as his selection registered.
Ding!
[Wild Ruins (Hard Difficulty) has been selected.]
The moment Leon stepped forward, his surroundings distorted. The entrance vanished, replaced by swirling colors as space itself twisted.
Fwish!
A vortex swallowed him whole.
After a few seconds, his feet touched solid ground again.
Leon found himself inside the [Wild Ruins].

The chamber around him was enormous. Stone walls rose high above, carved with glowing runes that pulsed faintly with energy. He stood in the middle of a circular platform, its surface engraved with ancient patterns.
Several stone bridges extended outward from the platform, each leading deeper into the dungeon.
Below them flowed a river of thick crimson liquid. It moved slowly, almost lazily, but Leon felt an instinctive sense of danger just from looking at it.
He had no intention of finding out what it was.
A dungeon’s challenge could vary depending on difficulty, but since no additional panels appeared, Leon guessed this was a straightforward dungeon: reach the end and defeat the boss.
Leon calmly walked toward one of the bridges.
As he stepped onto it, the stone beneath his feet felt solid, but the oppressive atmosphere intensified.
’As expected,’ Leon thought while crossing, ’the dungeon layout changes depending on the difficulty.’
The [Easy] and [Normal] versions of the [Wild Ruins] were almost identical.
The [Hard] version was completely different.
When Leon reached the end of the bridge—
BOOM!
A loud noise echoed through the chamber.
The stone floor ahead cracked, and several massive figures began rising from the ground.
Leon stopped.
[Ruins Golem]
[Level: 10]
[Combat Power: 1,500]
[Details: Golems created by a powerful being, they have been in these ruins for a long time.]
Five golems stood in front of him, completely blocking the path forward.
Their bodies were made of solid stone, each one towering over Leon.
Cracks ran along their frames, glowing faintly with inner heat.
Where their faces should have been, hollow openings burned with small, flickering flames.
They stood perfectly still, like statues.
’Trying to throw me in there?’ Leon grinned while glancing at the crimson river behind him. ’Won’t work.’
Each golem had terrifying combat power for its level. Any one of them could rival the [Fire Lizard] boss Leon had just defeated.
Facing five at once would have been impossible for most players. But Leon wasn’t most players.
Strong Fireball!
He raised his hand and launched a massive fireball forward.
The explosion slammed into the center golem, sending fragments of stone flying and disrupting the formation of the others.
Fwoosh!
Leon surged forward instantly. His [Flame Tail Sword] flashed as he struck the closest golem.
Crack!
The golem’s head shattered completely from the force of the blow, its body collapsing lifelessly.
Leon didn’t stop. He pivoted and swung at another golem. This time, the remaining golems reacted.
Swing!
A massive rocky fist came crashing down toward Leon. He twisted his body and leapt back, narrowly avoiding the attack.
At least he was no longer on the bridge. Falling was no longer an immediate threat. Unless they grabbed him.
And that seemed to be exactly what they were trying to do.
Instead of throwing punches, the golems lunged forward, arms outstretched, attempting to seize Leon.
"Perhaps throwing things into that liquid fuels something," Leon muttered.
Vision Enhancement!
His perception sharpened instantly.
The movements of the golems slowed in his eyes, making their intentions obvious. Leon dodged between them with precise steps, slipping past grasping stone hands.
Lightning Strike!
Zap!
A bolt of lightning slammed into one of the golems.
The electricity danced across its stone body, but it didn’t even flinch.
"Oh, right," Leon clicked his tongue. Stone wasn’t exactly conductive.
Strong Fireball!
He fired another spell. The explosion was violent.
Two golems were blasted apart, their bodies shattered into chunks of stone. They weren’t destroyed completely, but their forms were heavily damaged.
The remaining two golems rushed Leon.
Leon met them head-on.
With a single swing of his sword, he shattered one’s torso. Another swing reduced the second to rubble.
Even though their combat power was close to his own, Leon’s experience, reflexes, and skill put him far above them.
Leon turned toward the last two golems, their broken bodies twitching on the ground.
He stepped forward, ready to finish them off.
Then—
BOOM!
A sudden explosion shook the chamber. Leon froze.
The shattered remains of the two golems began to tremble violently.
"Wait a minute," Leon’s eyes widened slightly. "No way."
Stone fragments lifted into the air.
The two broken bodies began pulling toward each other, merging together as cracks sealed and energy surged.
Piece by piece, they fused into a single, towering mass.
"Hah... of course," Leon sighed.
[Ruins Golem (Mutated)]
[Level: 10]
[Combat Power: 1,900]
[Details: Two golems fusing with one another to create a stronger being.]
Leon had just witnessed a mutation.
It was rare, but not unheard of. In the future, mutations like this would become more common, especially in higher-difficulty content.
And now, the golem’s combat power had surpassed Leon’s.
ROAR!
The mutated golem let out a deafening roar. A shockwave rippled outward, shaking the chamber and rattling the bridges.
Leon tightened his grip on his sword. Even now, ke didn’t step back.
Instead, he raised his blade and prepared to attack.

chapters.title: Chapter 21: Mutated Ruins Golem, Acquiring The First Staff
paragraphs: Leon stared at the mutated ruins golem with a calm, almost empty expression, his sword already raised and ready to strike.
The effects of [Vision Enhancement] were still active, sharpening the world around him—but not for long. At most, he had fifteen seconds left.
Without it, dodging would become much harder.
Especially against a monster like this.
’Most of its combat power probably comes from raw strength and constitution,’ Leon thought. ’Its agility should still be low.’
Strong Fireball!
Leon thrust his hand forward and launched a blazing fireball straight at the mutated golem.
The massive creature reacted instantly. It raised both of its reinforced stone arms and crossed them in front of its body.
BOOM!
The fireball exploded against its guard, flames spreading everywhere, but when the smoke cleared, the golem was still standing.
"...Damn."
Fwoosh!
The mutated golem bent its legs and leapt forward with terrifying force, covering the distance in a single jump. Its massive arm swung down, aiming not to strike—but to grab.
"Still trying to throw me into that liquid, huh?" Leon’s eyes glinted. "Not happening."
Thanks to [Vision Enhancement], Leon could clearly see the trajectory of the attack. The monster was powerful, but its movements were heavy and predictable.
Leon dashed to the side, then instantly circled behind it.
Slash!
His sword struck the golem’s head with full force.
CRACK!
Deep fractures spread across the stone where Leon hit. The impact echoed through the chamber.
It wasn’t enough to kill it, but it was enough to prove something important.
’I can hurt it.’
That alone was more than enough.
Slam!
The golem twisted and slammed its fist toward Leon, trying to crush him outright.
Leon stepped back effortlessly, avoiding the blow just like before.
For several seconds, the exchange continued.
The mutated golem attacked relentlessly, swinging its arms, stomping the ground, and lunging again and again, desperately trying to seize the human before it.
But none of its attacks connected.
Leon moved smoothly, dodging each strike by a narrow margin, his movements precise and controlled. With [Vision Enhancement] active, every motion of the golem felt slow.
Seeing an opening, Leon stepped in once more.
Slash!
He struck the same cracked area on the golem’s head, deepening the fractures.
The golem reacted instantly, raising both arms to protect its head.
That was exactly what Leon was waiting for.
At the very last moment, he changed his stance.
Strong Fireball!
BOOM!
The spell detonated against the golem’s exposed side.
A massive chunk of its body was blown apart, stone fragments scattering across the chamber.
The mutated golem staggered.
Leon didn’t hesitate.
Slash!
His sword flashed, cutting cleanly through the weakened structure.
The golem collapsed, its massive body crumbling into lifeless rubble.
Ding!
[You have killed x3 "Ruins Golem" and gained 900 experience points.]
[You have killed "Ruins Golem (Mutated)" and gained 700 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered, items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
"Nice."
Leon exhaled lightly.
That fight alone had given him a massive amount of experience. He was now only a few monsters away from leveling up again.
More importantly, his storage space was filled with new items.
[Ruins Golem Essence x3: Consuming will increase Strength by 5.]
[Mutated Ruins Golem Essence: +7 Strength and +5 Constitution.]
[Ruins Golem Armor x4 (Rare): +100 Constitution, +80 Strength, -25 Agility.]
"Oh?"
Leon didn’t waste time.
He immediately consumed all the essences.
A warm sensation spread through his body as his muscles and bones grew denser and stronger.
Then his gaze shifted to the armor.
At a glance, it was clearly superior to the armor he was currently wearing—even at level 1.
The agility penalty wasn’t a flaw. Heavy armor always came with a trade-off.
Leon didn’t hesitate.
Fwish!
[You have consumed two identical equipments... enhancement successful!]
He enhanced the armor twice, creating two identical upgraded pieces.
Then, without stopping, he pushed further.
Fwish!
[Enhancement successful!]
"Yes!"
If that enhancement had failed, both armor pieces would have shattered completely.
But luck was on Leon’s side.
[Ruins Golem Armor +3 (Rare): +250 Constitution, +150 Strength, -10 Agility.]
The increase was massive. Not only did the stats skyrocket, but even the agility penalty was reduced.
That was the true strength of enhanced equipment.
Leon immediately removed his [Poison Mushroom Armor +2] and equipped the new armor.
The moment he did, he could feel the difference.
His body felt heavier, but also far sturdier.
His constitution was now so high that he could probably tank a direct hit from most monsters in this dungeon.
He glanced at his combat power.
[Combat Power: 1,204 (+1370)]
His combat power had officially surpassed 2,500.
"I gained over 500 combat power in an instant," Leon muttered with a grin. "Higher-difficulty dungeons really are the best."
