Ahead of him stood a massive gate.
There were other paths branching off to the sides, each leading deeper into the ruins, but Leon didn’t bother choosing carefully.
He wasn’t here to rush the exit.
He was here to get stronger.
Leon passed through the gate and entered a long hallway.
The corridor was dimly lit by flickering torches embedded in the stone walls. Shadows danced along the floor as Leon walked forward calmly.
Then—
Fwoosh!
A fireball shot out from the darkness ahead.
Leon immediately sidestepped, the spell passing right by him and exploding against the wall.
He reacted without hesitation.
Strong Fireball!
BOOM!
His fireball rushed forward and exploded deep in the hallway.
Ding!
[You have killed "Skeleton Magician (Level 10)" and gained 250 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered...]
"...I didn’t even get to see it."
Leon walked forward and checked the drops.
[Skeleton Magician Essence: Consuming will increase Spirit by 5.]
[Skeleton Staff (Uncommon): +100 Spirit. Requirement: At least knows one spell.]
[Skill Stone]
"Wow, nice."
This single enemy had dropped far more than expected.
Leon actually hoped to encounter more of them.
And as if the dungeon itself had heard him—
Fwish!
The torches at the end of the hallway flared to life.
Seven figures stepped out of the shadows.
Seven skeleton magicians.
Each one held a staff, all of them pointing directly at Leon.
"...Damn."
[Skeleton Magician]
[Level: 10]
[Combat Power: 1,600]
[Details: Skeletons that have learned low-level magic out of boredom after being trapped in these ruins for a long time.]
Fireball! Lightning Strike!
All seven skeleton magicians fired their spells at the same time, flooding the hallway with blazing fire and crackling lightning.
Leon’s expression didn’t change.
He sprinted forward, using the narrow walls of the hallway to his advantage, leaping and rolling past the incoming spells with precise movements.
The skeletons hesitated, clearly shocked.
Before their cooldowns could finish—
Strong Fireball!
Leon raised the skeleton staff he had just acquired in his left hand and pointed it forward.
The fireball he launched this time was far stronger than before.
BOOM!
The explosion engulfed the group.
The blast was so powerful that almost all of the skeleton magicians were destroyed instantly.
When the smoke cleared, only two remained.
They barely had time to react.
Leon was already in front of them.
Slash!
His sword flashed twice.
Both skeletons collapsed, their skulls cleanly severed.
Ding!
[You have killed x7 "Skeleton Magician" and gained 1,750 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered...]
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 8!]
[You have gained 5 points in all attributes and 5 free points to distribute.]
Leon exhaled slowly.
Along with the experience, the skeletons dropped [Skeleton Staff x7], [Skill Stones x7], and [Skeleton Magician Essence x7].
Every single one dropped the same items.
Leon was a bit surprised that no spell scrolls appeared, but his talent couldn’t force drops that didn’t exist.
He consumed all the essences, increasing his spirit by 40.
Then he began fusing the staffs.
Three out of four fusions succeeded, giving him a [Skeleton Staff +2].
He didn’t stop there.
Fwish! Ding!
[Enhancement successful!]
"Nice."
[Skeleton Staff +3 (Uncommon): +300 Spirit.]
It was a very basic weapon.
No special effects. No skills. Just raw spirit.
But Leon didn’t mind.
A 300 spirit boost was enormous, directly adding hundreds of combat power.
Leon held the staff in his left hand and the [Flame Tail Sword] in his right.
"I’m not used to fighting with both a sword and a staff," he muttered. "But I’ll manage."
With that, Leon stepped forward once more.
Deeper into the [Wild Ruins]. Eager to see what else the [Hard] difficulty had waiting for him.

chapters.title: Chapter 22: Level 9, Reaching the End of the Wild Ruins
paragraphs: Now that Leon’s combat power had climbed past 3,000, he wasn’t particularly afraid of the monsters inside the [Wild Ruins] anymore, even on [Hard] difficulty.
As he walked through yet another long stone hallway, he casually glanced at the items in his storage space, his attention landing on the [Skill Stones x8].
"Let’s see..."
Upgrading [Vision Enhancement] or [Appraisal] cost 3 skill stones each.
[Strong Fireball] required 5. And [Lightning Strike] needed a hefty 7.
Leon didn’t hesitate for long.
If he wanted efficiency, he had to pick the option that gave him the most overall value.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have upgraded "Strong Fireball (Level 4)" to "Strong Fireball (Level 5)"]
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have upgraded "Vision Enhancement (Level 3)" to "Vision Enhancement (Level 4)"]
Leon immediately checked the updated descriptions.
[Vision Enhancement (Level 4): Consume a certain amount of Spirit to enhance one’s dynamic vision for 60 seconds, 2-minutes cooldown.]
[Strong Fireball (Level 5): Focus your Spirit and condense it into a very strong fireball that strikes a target and may apply "Burn."]
"Nice."
Leon nodded in satisfaction.
These skill levels were already absurd for someone still inside the [Novice Village] phase.
Most players wouldn’t even dream of having level 5 offensive skills at this stage. And yet, Leon wasn’t satisfied.
He knew this wasn’t even close to his limit.
After all, even level 10 monsters couldn’t survive a single direct hit from his fireballs anymore. That alone was proof of how overwhelming his power had become.
With his upgraded skeleton staff in his left hand and the [Flame Tail Sword] in his right, Leon reached the end of the hallway where he had fought the skeleton magicians.
Holding two weapons at once still felt strange.
He was used to wielding a sword that boosted his magic, not splitting his focus between a blade and a staff.
Still, he knew this setup was temporary.
Once he acquired the items he truly wanted, this awkward fighting style would disappear.
Leon stepped forward, and froze.
"Huh?"
What appeared before him was completely different from what he expected.
In the [Easy] and [Normal] difficulties, the [Wild Ruins] remained indoors from start to finish: stone halls, chambers, bridges, and underground structures.
But now? Leon was outside.
Before him stretched a dense forest, thick with towering trees and tangled roots.
Sunlight filtered through the canopy above, casting broken shadows across the ground. The air felt alive, filled with faint spiritual energy.
"This isn’t normal..." Leon muttered.
He scratched his chin lightly.
"Maybe... even the boss is different?"
The dungeon layout had already diverged heavily from what he remembered. The monsters were stronger, smarter, and more aggressive.
In [Easy] and [Normal], the final boss was always the [Ruins Guardian], with its strength adjusted to the chosen difficulty.
But in Leon’s past life, many players speculated that the [Ruins Guardian] wasn’t the true ruler of the [Wild Forest].
They believed something stronger existed, but was unreachable.
Most assumed it was hidden behind [Hard] difficulty. Leon’s eyes gleamed.
"Looks like they were right."
He moved forward without hesitation, stepping into the forest beyond the ruins.
As he pushed through the trees, monsters quickly began to appear.
[Nature Foxes] darted between roots and bushes, their green-tinted fur blending perfectly with the surroundings.
A [Flower Fiend] emerged from the ground, its body made of twisting vines and thorn-covered petals.
None of them stood a chance. Leon raised his staff.
Strong Fireball!
BOOM!
One monster was erased instantly.
Lightning Strike!
Zap!
Another collapsed before it could even react.
If any survived or managed to dodge, Leon finished them with a single slash of his sword.
His raw strength alone was enough to crush level 10 monsters with ease.
Most of these enemies had combat power close to 2,000, far stronger than the monsters inside the ruins.
But against Leon, it didn’t matter.
His talent activated again and again, ensuring that every kill dropped everything it could.
Still, Leon didn’t stop to inspect every item. Right now, momentum mattered more than loot.
And eventually—
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 9!]
[You have gained 5 points in all attributes and 5 free points to distribute.]
"Phew."
Leon exhaled slowly. Only one more level.
Once he reached level 10, he would be forced to leave the [Novice Village] phase and enter the [Novice Divine Temple].
That was where the true [Eternal Ascension] began.
Compared to what came after, the novice phase really was just a playground.
Leon wasn’t scared. Unlike his past life, he knew what awaited him. And because of that... he felt calm.
He opened his [Storage Space] and reviewed everything he had obtained so far.
[Eternal Coins x285]
[Nature Fox Essence x9: +5 Spirit, +3 Agility.]
[Flower Fiend Essence x7: +4 Strength, +4 Constitution.]
[Nature Boots x5: +100 Agility, +50 Constitution. Requirement: Level 9.]
[Flower Petals x6: Cosmetic accessory. May be sold.]
[Skill Stones x8]
[Enhancement Stones x6]
"This is a lot."
Leon immediately began using the items. He consumed every essence without hesitation. Warm energy flooded his body.
[+28 Strength, +28 Constitution, +45 Spirit, +27 Agility.]
His stats climbed even higher.
Next, he focused on the [Nature Boots]. He attempted to fuse them.
Unfortunately, only one of the enhancement attempts succeeded. Two shattered into fragments.
Still, Leon wasn’t disappointed.
[Nature Boots +2 (Rare): +150 Agility, +75 Constitution.]
"Good enough."
He equipped them instantly.
As for the [Flower Petals], Leon shrugged and left them in storage. Cosmetic items sometimes gained value later on.
With his stats adjusted and equipment upgraded, Leon continued moving forward.
He was about to allocate his remaining stones when he stopped. Ahead was a small clearing. Three figures stood within it.
"Huh."
Leon scanned the surroundings first.
Trees formed a complete circle around the clearing, thick and impenetrable.
There was nothing beyond this place. Which meant only one thing.
"This is it."
The boss area.
Leon shifted his attention to the monsters. Two stood at the front.
The first was massive, a carnivorous flower over five meters tall.
Its blood-red petals looked like twisted tongues, constantly moving and releasing a heavy, suffocating fragrance into the air.
Sharp, jagged teeth lined the edges of its petals, glinting coldly.
The second figure was familiar: the [Ruins Guardian]. The same boss players fought on [Easy] and [Normal] difficulty.
[Ruins Guardian (Boss)]
[Level: 10]
[Combat Power: 2,500]
[Status: Controlled.]
[Details: The usual boss of the Wild Ruins. It seems to be controlled by something.]
And beside it—
[Flower Demon King (Boss)]
[Level: 10]
[Combat Power: 3,000]
[Details: A flower that spreads its fragrance to control others and use them to fight.]
"So that’s how it is," Leon muttered.
The [Ruins Guardian] was being controlled by the [Flower Demon King].
That alone proved how dangerous the flower truly was.
And yet... Leon’s expression didn’t change.
The [Flower Demon King] looked powerful. Its combat power, abilities, and presence all screamed "final boss."
But Leon knew better.
"It’s not the real one."
After all, it lacked the [Zone Boss] title. Leon shifted his gaze past the two bosses.
And there, sitting calmly on a throne woven entirely from living vines was the true ruler of the [Wild Forest]. The figure slowly leaned forward.
"A human has reached this place," it said calmly. "Very well."
Leon’s eyes narrowed as he read the panel that appeared.
[Wild Forest King (Zone Boss)]
[Level: 10]
[Talent: Constitution Enhancement (F-Level), Strength Enhancement (F-Level)]
[Combat Power: 4,000]
[Details: The strongest monster in the Wild Forest, ruler over all others.]
"As expected," Leon nodded. "This boss only exists on [Hard] difficulty."
Instead of fear, a smile spread across his face.
Even though the [Wild Forest King] was the strongest monster in the zone... Leon’s combat power was already higher than that.
Three bosses. Three massive loot drops. Leon tightened his grip on his sword and staff.
"I’m taking all of it."

"A human has reached this place," it said calmly.
"Very well."
Leon’s eyes narrowed as he read the panel that appeared.
[Wild Forest King (Zone Boss)]
[Level: 10]
[Talent: Constitution Enhancement (F-Level), Strength Enhancement (F-Level)]
[Combat Power: 4,000]
[Details: The strongest monster in the Wild Forest, ruler over all others.]
"As expected," Leon nodded.
"This boss only exists on [Hard] difficulty."
Instead of fear, a smile spread across his face.
Even though the [Wild Forest King] was the strongest monster in the zone...
Leon’s combat power was already higher than that.
Three bosses.
Three massive loot drops.
Leon tightened his grip on his sword and staff.
"I’m taking all of it."

chapters.title: Chapter 23: 4000 Combat Power, Wild Forest King
paragraphs: "It has been a while," the Wild Forest King said calmly, his voice echoing through the clearing. "Among all races, only a handful ever dare to come here. And those who do almost always die. You will join them as well."
There was a reason those words carried such weight.

At this stage, a combat power of 4,000 was terrifying. It was far beyond what any normal level 10 being should possess. In fact, for most players, even reaching half of that number would already be considered monstrous.
And yet—
[Combat Power: 1,620 (+2,520)]
Leon glanced at his own status panel, then lifted his head.
A faint grin formed on his lips as he raised his staff and pointed it forward without hesitation.
The Wild Forest King stood at roughly two meters tall. His body was humanoid, but his head was unmistakably that of a serpent, scales glinting faintly beneath the filtered forest light.
A long sword rested in his hands, its blade polished and sharp, and an oppressive aura radiated from him without restraint.
He did not rise from his throne of twisted vines.

To him, Leon was simply another challenger who had managed to make it this far. Most of the intruders who reached this clearing couldn’t even defeat the [Ruin Guardian] and the [Flower Demon King]. There was no reason for him to move yet.
Fwoosh!
The Flower Demon King shifted its massive body slightly. Its enormous petals trembled as a thick pink fragrance spread through the air, rolling forward like a visible mist.
The scent filled the clearing in an instant, surrounding Leon completely.
This was its true power.
Anyone caught by that fragrance would lose themselves, their mind eroded until nothing remained but obedience.
Once controlled, escape was impossible. They would become a puppet for the rest of their life.
And yet, Leon did not react at all.
The fragrance washed over him, seeped into the air around him, and then... nothing happened.
The Flower Demon King froze.
Even the Wild Forest King narrowed his eyes slightly from atop his throne.
"Your combat power," the king muttered slowly, finally focusing fully on Leon. "It is—"
Strong Fireball!
Leon did not give him the chance to finish.
Spirit surged through his staff as he released a fully condensed fireball. The level 5 spell flew forward in a blazing arc and slammed directly into the Flower Demon King’s massive body.
BOOM!
The explosion was violent. Flames engulfed the flower in an instant, charring its petals black and tearing through its core.
There was no resistance. No struggle. The overwhelming difference in combat power made everything else meaningless.
The Flower Demon King, a boss capable of enslaving others with ease, was annihilated in a single attack.
Its massive body collapsed into ash.
As soon as it died, the [Ruin Guardian] trembled violently. The control binding it vanished, and clarity returned to it.
The moment it registered what had happened, fear overwhelmed it completely.
Its first instinct was to run. How could it fight a human who had just erased the very being that controlled it?
"Useless."
The Wild Forest King finally moved.
He rose from his throne in a single smooth motion and slashed his blade forward without even looking at the guardian.
The sword flashed.
BOOM!
The [Ruin Guardian] shattered instantly, its body breaking apart before it could even take a step.
"Just stay down."
Leon wasn’t surprised by the king’s ability to speak.
In his past life, he had long grown used to the fact that truly powerful bosses possessed intelligence, awareness, and even language. That didn’t change the outcome. A fight was still inevitable.
Fwish!
The Wild Forest King vanished from his original position and reappeared in front of Leon, silver blade cutting through the air in a wide arc.
Leon raised his own sword and met the strike head-on.
Clang!
Their blades collided, neither yielding.
BOOM!
The shockwave from the impact surged outward, slicing through the surrounding trees. Thick trunks were cut cleanly in half, crashing to the ground behind them.

"Hah," the king said, his snake-like head shifting slightly as his gaze locked onto Leon. "I can tell immediately. You’re the strongest person who has ever come here... from a low-level world that is."
That statement carried weight.
Dungeons like this one existed across all of [Eternal Ascension]. Every novice village had its own version of the [Wild Ruins].
Which meant that this king had fought thousands upon thousands of challengers, humans, beasts, and races Leon had never even heard of.
And yet, none of them compared to the human standing before him now.
Leon did not respond.
Slash!
The Wild Forest King pressed forward, unleashing a series of rapid, powerful strikes. Each slash was precise, heavy, and meant to kill. The pressure was immense.
Leon met every single attack.
His movements were calm, deliberate, and refined by experience. He didn’t retreat. He didn’t panic. Each time the blade came toward him, he responded perfectly.
Even someone with equal combat power would normally falter under such relentless pressure.
But the king couldn’t find a single opening.
"And yet you carry a staff," the king said while attacking, his tone tinged with curiosity. "How strange. I have never seen a swordsman who fights with magic."
Leon already knew his path was unusual.
A swordsman who wielded magic, a mage who refused to abandon close combat—it was a difficult and unforgiving route. But it was the path he had chosen in his past life.
And this time, he was walking it far better.
Leon stepped back, narrowly dodging a downward slash, then raised his staff.
Lightning Strike! Strong Fireball!
A bolt of lightning shot toward the king. The Wild Forest King twisted his body and dodged it with ease, but in doing so, he exposed himself.
"Oh."
BOOM!
The fireball slammed directly into the position he had moved to, detonating violently and sending him flying backward.
His body crashed against the vine-covered throne, shattering parts of it on impact.
"Haha..." The king rose slowly, his body clearly damaged, scales scorched and cracked. "I see now... you are one of them.
Leon tilted his head slightly but didn’t dwell on the words. He tightened his grip on his sword and prepared to continue.
Vision Enhancement!
Spirit flowed through his eyes. The world sharpened instantly. Movements became clearer, slower, easier to track.
And then—
"The culmination of my strength," the king said, his eyes gleaming as he lowered his sword to his side. Power gathered around him in waves. "You die with me."
Leon’s eyes widened. He didn’t hesitate.
He rushed forward at full speed, closing the distance in an instant.
But just as he was about to reach him—
Crescent Slash!
The Wild Forest King swung his blade with everything he had. Power erupted outward, forming a massive crescent-shaped slash that tore through the air.
Leon reacted instantly. He swung his sword vertically, pouring all his strength into the block.
The impact was overwhelming.
The force hurled him backward several meters, his feet carving lines into the ground as he struggled to hold his stance.
And then—
SLASH!
The crescent cut through his blade. It struck Leon directly.
"HAH!" the Wild Forest King laughed, convinced of his victory. "An insect will always remain an insect. Especially a human from a low-level world."
He believed the fight was over.
But then—
"I’ll be taking that skill of yours."
The voice came from behind him. The king’s eyes widened.
A blade flashed and his head fell.
Leon stood behind the collapsing corpse, breathing heavily.
"Phew."
He looked down at the body of the [Wild Forest King].
The reason he survived was simple: the [Purple Jade Necklace] had activated its passive ability, forming a shield that absorbed the fatal blow.
Without that initial resistance, he would have died instantly though.
Ding!
[You have killed "Flower Demon King (Boss)" and gained 1,000 experience points.]
[You have killed "Wild Forest King (Zone Boss)" and gained 3,000 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered, items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
It was unfortunate that the Wild Forest King had destroyed the [Ruin Guardian], costing Leon its loot.
But Leon didn’t linger on that thought.
Without wasting a second, he opened his [Storage Space], eyes fixed on what the two bosses had left behind.

chapters.title: Chapter 24: Clearing the Hard-Difficulty Wild Ruins, Wild Forest Crown
paragraphs: The moment Leon opened his [Storage Space], a loud announcement echoed, not just in [Novice Village #1], but across every single novice village without exception.
[Congratulations to Leon Rykard for clearing the Hard difficulty "Wild Ruins".]
The message appeared simultaneously before countless players.
"What?"
"Holy shit... which novice village is that guy from?"
"Damn..."
Confusion, shock, disbelief, reactions erupted everywhere.
This was the first time such an announcement had ever appeared since the start of [Eternal Ascension].
Not a single player had even discovered the [Wild Ruins], yet this Leon guy cleared it already?
But while many villages buzzed with shock and awe, [Novice Village #5] reacted very differently.
"This little fuck!" Damon roared, slamming his fist down. "Our village is still stuck with that experience and resource penalty, and he’s already soaring ahead like this?!"
"We can still kill monsters just fine," Maki replied after a brief pause, her tone far calmer. "But maybe it’s time we stop messing around and actually focus on getting stronger."
"I know," Damon growled, clenching his teeth. "But now I’m sure of one thing. That bastard isn’t some random nobody like the others."
The announcement burned into his mind: Leon Rykard.
Damon and Maki exchanged a brief look. Neither of them spoke again, but neither was thinking of backing down. It didn’t matter how far Leon pulled ahead.
Eventually, they would catch up. Eventually, they would settle things.
Meanwhile, back in the depths of the [Wild Ruins], a different panel appeared before Leon. This one wasn’t global. It was his alone.
[Since you are the first to conquer this dungeon in its Hard difficulty, you have been rewarded with 20 Reputation Points.]
"Damn..."
Leon stared at the number, genuinely surprised. Twenty reputation points was an enormous reward, especially at this stage.
His gaze immediately shifted to his status.
[Reputation Points: 40]
"Hah," he muttered, unable to hide his satisfaction. "Only ten more, and I’ll get my first reward."
In his past life, Leon had never heard of any human reaching fifty reputation points before their first assessment at the [Novice Divine Temple].
Most players barely scraped together a handful by then.
He didn’t know exactly how much this would influence his future rewards, but one thing was certain: it wouldn’t hurt.
Then his eyes dropped to another line.
"Damn... I’m really close."
He needed barely any experience now. One or two decent monsters, and he’d level up. Once he reached level 10, he would be forced to advance to the next stage of [Eternal Ascension].
Before worrying about that, though, Leon refocused his attention on his [Storage Space].
[Eternal Coins x500]
[Flower Demon King Essence: Consuming will increase Constitution by 10 and Spirit by 15.]
[Wild Forest King Essence: Consuming will increase Strength by 30, Agility by 20, and Constitution by 15.]
[Skill Stones x6]
[Enhancement Stones x5]
[Wild Forest Sword (Epic): +250 Attack, +200 Strength. Requirement: Level 10.]
[Crescent Slash (Skill Book). Requirement: Level 10.]
[Sub-Talent Scrolls: Constitution Enhancement (F-Level) and Strength Enhancement (F-Level)]
[Wild Forest Crown (Epic): All attributes +100. Requirement: Conquer the "Wild Ruins" in "Hard" difficulty.]
"...Damn."
Even Leon had to admit it. The loot was insane.
Most of it clearly came from the [Wild Forest King], but that was to be expected. Zone bosses always dropped items far beyond normal standards.
Without wasting time, Leon consumed both essences. As the energy flowed into his body, he felt a clear and immediate change.

His muscles tightened slightly, his breathing steadied, and his spirit pool expanded. The stronger the monster, the greater the benefit from its essence, and these two had been among the strongest possible at this level.
Normally, players barely ever obtained monster essences. The drop rate was absurdly low.
Leon, however, was an exception.
After that, he checked his stones and merged them with what he already had.
[Skill Stones x14]
[Enhancement Stones x11]
"Nice."
With that amount, he could evolve multiple skills or reinforce several pieces of equipment once he found the right opportunity.
His gaze lingered briefly on the [Wild Forest Sword] and the [Crescent Slash] skill book. He wanted to equip and learn them immediately, but the level requirement stopped him short.
It wouldn’t take long to reach level 10, but rules were rules. For now, he stored them away.
Next, Leon picked up the [Wild Forest Crown].
He placed it on his head without hesitation.
The crown was woven entirely from thick vines, interlaced with small, living flowers that pulsed faintly with energy.
It didn’t feel heavy at all, but the moment he equipped it, power surged through his body.
The requirement was unusual. Instead of a level restriction, it demanded proof: conquering the [Wild Ruins] on [Hard] difficulty.
That condition alone made the item nearly impossible to sell. The number of people capable of meeting it was small, even across all races.
Leon felt the effect instantly. All attributes increased by one hundred.
That single item boosted his combat power by roughly eight hundred points in one go. It was absurd.
Finally, Leon turned his attention to the two sub-talent scrolls.
He already possessed [Constitution Enhancement], so he didn’t hesitate to learn the one he lacked.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have learned the F-Level Sub-Talent: "Strength Enhancement".]
[Strength Enhancement (F-Level): Permanently increases Strength by 10%.]
It functioned exactly as expected, mirroring [Constitution Enhancement] but affecting strength instead. Leon nodded in satisfaction.
Then his gaze fell to the remaining scroll in his hand.
Another player would have learned it immediately without thinking twice. But Leon already had that sub-talent.
Did that make the scroll useless? Not at all.
Sub-talents followed the same underlying rules as items. They could be fused.
Unlike equipment, however, a failed fusion wouldn’t destroy the existing sub-talent. Only the scroll itself would break.
Leon focused his mana, tore the scroll apart, and let the fragments dissolve into his body.
The energy merged with his existing sub-talent.
Ding!
[Fusion successful.]
[You have evolved "Constitution Enhancement (F-Level)" to "Constitution Enhancement (E-Level).]
[Constitution Enhancement (E-Level): Permanently increases Constitution by 20%.]
"Nice."
This improvement would scale even harder as his base attributes increased. It was a long-term benefit, and one that most players wouldn’t even consider possible this early.
’I wonder how far I can evolve it,’ Leon thought, a grin tugging at his lips. ’I’ll need more sub-talent scrolls for that, though.’
As that thought crossed his mind, a portal formed in front of the shattered throne. Its surface shimmered faintly.
It was the exit. Without hesitation, Leon stepped forward and left the [Wild Ruins].
Ding!
A few seconds later, he emerged outside the massive ruin structure, standing once again in the original [Wild Forest].
The air felt lighter here. Familiar.
"I’ll kill a few more monsters and move on," Leon said quietly, nodding to himself.
But before that, he wanted to meet David, Eleonore, and the others at least one more time.

Ding!
A few seconds later, he emerged outside the massive ruin structure, standing once again in the original [Wild Forest].
The air felt lighter here.
Familiar.
"I’ll kill a few more monsters and move on," Leon said quietly, nodding to himself.
But before that, he wanted to meet David, Eleonore, and the others at least one more time.

chapters.title: Chapter 25: Reaching Level 10, Fifty Reputation Points
paragraphs: Fwoosh!
Leon sprinted through the [Wild Forest], moving at full speed as he searched for Eleonore, David, Aaron, and Alice.
Now that he had almost reached level 10, he knew his time in the novice phase was coming to an end.
Once he entered the [Novice Divine Temple] and completed his first assessment, the real [Eternal Ascension] would begin.
After that, there was no guarantee he would see them again anytime soon.
At the very least, he wanted to say a few things before leaving.
The forest blurred around him as he ran. None of the monsters roaming the area could even begin to keep up with his pace.
Leon’s agility had long since surpassed what monsters at this level could handle, and even those that noticed him barely had time to react before he was already gone.
And honestly, even if they managed to attack, it wouldn’t matter much.
With [Constitution Enhancement], his upgraded equipment, and the bonuses from essences and the crown, his constitution had climbed past 700.
That was an absurd value at this stage. Even level 10 monsters would need to land multiple solid hits just to injure him, and most wouldn’t survive long enough to try.
Fear simply didn’t exist for him anymore in this forest.
After pushing forward for a while, Leon slowed slightly as he entered the level 6-7 area.
Based on their pace and strength, this was roughly where Eleonore’s group should be by now.
They were competent. Stronger than most. Their talents alone put them well above the average novice.
A few moments later, Leon felt it. Presences. Not monsters.
Fwish!
He dashed forward and emerged into a small clearing, where a familiar scene greeted him.
The four of them were sitting around a crude campsite, a pile of raw meat set aside, and a campfire that... wasn’t actually lit.
"How are we even supposed to cook this if we don’t have fire?" Aaron complained loudly, holding a slab of meat with clear frustration. "This is so dumb."
"Just eat it raw," David replied flatly, already biting into a piece of [Howler Wolf Meat]. "Like a man."
Aaron stared at him for half a second, then recoiled as he noticed David’s expression twist.
"Yeah, no. That’s disgusting. This is really bad."
"We need some kind of fire-related skill," Eleonore said thoughtfully. "Maybe I should try to get [Fire Arrows] or something similar."
"The drop rate is terrible," Alice sighed, leaning back. "And I’m honestly starting to starve."
Leon watched the scene for a brief moment, amused. It looked exactly like what it was, a group of capable players completely defeated by something as simple as cooking.
Then he stepped forward.
"Huh?" David turned his head first. "Damn. How do you always manage to find us?"
"Luck," Leon replied with a grin. "I am lucky, after all."
"With the amount of items you keep pulling out of nowhere?" Aaron laughed. "Yeah, I’d say that checks out."
Leon walked over and sat down near the campfire, settling beside Eleonore. Without ceremony, he raised his staff and focused his spirit.
Fwoosh!

A small, controlled flame bloomed at the center of the campfire, formed from the condensed heat of his [Strong Fireball]. It wasn’t violent or explosive, just a steady, clean flame, perfect for cooking.
The mood around the campsite instantly shifted.
"...You’re kidding me," Aaron muttered.
Leon casually pulled out a piece of [Roasted Ape Meat] from his storage and took a bite, clearly enjoying himself.
"You’re level 9 already," David said, glancing at the leaderboard. "That’s insane."
"It’s not that special," Leon replied calmly. "But I won’t be staying much longer."
"Where are you going?" Aaron asked before stopping himself.
"To another place," Eleonore answered instead, looking at Leon. "We do need to reach level 10. There has to be something after that."
Leon nodded. "Exactly."
He continued eating as he spoke, his tone relaxed but serious.
"I won’t stay long. I just wanted to tell you to be careful later on. Especially during your first assessment. And even more once you step onto the [Eternal Continent]."
Eleonore narrowed her eyes slightly. "How do you even know about all that?"
Leon didn’t hesitate. "Reward for clearing the [Wild Ruins]."
"Oh." She paused, then nodded. "That... actually makes sense."
Leon shared what information he could about the [Wild Ruins], avoiding anything that would raise suspicion.
He spoke with them for a few more minutes as they cooked their food properly this time, the earlier tension replaced by a calmer atmosphere.
Eventually, Leon stood up.
"I’ll be going," he said simply. "See you later. If we all survive."
They nodded in response. But just before he turned away, Leon added something else.
"You can all send me friend requests," he said. "I’ll accept them."
Ding! Ding! Ding! Ding!
Four notifications appeared in quick succession.
[You have received a friend request from "Eleonore Starlight"]
[You have received a friend request from "David Windbreak"]
[You have received a friend request from "Aaron Godfield"]
[You have received a friend request from "Alice Evicton"]
Leon accepted them all without hesitation. His friend list updated immediately, giving him a way to contact them.
"Oh, and take this."
He gave the [Dark Shell Shield +2] to Aaron.
"Damn, let me send you something!"
Ding!
[You have received 30 Eternal Coins from "Aaron Godfield"]
"Good enough," Leon nodded.
After that, they parted ways.
Leon pushed deeper into the forest, heading back toward the level 9-10 area.
Before long, he encountered a few wandering monsters.
Slash!
One clean swing of his sword was enough. The monster fell instantly.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 10!]
[You have gained 5 points in all attributes and 5 free points to distribute.]
Leon barely had time to register it before another panel appeared.
Ding!
[You have reached Level 10. Your experience will now be locked until you complete your first assessment.]
[You will be teleported to the "Novice Divine Temple" in five minutes for your first assessment. Take this time to prepare.]
Leon stared at the panel, expression neutral. This was expected.
But now that he had officially reached level 10, several things became possible.
Ding!
[Congratulations to Leon Rykard for being the first human to reach Level 10.]
Ding!
[Since you are the first person to reach Level 10, you have been rewarded with 10 Reputation Points and a Legendary Treasure Chest.]
Leon exhaled slowly. "Good."
This was exactly what he wanted. And the system wasn’t done yet.
Ding!
[Your reputation has reached 50.]
[You have received the "Heavenly One’s Favored" blessing. You will now gain 20 attributes per level.]
"...Wait a minute."
Leon’s eyes widened as he read the panel again.
"That’s way more than in my past life."
Reputation points existed to enhance growth, better level-up rewards, better long-term benefits.
But this was far beyond what he remembered. Either the thresholds had changed... or being the first to reach this milestone amplified the reward.
Either way, it didn’t matter. From now on, every level would make him absurdly stronger.
Beep!
[Warning: Four minutes remaining before teleportation to the "Novice Divine Temple".]
"Gotta be quick," Leon muttered.
He pulled out the [Legendary Treasure Chest]. It materialized in front of him, radiating a golden glow that stood out sharply against the forest.
Even in his past life, legendary chests were extremely rare. Most players never saw one at all.
Leon didn’t hesitate. He opened it.
Ding!
[100% Drop Rate has triggered. All items inside the treasure chest have been placed into storage space.]
Leon immediately opened his [Storage Space], eager to inspect it one last time before leaving the novice phase behind.

chapters.title: Chapter 26: Legendary Treasure Chest Items, Using Everything!
paragraphs: Leon quickly checked the new items resting in his inventory the moment the [Legendary Treasure Chest] finished opening.
His heart was still beating faster than normal. Even now, it felt unreal.
Without wasting time, he first pulled out the three [Howler Wolf Essences] he had been saving.
Those monsters were the very reason he had managed to reach level 10 in the first place, and there was no reason to hold back anymore.
Leon consumed all three of them one after another.

A familiar warmth spread through his body as the energy dissolved into him, reinforcing his stats and stabilizing his growth. Compared to everything else he was about to deal with, this part felt routine.
Once that was done, Leon finally turned his attention to the true prize. The chest items.
And the moment he looked at the list, his eyes widened.
There were far more items than he had ever seen come out of a single chest before.
[Gold Shield (Legendary): +500 Defense, 250 Constitution. Forms a protectiove armor outside the body, able to withstand some attacks. Requirement: 300 Constitution and Level 10.]
[Sub-Talent Scroll: Strength Enhancement (F-Level).]
[Skill Stones x10]
[Enhancement Stones x10]
[Silk Belt (Epic): +250 Defense, +100 Constitution, +150 Agility. Requirement: Level 10.]
[Healing Potion x3: May fully heal injuries.]
[Vine Bow (Legendary): +500 Attack, +300 Strength, +250 Agility. Has a chance to fire "Vine Arrows" that can restrict enemies. Requirement: At least one archer-type skill and Level 10.]
[Divine Elven Essence (Legendary): A rare essence left by high elves, consuming will increase all attributes by 100 and enhance bloodline.]
[Intermediate All-Attributes Pill: Increases all attributes by 50.]
"...DAMN!"
The word slipped out before Leon could stop himself.
In his past life, he had opened plenty of treasure chests. Some were good. Some were disappointing. A few were memorable.
But never had he seen something like this.
This wasn’t just generous. It was absurd.
Usually, the rank of a chest didn’t only affect the quality of the items inside. It also influenced how many items you could get in the first place. Treasure chests followed strict rules.
At minimum, a chest would always give one or two items. That part was guaranteed.
Everything beyond that depended on luck.
The higher the rank, the higher the odds of additional drops, but even then, it was rare to see more than four or five items at once.
Legendary chests were different.
They didn’t just improve quality. They increased guaranteed rewards too.
That was why they were so coveted. And also why they were so rare.
Leon slowly exhaled, forcing himself to calm down. Getting excited wouldn’t help him organize this mess.
He began sorting the items in his mind, separating what he needed immediately from what could wait.
First priority: anything consumable, that could strengthen him right now.
That narrowed it down to two items.
The [Divine Elven Essence]. And the [Intermediate All-Attributes Pill].
Leon paused for a brief moment, his thoughts drifting to a familiar face: Emilia.
The elf he had saved earlier, back when she had been poisoned in that cave.
If she were here... what would she think about this?
High elves weren’t just a myth or a title in [Eternal Ascension]. They were an actual race, with pride, history, and power behind them.
What would they think if they saw a human casually drinking something derived from them?
Leon shook his head. That wasn’t his problem right now.
Strength was strength. He picked up the [Intermediate All-Attributes Pill] first.
Without hesitation, he swallowed it.
Ding!
[You have consumed the "Intermediate All-Attributes Pill" and all your attributes have increased by 50.]
The change was immediate but subtle. His body felt more balanced, more stable, like everything had shifted into better alignment.
Satisfied, Leon reached for the second item. The [Divine Elven Essence].
It came in a small bottle, no bigger than his thumb. The liquid inside shimmered with a soft golden glow, almost alive.
Just looking at it made his instincts stir.
Leon didn’t hesitate. He drank it. The effect was instant.
Power surged through his veins like a tidal wave. His senses sharpened, his body hummed, and for a brief moment it felt like his entire being was being washed clean from the inside out.
He had never experienced anything like this. It was... incredible.
Ding!
[Your bloodline bas been purified by 1% by the Divine Elven Essence, all your attributes have increased by 100 as a result.]
[You have absorbed a trace of Elven Power, but the concentration is too low to inherit any skills.]
"Huh."
Leon blinked. That last message caught his attention.
Absorbed a trace of Elven Power? Too low to inherit any skills?
His mind immediately started working.
Did that mean if he obtained more of these... he could actually gain elven-related abilities?
The thought alone made his heart beat faster.
The [Divine Elven Essence] was probably one of those absurdly rare items, the kind with a drop rate so low most players would never even see it mentioned.
A 0.001% chance, maybe even lower. No wonder it was so powerful.
Leon forced himself to move on before he got lost in speculation.
Next came the sub-talent scroll.
He attempted to fuse the [Strength Enhancement] scroll with the sub-talent he already possessed.
Beep!
[Fusion failed.]
"...Damn."
Leon sighed, but he wasn’t too bothered.
Failure was always a possibility with these things. At least his existing sub-talent hadn’t degraded.
That alone was a win.
With consumables out of the way, Leon moved on to equipment.
He equipped the [Silk Belt (Epic)] first.
The moment it settled around his waist, he felt lighter and sturdier at the same time. His movements became smoother, more controlled.
Then he equipped the [Wild Forest Sword (Epic)].
The familiar weight of the blade rested comfortably in his hand, perfectly balanced.
Finally, Leon pulled out the [Crescent Slash] skill book.
He poured mana into it, letting the knowledge flow directly into his mind.
Ding!
[You have learned "Crescent Slash"]
[Crescent Slash (Epic-Tier Level 1): Charge your power into your sword before slashing forward, releasing a powerful crescent slash.]
"Nice."
Leon smiled.
He really wanted to test it immediately, to feel how it differed from his other attacks.
But when he checked the timer, he stopped himself. Only two minutes left before teleportation.
There wasn’t enough time to experiment.
As for the [Gold Shield (Legendary)] and the [Vine Bow (Legendary)], Leon already had people in mind: Aaron and Eleonore.
Both items suited them perfectly. Still, he didn’t give them away. Not yet.
These items were valuable, far too valuable to hand over without thought.
And even if he did, neither of them met the requirements yet.
’I could also sell them to the other races...’ Leon thought. ’I’ll be meeting them soon.’
That option stayed in the back of his mind.
With equipment handled, Leon moved on to the last part of his preparation: the stones.
[Skill Stones x24]
[Enhancement Stones x21]
Seeing those numbers alone was enough to lift his mood.
With this many, he could make real progress.
He quickly decided how to use the skill stones.
Ding!
[You have upgraded "Appraisal (Level 3)" to "Appraisal (Level 4)"]
[You have upgraded "Strong Fireball (Level 5)" to "Powerful Fireball (Level 6)"]
[You have upgraded "Lightning Strike (Level 2)" to "Lightning Strike (Level 3)"]
[You have upgraded "Crescent Slash (Level 1)" to "Crescent Slash (Level 2)"]
Four upgrades. Every single skill stone was gone.
Leon let out a slow breath. It was worth it. Especially his fireball.
It had changed names again. That alone showed how much stronger it had become.
Leon quickly checked the updated descriptions. Only two of them had changed.
[Appraisal (Level 4): Can be used to appraise monsters, item information, terrains, special materials and ores.]
For blacksmiths or alchemists, this ability would be priceless, especially this early in the game.
But Leon didn’t care much about that. For him, Appraisal was a tool.
And he wanted it strong enough to reveal more information than it normally should. That was the real value.
Next came his fireball.
[Powerful Fireball (Level 6): Focus your Spirit and condense it into a powerful fireball that hits several targets in a wide radius, and that has a good chance to "burn" them.]
"Hm."
The radius had increased. The power too.
Leon nodded, satisfied.
Then—
Beep!
[Warning: One minute remaining before teleportation to the "Novice Divine Temple".]
"Shit," Leon muttered. "Gotta be quick."
He immediately turned his attention to his remaining items, fingers flying as he prepared to use his [Enhancement Stones] before time ran out.

He really wanted to test it immediately, to feel how it differed from his other attacks.
But when he checked the timer, he stopped himself.
Only two minutes left before teleportation.
There wasn’t enough time to experiment.
As for the [Gold Shield (Legendary)] and the [Vine Bow (Legendary)], Leon already had people in mind: Aaron and Eleonore.
Both items suited them perfectly.
Still, he didn’t give them away.
Not yet.
These items were valuable, far too valuable to hand over without thought.
And even if he did, neither of them met the requirements yet.
’I could also sell them to the other races...’ Leon thought. ’I’ll be meeting them soon.’
That option stayed in the back of his mind.
With equipment handled, Leon moved on to the last part of his preparation: the stones.
[Skill Stones x24]
[Enhancement Stones x21]
Seeing those numbers alone was enough to lift his mood.
With this many, he could make real progress.
He quickly decided how to use the skill stones.
Ding!
[You have upgraded "Appraisal (Level 3)" to "Appraisal (Level 4)"]
[You have upgraded "Strong Fireball (Level 5)" to "Powerful Fireball (Level 6)"]
[You have upgraded "Lightning Strike (Level 2)" to "Lightning Strike (Level 3)"]
[You have upgraded "Crescent Slash (Level 1)" to "Crescent Slash (Level 2)"]
Four upgrades.
Every single skill stone was gone.
Leon let out a slow breath.
It was worth it.
Especially his fireball.
It had changed names again.
That alone showed how much stronger it had become.
Leon quickly checked the updated descriptions.
Only two of them had changed.
[Appraisal (Level 4): Can be used to appraise monsters, item information, terrains, special materials and ores.]
For blacksmiths or alchemists, this ability would be priceless, especially this early in the game.
But Leon didn’t care much about that.
For him, Appraisal was a tool.
And he wanted it strong enough to reveal more information than it normally should.
That was the real value.
Next came his fireball.
[Powerful Fireball (Level 6): Focus your Spirit and condense it into a powerful fireball that hits several targets in a wide radius, and that has a good chance to "burn" them.]
"Hm."
The radius had increased.
The power too.
Leon nodded, satisfied.
Then—
Beep!
[Warning: One minute remaining before teleportation to the "Novice Divine Temple".]
"Shit," Leon muttered.
"Gotta be quick."
He immediately turned his attention to his remaining items, fingers flying as he prepared to use his [Enhancement Stones] before time ran out.

chapters.title: Chapter 27: The Two Mysterious Figures, Ascending to The Novice Divine Temple
paragraphs: Leon quickly crushed the remaining [Enhancement Stones] in his hand and immediately began using them on his equipment.
There was no time to hesitate.
Ding!
[You have successfully enhanced your "Wild Forest Crown" (7 EC), "Wild Forest Sword" (7 EC) and "Silk Belt" (7 EC)]1
Leon let out a short breath.
Since all three pieces of equipment were epic-rank, their first enhancement each required seven Enhancement Stones.
The cost was high, but the return was always worth it.
He could have chosen to enhance his [Skeleton Staff +3] instead. That option had crossed his mind for a brief moment.
But in the end, Leon decided against it.
Right now, raw attributes mattered more than anything else. The sword, crown, and belt all provided massive stat boosts, especially after enhancement. Compared to that, the staff could wait.
Leon quickly opened the updated item panels.
[Wild Forest Sword +2 (Epic): +400 Attack, +270 Strength.]
[Wild Forest Crown +2 (Epic): All attributes +150.]
[Silk Belt +2 (Epic): +350 Defense, +150 Constitution, +200 Agility.]
"...Damn."
Every single piece had grown noticeably stronger. The increases weren’t minor either.
The crown alone granting +150 to all attributes was ridiculous.
Leon could feel it too. His body felt heavier, sturdier, more refined. His grip on the sword felt firmer, his movements more controlled.
Beep!
[Warning: Ten seconds remaining before teleportation to the "Novice Divine Temple".]
Leon didn’t waste another second.
He immediately opened his status panel, wanting to see everything clearly one last time before being pulled away.
[Name: Leon Rykard]
[Talent: 100% Drop Rate (SSS)]
[Sub-Talents: Constitution Enhancement (E-Level), Strength Enhancement (F-Level).]
[Level: 10 (Locked)]
[Constitution: 424 (+655 + 216)]1
[Skills: Appraisal (Lv.4), Vision Enhancement (Lv.4), Powerful Fireball (Lv.6), Lightning Strike (Lv.3), Crescent Slash (Lv.2)
[Combat Power: 3,264 (+6,032)]
[Free Points to Allocate: 20.]
[Eternal Coins: 3,138]
[Reputation Points: 50]
Leon stared at the numbers for a moment longer than he intended.
His combat power was brushing against ten thousand. That alone was insane.
Even in his past life, even across the many race he had encountered, almost nobody had reached something like this at level 10.
And yet, here he was. Leon clenched his fist slowly.
At that moment, he truly felt it. He was ready.
Then, just as the countdown was about to reach zero, another notification appeared in front of him.
Ding!
[You have received a message from "Eleonore Starlight"]
Leon blinked and opened it.
[Eleonore Starlight: I didn’t get to say it before, but good luck ٩(◕‿◕)۶]
A small smile tugged at the corner of Leon’s lips.
Without hesitation, he typed a response.
[Leon Rykard: See you soon.]
And the instant the message was sent—
BOOM!
A massive beam of blinding light descended from the sky.
The entire [Novice Village #1] shook as if struck by divine force. The pillar of light was so large it could be seen from anywhere within the village.
"H-Holy shit?"
"What the fuck is that thing!?"
"Someone’s ascending already?!"
Players everywhere froze in place, staring at the sky in disbelief.
The beam struck Leon directly, wrapping around his body as if it were lifting him by force.
In the next moment, he was carried upward, his surroundings dissolving into pure light as he ascended to the next stage of [Eternal Ascension].
But just as Leon vanished into the sky, two figures appeared at the spot where he had been standing.
They materialized silently, their forms shrouded in dense mist. Their features were impossible to see, as if reality itself refused to reveal them.
One was tall and broad-shouldered.
The other slimmer, standing with relaxed posture.
"Earth is a low-level world, right?" the male figure spoke, his voice calm but tinged with curiosity. "It’s only been a few hours, and one of them already ascended?"
"I guess so," the woman replied with a shrug. "But do you really think he has what it takes to survive the rest?"
The man rubbed his chin thoughtfully.
"Nah."
"As I thought," the woman smiled faintly. "Still, I wonder why the [Heavenly One] placed so much importance on this particular person."
"We’re not meant to understand his intentions," the man replied. "Better to focus on what we were asked to do."
"True," the woman said softly. "All we can do now is hope things go well. Not just for us, but for everything."
The man nodded.
"All the pieces are set. Now it’s time to see what happens. Everyone’s been waiting for this."
As soon as the conversation ended, both figures dissolved into faint, dark particles.
The mist lingering around the area dispersed, leaving no trace of their presence behind.
Ding!
[You are the first person from Earth to reach the "Novice Divine Temple", you have been rewarded with 25 Reputation Points.]
Ding!
[You have arrived at the "Novice Divine Temple"]
[Please enter the temple to begin your assessment, you may also reset inside if you want to.]
Leon opened his eyes. Clouds surrounded him.
He was standing on them, his feet pressing against a solid surface that felt no different from stone.
Before him stood a colossal structure.
A massive temple floated in the sky, its scale so overwhelming it made everything else seem insignificant.
Above the enormous gate at the front, glowing letters were engraved into the structure itself: Novice Divine Temple.
This place hovered above the clouds, unreachable by any normal means. It was the first true checkpoint for anyone who advanced beyond the novice stage.
"Seeing this again after so long..." Leon muttered, a grin forming on his face. "Incredible."
There were other Divine Temples for later assessments, each with its own atmosphere and rules.
But this one... This was where it all began.
Leon took a quiet breath and walked forward.
The moment he reached the entrance, the massive gate opened on its own, revealing a long corridor stretching inward.
He stepped inside without hesitation. The corridor was breathtaking.
Walls made of white jade rose hundreds of feet high on both sides, engraved with countless patterns.
Figures of various beings, some humanoid, some monstrous, some divine, were carved into the surface with impossible detail.
The entire place radiated majesty. At the end of the corridor stood another massive gate.
Leon walked until he reached it, then passed through. He entered a vast hall.
Ding!
[Killing is forbidden in here, any violators will be obliterated.]
Leon barely glanced at the message. He had no intention of fighting.
But the moment he stepped inside, he felt it. Thousands of gazes turned toward him at once.
"Someone new arrived once more."
"That race... I’ve never seen it before."
"It’s a human, though the ones I met weren’t from this low-level world."
"I see... Earth. A low-level world."
Leon remained calm. He didn’t react.
The hall was massive, filled with countless individuals gathered together. Every corner was occupied.
And yet, not a single one of them was human.
There were beings with wolf heads and humanoid bodies. Elves with glowing eyes. Demons with horns and wings.
Creatures with octopus-like limbs. Others with deep blue skin or crystalline features.
Races from countless worlds were gathered here in the [Novice Divine Temple].
Leon could see it clearly in their eyes: arrogance.
To them, someone from a low-level world couldn’t possibly stand on the same footing.
Leon didn’t care. Nobody could fight here anyway.
[Eternal Ascension] classified worlds into four ranks: Low, Intermediate, High, and Eternal.
No one knew exactly how the ranking system worked.
But Leon knew one thing: power decided everything.
Some of the races here possessed terrifying innate abilities.
Even so, Leon remained unfazed.
As he calmly observed his surroundings, a voice suddenly rang out behind him.
"No way..." a feminine voice said, filled with shock. "It’s you?!"
Leon turned around. Standing right in front of him was Emilia Verdant. The elf.
The very same one he had saved from poison back in that cave.
"Oh."
That was all Leon managed to say. For the first time since arriving, he was genuinely surprised.

chapters.title: Chapter 28: Divine Stele, S-Rank Evaluation
paragraphs: Emilia had died in Leon’s past life.
Because of that, seeing her standing here, alive, breathing, and looking at him with wide eyes, was extremely strange.
Back then, he hadn’t been strong enough. He hadn’t been fast enough. He had arrived too late, and by the time he learned of her fate, there was nothing he could do about it.
And now she was here. Alive.
Standing inside the [Novice Divine Temple], having already reached level 10.
What made it even stranger was the fact that Emilia recognized him instantly.
Leon was used to cold looks. Arrogant gazes. Indifference.
Especially here, where races from higher-level worlds naturally looked down on those from weaker ones.
Yet Emilia hadn’t hesitated for even a second. She had seen him and immediately called out.
Leon quickly opened his [Appraisal], directing it toward her without any hesitation.
The panel that appeared was different than usual.
[Name: Emilia Verdant]
[Level: 10]
[World: Verdia (High-Level)]
As one might expect, every individual or group in this hall was from a different world.
People from higher-level worlds had more restrictions placed on how much information others could see. Especially at this stage.
Verdia. A high-level world. That explained a lot.
Leon glanced around the hall while Emilia was still processing the shock of seeing him.
Nearly everyone present was from a different world.
Leon even took the time to observe some of those displayed, though the majority were from intermediate to high-level worlds.
One important thing Leon already knew, but many newcomers didn’t, was that this hall wasn’t temporary.
People could stay here as long as they wanted.
Only after completing their first assessment would they be allowed to leave the [Novice Divine Temple] and move on to the next domain of [Eternal Ascension].
"I’m... surprised," Emilia finally said as she stepped closer to him. "I really thought we wouldn’t meet again for a while."
Leon shrugged lightly.
"Fate’s strange," he replied. "At least you’re safe."
Emilia let out a small laugh.
"Yeah," she said, though there was something sharp behind it. "The ones who tried to kill me already moved on to the next domain. I didn’t find them in my novice village."
Leon’s expression didn’t change, but his thoughts shifted immediately.
In his past life, those people had succeeded, as Emilia had arrived in his novice village and died.
This time, Leon had intervened. He had changed the outcome.
But the people behind it were still out there. And now they were ahead.
"Did you go through your assessment yet?" Leon asked, already aware of how this whole thing works.
"No," Emilia shook her head. "I’m still trying to understand how this place works. And... I want to prepare first. Just in case."
Leon nodded. That was the smart move.
The first assessment was always done solo.
Once you entered, it was just you and the trial.
Because of that, support-focused individuals were naturally at a disadvantage.
People like Alice, for example, would struggle far more than front-line fighters.
"Let’s move," Leon said simply, already turning around.
Emilia hesitated for half a second, then followed him, her bow resting against her side.
As they walked together, Leon could feel eyes on them.
A human and an elf. Side by side. That alone drew attention.
Some gazes were curious. Others were disdainful. A few were openly mocking.
Leon ignored all of it. Eventually, they reached the center of the hall.
There, standing tall and unmoving, was a massive divine stele.
Its surface looked like smooth stone, yet light constantly flowed beneath it, as if something alive existed inside.
A person stood before it now, their palm pressed against the surface.
Others had gathered around, watching closely.
After a few seconds—
Ding!
[C-Rank.]
A panel appeared above the stele. Immediately, voices erupted.
"Hah, only C-Rank?"
"I mean, that’s still decent. Only around twenty percent of people can even complete that."
"Yeah, but the rewards won’t be that great."
"What are you talking about? Don’t you need at least 4,000 Combat Power just to qualify for a C-Rank assessment?"
"Well, I’ve got over 6,000, so I’m aiming for B-Rank."
Leon listened quietly. This was the [Divine Stele].
Its purpose was simple: it evaluated an individual and determined the highest-rank assessment they were allowed to attempt.
The ranks went from F all the way to S.
The higher the rank, the harder the assessment. And the better the rewards.
It was said that even among high-level worlds, very few people could clear an A-Rank assessment.
As for S-Rank... Those were legends.
Only people from Eternal-level worlds were even qualified.
And even then, completion rates were abysmal.
Failure didn’t mean death, at least not immediately.
If you failed an assessment, you were downgraded to the rank below and forced to attempt that one instead.
For example, if that person failed their C-Rank assessment, they would have to go through a D-Rank one and so on.
But if you failed an F-Rank assessment... You were obliterated.
Deemed too weak to continue existing in [Eternal Ascension].
In his past life, Leon had only qualified for a D-Rank assessment.
He barely survived it. The rewards were mediocre at best. This time was different.
"My turn," Leon said, stepping forward with a faint grin.
As he approached the stele, whispers followed.
"A human..."
"I’ve heard of them. Weak race."
"I met some from an intermediate-level world before, but this one’s from a low-level world."
"E-Rank should be more than enough for him."
Emilia watched quietly from behind, her gaze fixed on Leon.
She didn’t say anything. She just waited.
Leon placed his palm against the divine stele.
For a brief moment, nothing happened.
Then—
Fwoosh!
A blinding light exploded outward, flooding the entire hall.
People cried out in surprise, shielding their eyes. The stele vibrated violently.
BOOM!
A massive panel appeared above it.
[S-Rank]
The hall fell into stunned silence.
"...What?"
"S-Rank?"
"That’s impossible!"
"I thought only people from Eternal-level worlds could get that!"
"This has to be a mistake..."
Emilia stared at the panel, then burst out laughing.
She couldn’t help it. Of course it was S-Rank. She had expected nothing else.
Leon had never bragged. Never showed off his strength.
But she knew. From the moment he saved her, she knew he was different.
"Don’t you need around 8,000 Combat Power just for A-Rank?" someone shouted.
"Then how much do you need for S-Rank?!"
"At least 10,000... This is insane."
"A low-level world human... at level 10...?"
No one could understand it. And more importantly, no one dared approach him.
In front of them stood someone with nearly ten thousand combat power. A complete anomaly.
Leon calmly stepped away from the stele and returned to Emilia.
She took her turn next. Light flared.
And moments later—
[A-Rank]
Leon nodded, "That’s good."
Emilia let out a small sigh.
"Not as good as yours," she said, shaking her head. "But I’m satisfied. Now we just need to complete them."
Leon didn’t respond immediately.
He didn’t know what an S-Rank assessment contained.
In his past life, he had never even seen one. He would be going in blind. But he wasn’t afraid.
’The rewards will be worth it,’ Leon thought calmly. ’I’ll be fine.’
They walked together toward the far end of the hall. Seven gates stood there, each marked with a letter, from F to S.
A person could only enter a gate if their evaluation matched it, or was lower.
"See you later," Leon said, "Let’s both complete our assessments."
Emilia looked at him for a moment, her expression unreadable. Then she nodded.
"Alright."
She headed toward the A-Rank gate, where only a few others stood nearby, and stepped inside.
As for Leon, he walked toward the S-Rank gate.
There was no one else around it. Not a single person. Because no one else here qualified.
Leon stopped in front of the gate and took a slow, steady breath.
Then, without hesitation, he stepped inside.

There, standing tall and unmoving, was a massive divine stele.
Its surface looked like smooth stone, yet light constantly flowed beneath it, as if something alive existed inside.
A person stood before it now, their palm pressed against the surface.
Others had gathered around, watching closely.
After a few seconds—
Ding!
[C-Rank.]
A panel appeared above the stele.
Immediately, voices erupted.
"Hah, only C-Rank?"
"I mean, that’s still decent.
Only around twenty percent of people can even complete that."
"Yeah, but the rewards won’t be that great."
"What are you talking about?
Don’t you need at least 4,000 Combat Power just to qualify for a C-Rank assessment?"
"Well, I’ve got over 6,000, so I’m aiming for B-Rank."
Leon listened quietly.
This was the [Divine Stele].
Its purpose was simple: it evaluated an individual and determined the highest-rank assessment they were allowed to attempt.
The ranks went from F all the way to S.
The higher the rank, the harder the assessment.
And the better the rewards.
It was said that even among high-level worlds, very few people could clear an A-Rank assessment.
As for S-Rank...
Those were legends.
Only people from Eternal-level worlds were even qualified.
And even then, completion rates were abysmal.
Failure didn’t mean death, at least not immediately.
If you failed an assessment, you were downgraded to the rank below and forced to attempt that one instead.
For example, if that person failed their C-Rank assessment, they would have to go through a D-Rank one and so on.
But if you failed an F-Rank assessment...
You were obliterated.
Deemed too weak to continue existing in [Eternal Ascension].
In his past life, Leon had only qualified for a D-Rank assessment.
He barely survived it.
The rewards were mediocre at best.
This time was different.
"My turn," Leon said, stepping forward with a faint grin.
As he approached the stele, whispers followed.
"A human..."
"I’ve heard of them.
Weak race."
"I met some from an intermediate-level world before, but this one’s from a low-level world."
"E-Rank should be more than enough for him."
Emilia watched quietly from behind, her gaze fixed on Leon.
She didn’t say anything.
She just waited.
Leon placed his palm against the divine stele.
For a brief moment, nothing happened.
Then—
Fwoosh!
A blinding light exploded outward, flooding the entire hall.
People cried out in surprise, shielding their eyes.
The stele vibrated violently.
BOOM!
A massive panel appeared above it.
[S-Rank]
The hall fell into stunned silence.
"...What?"
"S-Rank?"
"That’s impossible!"
"I thought only people from Eternal-level worlds could get that!"
"This has to be a mistake..."
Emilia stared at the panel, then burst out laughing.
She couldn’t help it.
Of course it was S-Rank.
She had expected nothing else.
Leon had never bragged.
Never showed off his strength.
But she knew.
From the moment he saved her, she knew he was different.
"Don’t you need around 8,000 Combat Power just for A-Rank?" someone shouted.
"Then how much do you need for S-Rank?!"
"At least 10,000...
This is insane."
"A low-level world human... at level 10...?"
No one could understand it.
And more importantly, no one dared approach him.
In front of them stood someone with nearly ten thousand combat power.
A complete anomaly.
Leon calmly stepped away from the stele and returned to Emilia.
She took her turn next.
Light flared.
And moments later—
[A-Rank]
Leon nodded, "That’s good."
Emilia let out a small sigh.
"Not as good as yours," she said, shaking her head.
"But I’m satisfied.
Now we just need to complete them."
Leon didn’t respond immediately.
He didn’t know what an S-Rank assessment contained.
In his past life, he had never even seen one.
He would be going in blind.
But he wasn’t afraid.
’The rewards will be worth it,’ Leon thought calmly. ’I’ll be fine.’
They walked together toward the far end of the hall.
Seven gates stood there, each marked with a letter, from F to S.
A person could only enter a gate if their evaluation matched it, or was lower.
"See you later," Leon said, "Let’s both complete our assessments."
Emilia looked at him for a moment, her expression unreadable.
Then she nodded.
"Alright."
She headed toward the A-Rank gate, where only a few others stood nearby, and stepped inside.
As for Leon, he walked toward the S-Rank gate.
There was no one else around it.
Not a single person.
Because no one else here qualified.
Leon stopped in front of the gate and took a slow, steady breath.
Then, without hesitation, he stepped inside.

chapters.title: Chapter 29: S-Rank Assessment, Legacy Fragments
paragraphs: Fwish! Ding!
[You have arrived at the S-Rank Assessment Ground: "Origin Plains"]
Leon slowly opened his eyes. The first thing he noticed was the silence.
It wasn’t the peaceful kind either. It was heavy, pressing down on him from all sides, as if the land itself was watching.
Dark green grass stretched endlessly across the plains, its color muted, almost drained of life.
Above him, the sky was dim and clouded, with no visible sun or stars, just a dull, oppressive glow that made it hard to tell whether it was day or night.
Far in the distance stood a massive mountain. It towered over everything else in the plains, rising like a pillar that pierced the sky.
Its peak radiated an overwhelming power, faint waves of pressure rolling outward from it, subtle yet impossible to ignore.
Leon narrowed his eyes.
"This is..."
He had never seen this place before. And yet, as he stared at the mountain, a strange feeling stirred within him.
Not in the sense that he remembered it, but more like his body recognized it.
As if something deep inside him was being pulled toward that peak, quietly urging him to move.
Leon frowned slightly. What made things even stranger was the lack of information.
Normally, the moment someone entered an assessment ground, a panel would appear explaining the objective.
Even A-Rank assessments gave at least some guidance, as he had spoken to some people who went through them.
"You’ll know what to do as soon as it starts."
But now? Nothing.
Leon waited for a few more seconds, scanning his surroundings, half-expecting another panel to pop up.
But nothing appeared.
"...So I have to figure it out myself," he muttered.
He crouched down and placed his palm against the ground, channeling his power.
Appraisal!
He wanted a map. Or at least some basic information about the terrain.
Beep!
[You are not allowed to analyze this place.]
Leon’s brow twitched.
"So it’s restricted."
Either the assessment itself blocked Appraisal entirely, or his skill simply wasn’t high enough to pierce whatever authority governed this land.
Given that this was an S-Rank assessment, the latter wouldn’t be surprising.
He stood back up and dusted off his hand.
"Fine."
If he couldn’t rely on Appraisal, then he’d do things the old-fashioned way.
Leon lifted his gaze once more toward the distant mountain. The pressure coming from its peak hadn’t lessened in the slightest.
If anything, the longer he stared, the more it felt like the source of everything here.
"That’s where I’m supposed to go," he concluded.
There was no time limit announced, which meant he didn’t need to rush recklessly. Still, standing still wouldn’t accomplish anything either.
Leon leaned forward and burst into motion.
The moment he sprinted, the plains around him blurred.
His agility had long surpassed what level 10 should allow, and every step sent him flying dozens of meters forward.
The dark grass bent under his feet, the air whistling past his ears as he advanced straight toward the mountain.
For several minutes, nothing happened.
No monsters. No obstacles. Just the endless plains and that looming peak ahead.
Then—
BOOM!
The ground in front of Leon suddenly split open.
A massive fissure tore through the earth, stretching wide enough to swallow buildings.
From within the darkness below, cold, oppressive auras surged outward.
Leon skidded to a halt just as figures began to crawl out of the crack. Six of them.
They were clad in pitch-black armor, their forms tall and imposing.
Dark mist leaked from the gaps in their armor, and beneath their helmets, faint crimson lights flickered where eyes should have been.
Every single one of them fixed their gaze on Leon. Leon exhaled slowly and activated Appraisal.
[Soldier of Darkness]
[Level: 10]
[Talent: Darkness Control (D-Level)]
[Combat Power: 8,000]
[Details: Soldiers of darkness that follow the will of the Heavenly One. They will eliminate anything that obstructs their path.]
Leon’s eyes sharpened.
"So that’s how it is."
Each of these soldiers was pushing the absolute limit of level 10 combat power.
One of them alone would be enough to massacre an entire novice village.
Even inside the Novice Divine Temple, very few people could confidently defeat even one.
Six at once would normally be a death sentence. Leon, however, felt no fear.
"Well," he muttered, tightening his grip on both his staff and sword, "this is an assessment. I can’t die here."
His gaze hardened.
"But that doesn’t mean I can afford to hold back."
He raised his staff and poured Spirit into it without hesitation.
Powerful Fireball! Lightning Strike!
The air distorted violently.
A massive fireball condensed in front of Leon, its heat warping the space around it.
At the same time, crackling arcs of lightning gathered overhead, responding to his call.
He thrust his staff forward.
BOOM!
The fireball exploded as it struck the front line of soldiers, engulfing the area in searing flames.
The explosion was far stronger than anything Leon had used before.
The upgraded skill unleashed its full power, scorching the plains and sending shockwaves outward.
Two of the soldiers were instantly reduced to charred remains.
The other four were thrown back, their armor cracked and blackened, dark mist leaking uncontrollably from their bodies.
Leon’s eyes flicked toward them.
"So it works."
A level 6 skill was something no one at this stage should possess.
The damage and area of effect were on a completely different level.
Zap!
The lightning strike descended next, slamming into one of the remaining soldiers. Electricity danced across its armor, locking its body in place.
Leon noticed something interesting at that moment. The other soldiers reacted.
They moved, positioning themselves between Leon and the stunned soldier, raising their blades defensively.
"I guess they have some sort of intelligence," Leon muttered.
One of the soldiers suddenly lunged forward, its movements sharp and decisive.
A dark blade flashed as it aimed straight for Leon’s neck. Leon didn’t even flinch.
Vision Enhancement!
The world slowed. Every motion became crystal clear.
Leon sidestepped with ease, the blade slicing through empty air.
In the same motion, he swung his sword, cutting cleanly through the soldier’s side.
The dark armor split apart.
Before the soldier could retreat, Leon followed up with another slash, this time cleaving its body in half.
The remains collapsed onto the grass. Only three left.
They hesitated. Whether it was fear or calculation, Leon didn’t care.
"If you won’t come to me," he said calmly, "I’ll go to you."
He shifted his stance and poured power into his sword.
Crescent Slash!
Energy gathered along the blade, forming a sharp, crescent-shaped arc.
The soldiers realized what was coming and attempted to move, but it was too late.
SLASH!
The crescent tore through the air, cutting across the plains in a wide arc.
It passed through all three soldiers in an instant, slicing cleanly through their armor and bodies.
They fell without another sound. Leon lowered his sword and let out a slow breath.
"...Yeah. Definitely overpowered."
Ding!
[You have killed x6 "Soldier of Darkness"]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered. Items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
Leon immediately opened his storage, scanning through the loot. Given the nature of this place, he doubted these drops were meaningless.
And sure enough—
[Sub-Talent Scroll x6: Darkness Control (D-Level)]
[Sword of Darkness x3 (Epic): +300 Attack, +200 Strength. Requirement: At least one darkness-related skill or sub-talent.]
[Legacy Fragment x4 (Legendary): Pages taken from the Book of Inheritance. Records the legacy of the gods. Gather all fragments to obtain the inheritance. (4/30)]
Leon paused.
"...Legacy Fragments."
He focused on the pages. Each one was old, its surface covered in symbols and characters unlike anything he had ever seen.
Numbers were etched at the bottom of each page: 5, 8, 11, and 4.
When he tried to read them, nothing happened. He couldn’t understand a single word.
Eternal Ascension automatically translated all languages, regardless of world or race. The fact that this wasn’t being translated meant only one thing.
"This is beyond the system’s standard rules."
Leon’s expression grew serious. Thirty pages total. He had four.
"So this is the objective," he murmured. "Collect the pages. Then something happens."
Not every enemy dropped them, which meant he’d have to hunt specific targets, or perhaps stronger ones.
Leon’s gaze sharpened with anticipation.
He also noted the other drops. Six D-Rank sub-talent scrolls were absurdly valuable, even at higher levels.
The swords were powerful too, though their requirements made them useless to him for now.
Without hesitation, Leon took one of the sub-talent scrolls and poured his mana into it.
The scroll tore apart, dissolving into dark particles that seeped into his body.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have learned the D-Level Sub-Talent: "Darkness Control"]
