chapters.title: Chapter 37: Players Killers Already? Hub City
paragraphs: Appraisal!
Leon slowed to a stop and crouched slightly, pressing his palm against the ground. The familiar sensation spread through his arm as the skill activated.
Ding!
In an instant, a massive map unfolded before his vision, layers of terrain and landmarks spreading outward like a living projection.
"Perfect."
It wasn’t a map of the entire [Lower Domain]. That would have been impossible, the place was far too vast for that.
But it showed everything around him in clear detail. Plains, roads, monster zones, and distant landmarks all appeared at once.
Leon’s eyes moved quickly across it.
"And there’s the desert."
He focused on the golden stretch to the side. It wasn’t as far from the plains as he had initially thought. That meant Emilia couldn’t be too far away.
"And ahead..." his lips curled into a grin, "...the first city."
The symbol was clear. Roads converged there from multiple directions, marking it as a central point.
"That should be somewhat safe."
Of course, Leon knew better than to believe any place in [Eternal Ascension] was truly safe.
Danger existed everywhere, in one form or another. But cities were different. Rules were tighter. Players gathered. Opportunities appeared.
Once he reached it, he could finally begin what he had planned for the [Lower Domain].
Just like in the [Novice Village], this stage was full of chances: hidden ones that only someone with knowledge of the future could truly exploit.
Leon broke into a sprint, his body moving smoothly across the plains. The grass bent under his feet as the wind rushed past him.
It didn’t take long before monsters began to react.
A [Plains Bear] burst from the tall grass with a roar, its massive body charging straight at him.
Leon didn’t slow down. A single strike was enough to bring it down.
Further ahead, a group of [Dwarven Goblins] tried to surround him, crude weapons raised. They didn’t last even a few seconds.
One after another, monsters attempted ambushes. None of them succeeded.
Leon moved efficiently, killing only what got in his way and ignoring everything else. His goal wasn’t to grind here. It was to reach the city as quickly as possible.
Eventually, as the plains stretched thinner and the terrain began to change, Leon saw it.
In the distance, rising above the land, stood the first city. Even from far away, it was impossible to miss.
"That’s it."
The place was known as [Hub City].
The name was simple, but accurate. It was the central hub for most players entering the [Lower Domain].
Roads from different zones all led there, making it a natural gathering point.
Inside, players from countless races crossed paths: elves, demons, and races Leon couldn’t immediately name.
Some were friendly. Some weren’t. Good people and bad people mixed freely.
Leon’s gaze shifted slightly.
Beyond the city, further off to the side, he could see the desert stretching endlessly. That path also led to the city, connecting the [Hard] spawn zone directly to it.
And then, by sheer coincidence—
Ding!
[You have received a message from "Saintess"]
Leon blinked.
[Saintess: Look to your left.]
Leon turned his head. That was when he saw her.
Emilia was running toward him, her scepter held firmly in her hand. Her robes fluttered behind her as she closed the distance quickly.
Leon stopped moving. A wide grin spread across his face as he waited for her to reach him.
"You run really fast for a priestess."
Emilia came to a stop in front of him and puffed out her chest, clearly proud.
"I’m not a priestess. I’m a saintess," she said firmly. "And even though I have support spells, I can fight with magic too."
"I know."
Leon wasn’t surprised.
The [Desert] was the [Hard] spawn zone of the [Lower Domain]. Enemies there ranged from five thousand to six thousand five hundred combat power.
For someone to survive there alone, and kill monsters consistently, meant they were far from ordinary.
The fact that Emilia was doing it so early already made things clear.
’As expected from someone from a high-level world.’
Leon didn’t like the way worlds were categorized. Too many people judged others based on that label alone. Still, he couldn’t deny reality.
There were exceptions, but higher-ranking worlds usually produced stronger individuals.
"I wanted to ask about your talent," Leon said as they began walking toward the city together. "Is it..."
"Elven Saintess," Emilia replied immediately, a grin forming on her face. "SS-Level."
Leon nodded.
"As I thought. That explains why you were allowed to use that ID."
Things were starting to connect in his mind. His theory was becoming clearer.
Certain [Talents] or [Titles] acted as conditions. Without them, some IDs simply couldn’t be used.

He hadn’t come up with that idea out of idle curiosity. In his past life, there were players with extremely specific names, names that clearly meant something. Too many coincidences for it to be random.
Perhaps, if a name was too unique, it meant it was tied directly to something deeper.
They continued forward. The closer they got to the city, the fewer monsters appeared.
The area around [Hub City] was relatively clear, maintained by players themselves.
After a few minutes of walking, Leon reached for his [Storage Space], intending to check the items he had collected earlier.
Then—
Fwoosh!
A sharp sense of danger washed over him.
Leon’s expression changed instantly. He turned around just in time to see an arrow flying straight toward them.
"Shit."
Emilia reacted at the same moment. Both of them dodged aside as the arrow slammed into the ground behind them.
Boom!
A violent explosion erupted where it landed. The shockwave sent dirt and debris flying.
Leon felt the impact, but his [Purple Jade Necklace] activated, absorbing most of the damage.
Emilia was thrown slightly off balance, but her constitution was high enough to endure it.
Still, the situation was clear.
"Player killers already," Leon sighed. "They usually become more common later. I didn’t expect them this early."
Darkness Barrier!
Leon cast his skill instantly. A faint, dark barrier formed around him, thick and durable.
Thanks to his sub-talent, its defensive power was far higher than normal.
"What do we do?!" Emilia groaned. "We don’t even know where they are! Why would they attack us?!"
"Items," Leon replied calmly, "When you kill someone, you can take everything in their [Storage Space]. With how many people are in [Eternal Ascension], one or two deaths don’t matter to them."
In his past life, many player killers were lazy. They relied on numbers or cheap tactics. These ones were different.
That arrow alone was strong enough to kill most unprepared players instantly.
After that first attack, no second arrow came.
Either they realized Leon and Emilia weren’t easy targets and backed off, or they were waiting for another opportunity.
"Player killers are usually overleveled compared to their victims," Leon said. "Let’s get to [Hub City] quickly."
Emilia nodded.
They broke into a run, moving at full speed. Both of them stayed alert, constantly glancing back in case another attack came.
Fortunately, none did.
Even in the [Lower Domain], danger was always present. And Leon knew this was nothing compared to what awaited later.
As they ran, Leon glanced at Emilia, then opened his friend list briefly.
"Eleonore, David, Aaron, and Alice should be fine on their own for now," he thought. "But eventually... they all die."
Early success meant nothing. If he wanted to survive long-term, he needed to grow stronger than everyone else. Much stronger.
With that thought firmly in his mind, Leon and Emilia finally reached the massive gates of [Hub City].
But as they drew closer, Leon frowned.
"...That’s more people than I expected."
The city was crowded. Not just inside the walls, but outside as well. Players gathered everywhere, resting, trading, arguing, and preparing.
"I hope we don’t run into any elves from my world," Emilia said quietly, her expression darkening. "I’m not sure I can beat them."
"Even with eight thousand combat power?" Leon asked, surprised. "How strong are they?"
"Not strong enough for an S-Rank assessment," Emilia replied, "but stronger than me. And there are a lot of them."
Leon nodded.
"Then we’ll be careful."
After a few more minutes, the two of them passed through the gates.
Ding!
[You have entered "Hub City"]
[Please be careful, for an event will be happening soon.]
"Oh?"

chapters.title: Chapter 38: An Event is Happening Soon, Merek The Alchemist
paragraphs: "An event?" Emilia tilted her head slightly. "I guess it is a game. I should have expected it," she said, smiling faintly.
Leon, on the other hand, was genuinely surprised. In his past life, he had never experienced an event in [Hub City].
Back then, it had taken him nearly a full week just to escape the [Novice Village] phase.
By the time he reached the [Lower Domain], whatever had happened here was already long over.
So this was something he had completely missed.
Events, by nature, were extremely rare. They didn’t happen often, and most players could go months without encountering even one.
But when they did occur, they were almost always worth it. The rewards were usually far above what normal grinding could provide.
That alone explained a lot. Now he understood why [Hub City] was so crowded.
Normally, most players preferred to stay in the wild. Some even went as far as establishing their own [Strongholds] in different domains to secure a safer place to rest and regroup.
Anyone could create a [Stronghold], as long as they found a [Stronghold Token].
But those were so rare that most people never even saw one in their lifetime. Because of that, players usually chose to join an existing stronghold instead of creating their own.
Most strongholds were tied directly to guilds.
For example, Eleonore’s guild had possessed its own stronghold in the [Higher Domain] before she died.
As for the [Eternal Domain]... that was on an entirely different level.
The strongest and largest strongholds existed there. Some were so massive they resembled full-fledged kingdoms, capable of housing millions of people at once.
Would Leon ever aim for something like that? Absolutely not.
But even so, he still wanted something. A place where he and his companions could rest safely in each domain. Somewhere stable.
Still, that wasn’t his priority right now.
What mattered was that all these people gathering here had a reason.
They were here for the event.
"Are we participating?" Emilia asked, her expression slightly tense as she glanced around. "There are so many people... and some of them feel really strong."
Leon chuckled.
"Trust yourself more," he said with a grin. "You’re stronger than, like, ninety-five percent of them."
Emilia immediately frowned.
"That still means five percent can beat me," she replied, clearly offended. "I need to rise above ninety-nine point nine percent. That’s the only way I’ll have a real chance at getting my revenge."
"Hah."
Leon didn’t argue. He understood that mindset better than anyone.
As they talked, the two of them reached the central square of [Hub City]. It was wide and open, designed to accommodate large crowds, and right now, it was packed.
Players stood in groups, some chatting excitedly, others arguing, and some simply waiting.
"I heard there was an event coming, so I rushed here as fast as I could."
"Events in [Hub City] are mostly for level ten to fifteen players. If you’re above that, it’s pointless."
"Goddamn it... I just reached level sixteen. I didn’t know that.
Voices overlapped, filling the square with noise and energy.
The atmosphere was lively. Players moved constantly through the streets, filling every corner of the city with motion.
"Should we wait?" Emilia asked. "We don’t even know when the event starts."
Leon didn’t answer right away. He already knew.
If the system panel itself warned players that an event would happen "soon," that usually meant within a day. At most.
"I want to check something in [Hub City] first," Leon said after a moment. "If it’s not done by then, we can head out for a bit and come back later."
"Sure!"
Emilia nodded without hesitation.
She could probably move ahead on her own if she wanted to. She was strong enough for that. But staying with Leon made her feel safer.
Especially with everything else going on.
The elves from her world would kill her on sight if they recognized her. On top of that, there were player killers lurking around, like the ones who had already attacked them earlier.
Taking unnecessary risks right now wasn’t worth it.
"Elves live for a long time," Emilia said suddenly. "But in [Eternal Ascension], we only get one life too. I wonder if there’s a way to get more lives..."
"There is," Leon replied calmly. "But it’s rare. Extremely rare."
That would require a [Resurrection Stone].
And the place he was heading to right now was directly related to that very thing.
Because no matter how strong he became, if he was ambushed or faced someone far beyond him, death would still be the end.
’I can’t let what happened in my past life happen again,’ Leon thought.
They moved deeper into [Hub City], far past the areas most players gathered in. The further they went, the quieter it became.
Eventually, there were almost no players around. Most people had no reason to come this far.
The streets here were broken and abandoned. Buildings stood half-destroyed, their walls cracked, roofs caved in, and interiors stripped bare. There was nothing to loot, nothing to gain.
That was exactly why this area was ignored.
After a few minutes of walking through the ruined district, Leon stopped. He stood in front of a shop.
At first glance, it looked just as destroyed as everything else. Its walls were damaged, and parts of the structure had collapsed. It blended in almost perfectly with the surroundings.
But there was one difference. A small sign hung above the entrance.
[Open]
"Bingo," Leon grinned as he walked forward and pushed the door open.
Emilia followed him inside, looking around with a confused expression.
"Where are we?"
"An alchemist," Leon replied simply.
Inside the shop, furnaces lined the walls. Strange tools and containers were scattered everywhere. Bottles, powders, crystals, and ingredients filled the shelves.
It was clear that this place was used to refine potions, pills, and other items.
"New customers... after so long?" a voice spoke.
Merek, the alchemist, stepped forward.
"I honestly thought no one else would ever come here."
He was a humanoid figure of average height, with blue skin and long ears. A monocle rested over one eye, and when he smiled, a row of sharp teeth was visible.
He wasn’t a player from another world. He was what most called a "Native." Others simply called them NPCs.
But unlike mindless entities, Merek had his own intelligence. His own will.
He could attack. He could be killed.
The main difference between him and players was that he wasn’t allowed to leave this shop.
He followed the will of the [Heavenly One], bound to this place for now.
"I want you to help me," Leon said calmly. "I want—"
"It doesn’t work like that, young man," Merek interrupted, wagging a clawed finger with a wide grin. "If you want something from me, you’ll need to prove yourself first."
’Here we go,’ Leon thought.
At that moment, a system panel appeared before both Leon and Emilia.
Ding!
[You have triggered the S-Level Secret Quest: "Alchemist’s Materials"]
[Time Limit: None.]

"I want you to bring me some materials from the nearby [Undead Temple]," Merek said. "If you bring everything I need... I might have something for you. Though I should warn you, very few ever manage to do it."
Leon already knew what the reward was. The [Resurrection Stone].
There was no way he was letting this chance slip by. Another panel appeared.
Ding!
[0/25 Undead Core, 0/50 Corrupted Bones, 0/1 Undead King Heart]
Those were the required materials. If they gathered all of them, each of them would be able to resurrect once.
Leon had always planned to make sure Emilia got one as well. She was just as much in danger as he was.
"Amazing," Emilia said, staring at the panel with wide eyes. "You really do know everything, Leon."
Leon shrugged.
"We should focus on gathering the materials first."
"Their drop rates are quite low," Merek added arrogantly. "Most who accept my quest never return. I assume they either die... or realize how impossible it truly is~"
"Give me a few hours," Leon said calmly as he turned toward the door. "I’ll be back."
Merek laughed.
"Hah. You’ll understand how difficult it is soon enough, human."

chapters.title: Chapter 39: The Undead Temple, Hard Difficulty Yet Again
paragraphs: "All the items listed are related to the undead," Emilia said thoughtfully. "And he also mentioned something about an [Undead Temple]..."
"It’s a dungeon nearby," Leon replied calmly. "But the recommended level for it is fifteen."
Emilia sucked in a breath. "That’s way higher than our current level. Should we wait?"
"That depends on the event," Leon answered as they left the alchemist’s shop. "If the timing lines up, I think we can clear it anyway. The difficulty matters more than the recommendation."
They didn’t linger in the ruined district for long and soon made their way back toward the main square of [Hub City].
As the first hub most players encountered in the [Lower Domain], [Hub City] felt... normal.
There were no strange structures floating in the air, no hidden traps embedded into the streets, and no monsters roaming freely.
It was one of the rare places in [Eternal Ascension] where players could actually lower their guard, at least a little.
Of course, that didn’t include player killers. But even PKs usually avoided people around their own level. The risk was too high.
Death here was permanent, and no amount of loot was worth gambling your existence against someone of equal strength.
That was why they almost always targeted players much weaker than themselves.
It was a way to have guaranteed profits, as you could acquire the player’s items.
Some people called it efficiency. Leon called it cowardice.
"Here," Leon said casually as they walked, sending a panel toward Emilia. "By the way."
His [Skills] panel opened before her eyes.
[Celestial’s Skills: Appraisal (Lv.4), Vision Enhancement (Lv.4), Powerful Fireball (Lv.6), Lightning Strike (Lv.3), Crescent Slash (Lv.2), Darkness Barrier (Lv.1)]
Emilia stopped walking for a second and stared.
"...Wow," she said honestly. "You have so many skills."
Then she smiled brightly.
"Here’s mine!"
Ding!
A new panel appeared before Leon.
[Saintess’ Skills: Appraisal (Lv.2), Agility Enhancement (Lv.3), Divine Beam (Lv.2), Strength Buff (Lv.1)]
Compared to Leon’s, her list was much shorter. The skill levels were lower as well. That was expected.
Leon was able to obtain a lot of [Skill Stones] early on thanks to his talent. Emilia simply hadn’t had the same opportunities yet.
"My only attacking spell is [Divine Beam]," Emilia said with a shrug. "But thanks to my talent’s passives, I can still keep up."
Leon nodded. He already knew that her [Elven Saintess] talent carried two powerful passive effects.
"Looks like I won’t need to protect you as much as I thought," Leon said with a grin.
"You never needed to," Emilia replied confidently. "And I can buff you too."
"Nice."
They exited the square, passing through crowds of players from countless races.
Some looked excited, some tense, some impatiently checking their panels every few seconds.
Everyone was waiting for the event.
Leon didn’t bother stopping or talking to anyone. Instead, his attention shifted to the map hovering in his vision.
’The [Undead Temple] should be close.’
He focused for a moment and scrolled through the surrounding area.
Sure enough, not far from [Hub City], there was a location marked with a skull-shaped symbol. The distance wasn’t great.
If they moved fast, they could clear the dungeon and be back before the event announcement even appeared.
"Let’s go," Leon said.
Not everyone stayed idle in the city. While many players preferred to wait for events, others continued grinding outside.
After all, events always gave a system-wide warning around thirty minutes before they began.
There was no reason to waste time.
Fwoosh!
Leon and Emilia left [Hub City] and sprinted toward the [Undead Temple].
Vision Enhancement!
Leon activated his skill, and the world around him sharpened. Distances felt shorter. Details became clearer. Even the terrain ahead seemed easier to read.
They encountered no trouble along the way. Still, Leon didn’t relax.
’Maybe they gave up,’ he thought, ’but I’m not stupid enough to assume we’re safe.’
Eventually, the temple came into view. It was massive.
A dark, ancient structure rising from the ground, its walls cracked and worn by time.
Several of its pillars were made from a mix of stone and bones, fused together unnaturally.
At the very top of the structure sat a giant skull, carved into the architecture itself. The mark of a king.
Hundreds of players had already gathered outside the entrance, forming groups and arguing over strategies.
"Hard is suicide without a full party."
"I heard the boss drops insane items though."
"We should wait for more people."
Leon didn’t pay them any attention.
He walked straight toward the entrance, Emilia right beside him.
Fwish! Ding!
[Which difficulty do you wish to choose?]
[Easy] [Normal] [Hard]
Just like the [Wild Ruins], the dungeon allowed players to choose its difficulty.
Most people didn’t know this, but Merek’s quest came with a condition.
Only the [Hard] difficulty spawned the [Undead King].
And only the [Undead King] dropped the heart required for the quest.
This, combined with the already low drop rates of the other materials, was the real reason almost no one ever completed it.
’Hard difficulty... recommended combat power around 16,000.’
Leon’s current combat power was far below that. But that didn’t worry him. Combat power wasn’t everything.
He had buffs. He had burst damage. He had Emilia.
And on top of that... He had [Celestial’s Might].
Even if it hadn’t activated yet, the passive alone made him confident.
Leon selected [Hard].
Ding!
[Undead Temple (Hard Difficulty) has been selected.]
[Party of 2 detected: Celestial and Saintess.]
"Perfect."
No one interfered as the two stepped forward. Their surroundings blurred.
Fwish!
A moment later, solid ground returned beneath their feet. They had entered the [Undead Temple].
Emilia looked around nervously. The air felt heavy. Cold.
"I... this is crazy," she admitted. "These monsters are going to be really strong..."
Leon smiled.
"Yeah," he said. "But that also means more experience and better items."
They stood in a massive stone hall, lit by torches mounted on bone-like handles.
The flames flickered weakly, casting long shadows across the walls.
The two moved forward carefully. After about a minute of walking, Leon felt it.
Enemies. And then they appeared.
[Undead Skeleton]
[Level: 15]
[Combat Power: 11,000]
[Details: Skeletons trained by the ’Undead King’ and bound to his absolute will.]
Eight skeletons stepped into view, each holding a rusted sword. A faint blue fire burned in their eye sockets as they locked onto Leon and Emilia.
Emilia shuddered. "These things are creepy. Let’s deal with them quickly."
"Agreed."
Strength Buff!
Emilia raised her scepter, and light flowed toward Leon.
Ding!
[Your Strength has been doubled.]
[Strength: 384 (+643)]
Leon felt power surge through his body.
His muscles tightened. His grip felt heavier. Stronger.
An increase of nearly one thousand strength meant his combat power jumped by roughly two thousand in an instant.
Support spells scaled with the target’s stats.
And Leon’s stats were abnormal for his level. Emilia smiled slightly, confident.
Leon stepped forward, sword in hand, his grin widening.
"I’m getting to your king," Leon said simply, "But I also need your materials, as well as his heart."

And Leon’s stats were abnormal for his level.
Emilia smiled slightly, confident.
Leon stepped forward, sword in hand, his grin widening.
"I’m getting to your king," Leon said simply, "But I also need your materials, as well as his heart."

chapters.title: Chapter 40: Fighting Undead Skeletons, Acquiring Materials
paragraphs: Slash!
The [Undead Skeletons] were indeed powerful, just as Leon expected from monsters inside a [Hard] difficulty dungeon.
Their movements were precise, their sword swings sharp, and their coordination far better than anything found in the wild.
But even so, they weren’t nearly strong enough to threaten him.
Leon stepped forward without hesitation, parrying the first skeleton’s sword with a clean motion.
The impact echoed through the stone hall, but Leon didn’t even flinch. Using the opening created by the parry, he twisted his wrist and slashed upward.
Crack!
The skeleton’s body was split apart in a single strike. Bones scattered across the floor before dissolving into gray mist.
Another skeleton rushed him from the side, its blade aimed for his ribs. Leon shifted his footing and intercepted it mid-swing, his enhanced strength overwhelming the undead creature instantly.
His sword tore straight through its torso.
At the same time—
Divine Beam!
A column of radiant light erupted from Emilia’s scepter, piercing straight through one of the skeletons.
Holy energy surged through its body, and the undead let out a silent scream before collapsing.
The beam didn’t stop there. It continued forward, burning into two more skeletons and leaving visible cracks along their frames.
Undead-type enemies were naturally weak to holy attacks, and Emilia’s spell exploited that weakness perfectly.
Still, even with their numbers, the skeletons couldn’t push Leon back.
He advanced steadily, blade flashing again and again. Every strike was decisive. Every movement efficient.
His increased strength made each swing lethal, and his experience ensured he never wasted motion.
Within seconds, the hall fell silent.
Ding!
[You have killed x7 "Undead Skeleton" and gained 7,000 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered, items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
The system’s message appeared calmly.
One of the more interesting aspects of [Eternal Ascension] was how parties worked. Unlike many games, experience wasn’t split between members.
As long as the system recognized that you contributed to the fight, you received the full experience for the kills you participated in.
Loot worked the same way, though drop rates still depended on individual talents.
That was why Leon received credit for seven kills instead of eight. Emilia’s [Divine Beam] had completely finished off one skeleton on its own.
However, for the others she damaged, she still received the same experience Leon did.
Leon opened his storage space without hesitation.
[Undead Core x7]
[Corrupted Bones x13]
[Undead Sword x6 (Uncommon): +750 Attack, +500 Strength. Requirement: Level 13.]
[Undead Skeleton Essence x5: Consuming will increase strength 8.]
"Nice," Leon muttered, genuinely pleased.
The drops were far better than he expected for a single group of monsters. Especially the [Undead Swords]. Six of them meant he could immediately attempt equipment fusion.
Without wasting time, Leon initiated the process.
Ding!
[You have consumed two identical equipments... enhancement successful!]
Light flickered briefly around the weapon in his hands.
[Undead Sword +3 (Uncommon): +1,100 Attack, +700 Strength, +200 Agility. Requirement: Level 14.]
Leon’s eyes lit up.
The level requirement had increased, but the stats more than made up for it. If he didn’t find a better weapon before reaching level fourteen, this sword would easily carry him for a while.
And knowing this dungeon, better loot was very likely.
He then consumed all five [Undead Skeleton Essences] without hesitation. Power flowed into his body as his strength rose by forty points.
Only then did Leon notice two new panels hovering before him.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 11!]
And immediately after—
[Due to "Heaven’s Blessing", you have gained 100 points in all attributes, and 100 free points to distribute.]
"HAHA!" Leon laughed out loud.
’It worked!’
He had known it would activate. A passive tied to a celestial title wouldn’t be fake.
But actually seeing it trigger, actually receiving the rewards, made it feel overwhelmingly real.
Emilia blinked in confusion as she looked at Leon.
"I only got a few materials and one essence," she said slowly. "My drop rate isn’t great, but... did you just level up?"
"Yeah," Leon replied, still grinning. "I’m good for now. I got a lot stronger."
He immediately allocated his free points, placing half into [Strength] and the other half into [Spirit].
The effect was instant.
His [Combat Power] jumped sharply, rising by nearly one thousand from a single level-up.
Being a [Celestial Being] truly was absurd.
Still, Leon kept himself grounded. There were others out there, other celestials.
And there was always the chance that they possessed the same passive.
"Wow..." Emilia stared at him, eyes wide. "You feel... way stronger."
Rapid increases in power were impossible to hide. Even without seeing his panel, she could feel the pressure radiating off him.
Leon glanced at his updated combat power.
[Combat Power: 4,524 (+7,436)]
"Just over twelve thousand," he said with satisfaction.
After Emilia absorbed the essence she had obtained, the two pressed deeper into the [Undead Temple].
They encountered several more groups of [Undead Skeletons] along the way. With their coordination improving and Emilia supporting him when needed, they cleared each group efficiently.
Before long, Emilia also reached level eleven.
From level ten onward, experience requirements increased steadily, an additional two thousand per level until level twenty-five. After that, leveling became far more difficult.
But for now, fighting monsters above their level inside a [Hard] dungeon gave them more than enough experience.
Eventually, they entered a large chamber. The ceiling stretched high above them, and at the far end stood a wide flight of stone stairs leading downward.
However, the path was blocked.
Two new types of undead stood between them and the stairs.
[Undead Zombie]
[Level: 15]
[Combat Power: 11,800]
[Exclusive Talent: Infection]
[Details: A zombie that can infect others into joining them, do not let it hit you too much.]
[Undead Ghoul]
[Level: 15]
[Talent: Agility Enhancement (E-Level)]
[Combat Power: 12,500]
[Details: Ghouls that live deep inside of the "Undead Temple", protecting the way to the king’s tomb.]
Before Leon could speak—
Divine Beam!
Emilia struck first.
Her holy beam pierced straight through an [Undead Zombie] and continued into a nearby [Undead Ghoul], obliterating both in an instant.
"Haha!" she laughed, clearly encouraged.
Leon, however, didn’t rush forward. Instead, he raised his staff.
The [Infection] talent made the zombies extremely dangerous at close range.
Repeated hits could eventually turn a player into one of them. That mechanic existed only in the [Hard] difficulty.
Staying back was the correct choice.
Powerful Fireball! Lightning Strike!
A blazing sphere of fire exploded among the undead, followed by a crackling bolt of lightning.
Several monsters were scorched instantly, collapsing before they could even react.
The remaining undead let out distorted growls and charged forward at full speed.
Emilia stepped back instinctively, her skills still on cooldown.
Leon didn’t move.
Darkness Barrier:
A faint dark shield formed around him just as the zombies reached him. Their claws slammed into the barrier repeatedly.
Nothing happened. The barrier didn’t even tremble.
Leon smiled. "Guess I didn’t need to worry after all."
He stepped forward and decapitated one of the zombies in a single swing.
Slash! Slash!
The others clawed at him desperately, but their attacks were useless. The barrier’s durability was massively boosted by Leon’s [Vessel of Darkness] sub-talent.
Within seconds, the zombies fell. Only the [Undead Ghouls] remained.
Their claws glinted as they circled cautiously.
Leon took a step forward—
BOOM!
The ground cracked violently beneath him.
Leon instantly leaped back as a massive clawed arm burst from the floor.
Stone shattered. Dust filled the air. Something climbed out.
[Undead Ghoul (Mutated)]
[Level: 15]
[Talent: Agility Enhancement (D-Level)]
[Combat Power: 13,700]
[Details: A ghoul that surpasses all the others, its claws are sharp, able to cut through any skin.]
"Damn," Emilia said sharply, activating [Agility Enhancement]. "Be careful."
"Yeah," Leon replied, tightening his grip on his staff and sword.
He knew what lay beyond those stairs. The final chamber. And the [Undead King].

chapters.title: Chapter 41: Emilia’s First Sub-Talent, Reaching The Final Chamber
paragraphs: The mutated undead ghoul was massive.
It stood nearly three times taller than the normal ones, its twisted body stretched and reinforced by corrupted energy.
Its skin was thick, gray, and cracked, as if it had been stitched together from several corpses and forcefully kept alive.
Each time it swung its oversized claws at Leon, the air itself seemed to tear.
Boom!
Leon narrowly dodged to the side, and the claws slammed into the stone floor instead. Deep grooves were carved into the ground, spreading outward like spiderweb cracks.
"...That thing’s strength is on another level," Leon muttered.
Slash!
He lunged forward and struck, his blade cutting across the ghoul’s torso.
Blackened blood sprayed out, but the monster barely staggered. It simply let out a low, distorted growl and swung again.
Leon raised his hand instinctively.
Darkness Barrier!
A semi-transparent wall of black energy formed in front of him just as the claws crashed into it.
Crack!
Leon’s eyes narrowed.
Unlike the previous [Undead Zombies], the barrier didn’t fully absorb the impact. Thin cracks spread across its surface, pulsing faintly before stabilizing.
"So it can actually damage it," Leon noted calmly.
That alone told him everything he needed to know. This wasn’t something he could casually tank forever.
Powerful Fireball!
A blazing sphere of compressed flames formed above Leon’s palm and shot forward. It slammed directly into the mutated ghoul’s chest.
Boom!
The explosion engulfed its upper body in fire. The monster roared in pain and was forced several steps backward, its scorched flesh smoking heavily.
"Now," Leon said simply.
Emilia had already prepared herself.
She lifted her staff without hesitation, holy light gathering at its tip.
Divine Beam!
A radiant beam of white light shot forward and pierced straight through the ghoul’s shoulder.
BOOM!
The arm exploded into fragments of bone and decayed flesh, crashing to the ground. The mutated undead ghoul staggered violently, its balance thrown off, but it didn’t fall.
"It’s still alive?" Emilia gasped.
"That thing’s durable," Leon sighed.
Before either of them could press the advantage, movement erupted around them.
The remaining undead ghouls finally acted.
Several of them rushed forward at the same time, their claws raised high, their jaws hanging open as dark energy poured from their mouths.
Their footsteps echoed through the chamber as they closed the distance rapidly.
Strength Buff!
Golden light enveloped Leon once more, sinking into his body.
Ding!
[Your Strength has been doubled from the buff.]
Leon felt the familiar surge of power rush through his muscles. His grip tightened around his sword as he focused everything into a single motion.
For a brief moment, the world slowed.
Then—
Crescent Slash!
A massive crescent-shaped blade of energy surged forward from Leon’s sword. It swept through the chamber in a wide arc, passing through every ghoul in its path.
Shhk!
The sound was clean and decisive.
The normal ghouls were cut in half instantly, their bodies collapsing to the ground before they even realized what had happened.
Even the mutated one wasn’t spared.
The crescent struck its lower body, severing both legs and sending the upper half crashing heavily onto the floor.
The creature writhed briefly, disoriented and enraged, clawing uselessly at the stone.
Lightning Strike!
Leon raised his sword once more, lightning gathering around the blade before crashing down in a blinding flash.
Crack!
The bolt struck the mutated ghoul directly in the head.
Its body twitched once... then went still. Silence filled the chamber.
Ding!
[You have killed x5 "Undead Zombie" and gained 3,250 experience points.]
[You have killed x6 "Undead Ghoul" and gained 3,500 experience points.]
[You have killed "Undead Ghoul (Mutated)" and gained 1,200 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered...]
Leon exhaled slowly, lowering his sword.
But before he could even open his storage panel—
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 12!]
[Due to "Heaven’s Blessing", you have gained 100 points in all attributes, and 100 free points to distribute.]
"Hah," Leon grinned. "Higher difficulty dungeons really are the best."
"You leveled up again?!" Emilia stared at the party panel in disbelief. "That’s... that’s incredible."
Leon’s level had jumped once more, widening the gap between him and most players their level.
Thanks to the fact that Emilia’s [Strength Buff] counted as technical assistance, she also received a share of the kills.
Her own experience increased noticeably, even if she hadn’t landed the final blows.
Leon didn’t hesitate. He immediately allocated all 100 free points into [Spirit].
He could already feel the difference. His mana pool expanded, and the flow of energy within him became smoother and denser.
After that, both of them looked ahead. The chamber was completely empty now.
No more enemies. Which meant only one thing.
"This should be the last stretch," Leon said.
They advanced deeper into the [Undead Temple], descending toward its lowest level. Along the way, Leon absorbed the monster essences he had obtained.
Ding!
[+59 Strength, +24 Agility, +10 Constitution.]
He nodded slightly. Solid gains.
More importantly, the materials dropped were exactly what he needed.
[+12 Undead Cores, +25 Corrupted Bones.]
Leon checked the quest requirements briefly.
"...Yeah," he muttered. "I’m almost done."
At this point, the boss was guaranteed to give him whatever was missing.
Aside from materials, he also received several rare items. Six [Sub-Talent Scrolls: Agility Enhancement (E-Level)].
And one [Agility Enhancement (D-Level)] scroll from the mutated ghoul.
Leon didn’t waste any time.
The first thing he did was attempt to fuse them with his existing sub-talent.
Ding!
[Fusion failed.]
The first attempt failed. He tried again.
Ding!
[Fusion failed.]
Third attempt.
Ding!
[Fusion failed.]
Leon frowned slightly, but remained calm.
Fourth attempt—
Ding!
[Fusion successful.]
[You have evolved "Agility Enhancement (E-Level)" to "Agility Enhancement (D-Level).]
"Good," Leon said quietly.
He didn’t even pause to read the description.
Instead, he immediately used the D-Level scroll as well.
And—
Ding!
[Fusion successful.]
"Oh shit," Leon blurted out instinctively.
Emilia turned toward him, confused. "What happened?"
"It worked," Leon said, grinning.
[You have evolved "Agility Enhancement (D-Level)" to "Super Agility Enhancement (C-Level).]
The name had changed slightly, but that wasn’t what mattered most.
Leon opened the description.
[Super Agility Enhancement (C-Level): Permanently increases agility by 50%.]
Leon closed the panel slowly.
Just the thought of how powerful this sub-talent could become at higher levels made his heart race slightly.
If it reached B-Level, or even A-Level, his movement speed would become absurd.
Still, he had two sub-talent scrolls left. Without hesitation, he handed them to Emilia.
"Huh?" She blinked in confusion, then looked at the items.
Her eyes widened instantly.
"N-No way?!"
Sub-talents were absurdly rare.
Most players wouldn’t even see one until they were deep within the [Lower Domain], and even then, the drop rates were terrible.
Not every monster could drop them, and even when they did, there was no guarantee it would be a useful one.
The fact that Leon was giving her two without hesitation felt unreal.
"Thank you," Emilia said sincerely, bowing slightly.
She learned the sub-talent and then fused it with the second scroll.
Ding!
[Fusion successful.]
She gained [Agility Enhancement (D-Level)], noticeably improving her movement speed.
After finishing their preparations, the two descended the final flight of stairs. At the bottom stood an enormous ancient door.
Its surface was covered in old, intricate runes, mixed with unmistakable undead symbols. A heavy pressure seeped from it, far stronger than anything they had felt so far.
Leon studied it briefly.
"Definitely something exclusive to the [Hard] difficulty," he mumbled.
The boss of the [Easy] and [Normal] difficulty was the [Death Revenant]. Strong, yes, but nothing compared to what awaited them here.
Leon pushed the door open.
Creeeak!
The sound echoed as the massive doors slowly parted. Beyond them lay the boss chamber.
It was vast, ominous, and dimly lit by flickering torches embedded into the walls.
The air was heavy, thick with death energy, pressing down on them like an invisible weight.
"Makes me realize something," Emilia said quietly, shivering. "We were running this place at level 10 and 11... even though it’s a level 15 zone."
Leon didn’t respond. His eyes were locked onto the center of the chamber.
There, standing calmly, was the ruler of this place.
"A human and an elf," a cold voice echoed, "entering my temple and slaughtering my undead..."
The figure slowly turned toward them.
"Pathetic."
A towering being clad in an obsidian robe stood before them, a scepter gripped tightly in its skeletal hand. Its eyes burned with malevolent green flames.
The [Undead King].
Appraisal!
Both Leon and Emilia activated it instantly.
[Undead King (Zone Boss)]
[Level: 15]
[Combat Power: 16,000]
[Talent: Spirit Enhancement (D-Level), Basic Necromancy (E-Level)]
[Details: The ruler of the Undead Temple, commander of all undead within this domain.]
Leon tightened his grip on his sword and staff. Emilia raised her scepter.
The fight was about to begin.

"You leveled up again?!" Emilia stared at the party panel in disbelief.
"That’s... that’s incredible."
Leon’s level had jumped once more, widening the gap between him and most players their level.
Thanks to the fact that Emilia’s [Strength Buff] counted as technical assistance, she also received a share of the kills.
Her own experience increased noticeably, even if she hadn’t landed the final blows.
Leon didn’t hesitate.
He immediately allocated all 100 free points into [Spirit].
He could already feel the difference.
His mana pool expanded, and the flow of energy within him became smoother and denser.
After that, both of them looked ahead.
The chamber was completely empty now.
No more enemies.
Which meant only one thing.
"This should be the last stretch," Leon said.
They advanced deeper into the [Undead Temple], descending toward its lowest level.
Along the way, Leon absorbed the monster essences he had obtained.
Ding!
[+59 Strength, +24 Agility, +10 Constitution.]
He nodded slightly.
Solid gains.
More importantly, the materials dropped were exactly what he needed.
[+12 Undead Cores, +25 Corrupted Bones.]
Leon checked the quest requirements briefly.
"...Yeah," he muttered.
"I’m almost done."
At this point, the boss was guaranteed to give him whatever was missing.
Aside from materials, he also received several rare items.
Six [Sub-Talent Scrolls: Agility Enhancement (E-Level)].
And one [Agility Enhancement (D-Level)] scroll from the mutated ghoul.
Leon didn’t waste any time.
The first thing he did was attempt to fuse them with his existing sub-talent.
Ding!
[Fusion failed.]
The first attempt failed.
He tried again.
Ding!
[Fusion failed.]
Third attempt.
Ding!
[Fusion failed.]
Leon frowned slightly, but remained calm.
Fourth attempt—
Ding!
[Fusion successful.]
[You have evolved "Agility Enhancement (E-Level)" to "Agility Enhancement (D-Level).]
"Good," Leon said quietly.
He didn’t even pause to read the description.
Instead, he immediately used the D-Level scroll as well.
And—
Ding!
[Fusion successful.]
"Oh shit," Leon blurted out instinctively.
Emilia turned toward him, confused.
"What happened?"
"It worked," Leon said, grinning.
[You have evolved "Agility Enhancement (D-Level)" to "Super Agility Enhancement (C-Level).]
The name had changed slightly, but that wasn’t what mattered most.
Leon opened the description.
[Super Agility Enhancement (C-Level): Permanently increases agility by 50%.]
Leon closed the panel slowly.
Just the thought of how powerful this sub-talent could become at higher levels made his heart race slightly.
If it reached B-Level, or even A-Level, his movement speed would become absurd.
Still, he had two sub-talent scrolls left.
Without hesitation, he handed them to Emilia.
"Huh?" She blinked in confusion, then looked at the items.
Her eyes widened instantly.
"N-No way?!"
Sub-talents were absurdly rare.
Most players wouldn’t even see one until they were deep within the [Lower Domain], and even then, the drop rates were terrible.
Not every monster could drop them, and even when they did, there was no guarantee it would be a useful one.
The fact that Leon was giving her two without hesitation felt unreal.
"Thank you," Emilia said sincerely, bowing slightly.
She learned the sub-talent and then fused it with the second scroll.
Ding!
[Fusion successful.]
She gained [Agility Enhancement (D-Level)], noticeably improving her movement speed.
After finishing their preparations, the two descended the final flight of stairs.
At the bottom stood an enormous ancient door.
Its surface was covered in old, intricate runes, mixed with unmistakable undead symbols.
A heavy pressure seeped from it, far stronger than anything they had felt so far.
Leon studied it briefly.
"Definitely something exclusive to the [Hard] difficulty," he mumbled.
The boss of the [Easy] and [Normal] difficulty was the [Death Revenant].
Strong, yes, but nothing compared to what awaited them here.
Leon pushed the door open.
Creeeak!
The sound echoed as the massive doors slowly parted.
Beyond them lay the boss chamber.
It was vast, ominous, and dimly lit by flickering torches embedded into the walls.
The air was heavy, thick with death energy, pressing down on them like an invisible weight.
"Makes me realize something," Emilia said quietly, shivering.
"We were running this place at level 10 and 11... even though it’s a level 15 zone."
Leon didn’t respond.
His eyes were locked onto the center of the chamber.
There, standing calmly, was the ruler of this place.
"A human and an elf," a cold voice echoed, "entering my temple and slaughtering my undead..."
The figure slowly turned toward them.
"Pathetic."
A towering being clad in an obsidian robe stood before them, a scepter gripped tightly in its skeletal hand.
Its eyes burned with malevolent green flames.
The [Undead King].
Appraisal!
Both Leon and Emilia activated it instantly.
[Undead King (Zone Boss)]
[Level: 15]
[Combat Power: 16,000]
[Talent: Spirit Enhancement (D-Level), Basic Necromancy (E-Level)]
[Details: The ruler of the Undead Temple, commander of all undead within this domain.]
Leon tightened his grip on his sword and staff.
Emilia raised her scepter.
The fight was about to begin.

chapters.title: Chapter 42: The Undead King, Using Celestial’s Might
paragraphs: "Come forth, my undead knights."
The moment those words left the [Undead King]’s mouth, the atmosphere inside the chamber changed completely.
He lifted his scepter high, and a chilling aura poured out from his body, spreading across the stone floor like a living thing.
The torches flickered violently, their flames shrinking as death-aspected mana flooded the room.
Basic Necromancy!
The Undead King didn’t hesitate. Along with his talent, he activated a skill engraved deep into his existence.
Undead Knight Summon!
Fwoosh!
The ground trembled.
Dark cracks spread across the floor in front of the Undead King, and thick waves of black mist erupted upward. For several seconds, nothing could be seen except swirling death energy.
Then—
Five figures slowly emerged.
Bone hands clawed their way out of the ground, followed by armored legs, torsos, and finally helmeted heads. Each one rose in complete silence, standing in perfect formation before their king.
[Undead Knight]
[Level: 15]
[Exclusive Talent: Undead Summon (D-Level)]
[Combat Power: 15,000]
[Details: Knights summoned by the Undead King using necromantic authority.]
The Undead Knights stood roughly 1.8 meters tall, clad head to toe in obsidian-black armor etched with faint green runes. Each of them wielded a heavy sword that pulsed with death energy.
Their presence alone was oppressive.
Behind them, the Undead King himself radiated even more pressure.
Leon immediately understood the situation.
In raw numbers, both the knights and their king were stronger than him.
But that didn’t matter. Leon moved.
He rushed forward without hesitation, his boots scraping against the stone floor as he closed the distance.
"Foolish," the Undead King said coldly. "Protect me, knights. We shall erase this player."
At his command, the Undead Knights shifted instantly.
They spread out, forming a defensive formation in front of the king. Swords were lifted, blades angled toward Leon, their movements perfectly synchronized.
Powerful Fireball! Lightning Strike!
Leon attacked first.
A blazing fireball roared through the air, followed immediately by a bolt of lightning crashing down from above. The spells collided with the front line of knights in rapid succession.
Boom! Crack!
But instead of being blown apart—
The knights merely slid back a step.
Their armor glowed faintly, absorbing most of the impact.
Leon’s eyes narrowed.
"Their armor has magic resistance," he said calmly. "Be careful."
Divine Beam!
Emilia stepped forward and fired her holy beam. The light washed over all five knights, striking them directly.
Yet just as Leon warned, it only left shallow scorch marks across their armor.
"Ah shit," Emilia muttered. "I seriously need more skills."
"We’ll get them soon enough," Leon replied without looking back. "Just buff me."
To Leon, Emilia was already one of the best supports he had ever encountered—possibly in the entirety of [Eternal Ascension].
Not just because she had buffs, but because of what she was. Her [Support Saint] title was absurd.
Her constitution was multiplied by five, making her far more durable than any player at her level. On top of that, her support-type spells were strengthened by her unique trait.
Leon still needed to ask her about the full passive effects of her [Elven Saintess] talent. That knowledge would determine their future strategy.
But for now, this was enough.
Vision Enhancement!
The world sharpened around Leon. Colors became clearer, movements slower, and weak points more visible.
Fwish!
He dashed toward the nearest Undead Knight and swung his sword.
Clang!
The knight blocked, its blade meeting Leon’s with a heavy metallic impact. Sparks flew as the two forces collided.
At the same moment—
The other four knights moved.
They surrounded Leon from all sides, swords rising in unison. Even the Undead King raised his scepter, green flames gathering at its tip.
Spectral Flames!
A wave of ghostly fire surged forward, rushing toward Leon along with the knights’ blades.
"Leon!" Emilia shouted, panic creeping into her voice.
She tried to move, but she knew it.
There was nothing she could do right now.
Against opponents with higher combat power and equipment designed to counter magic, reaction time was everything.
In Leon’s past life, moments like this happened constantly.
If you couldn’t adapt fast enough, death was immediate.
That was why items like [Resurrection Stones] were priceless. They allowed a single mistake, just one, to not be the end.
But just as the attacks were about to land—
Ding!
[Celestial’s Might has activated.]
Leon’s eyes turned silvery-white.
A terrifying pressure exploded outward from his body, sweeping across the entire chamber like a divine storm.
"What?!"
Every undead froze.
Their bodies began trembling uncontrollably, as if forced to kneel before something far above them.
Ding!
[Enemy attributes have been reduced by 30%.]
The change was instant. The oppressive pressure vanished, replaced by instability.
[Undead King]
[Combat Power: 11,200]
[Undead Knight]
[Combat Power: 10,500]
They were still dangerous. They still had their skills, experience, and coordination.
But they were no longer overwhelming.
"A celestial?" the Undead King said sharply, his voice filled with shock. "Impossible... they should all be... never mind."
He clearly recognized Leon’s title. But he chose not to continue.
Clang!
Leon blocked the incoming blades with ease now, his sword moving smoothly as he parried and countered.
Slash!
One Undead Knight’s armor split open as Leon’s blade cut cleanly through its torso. The knight collapsed, its body dissolving into black mist.
Spectral Flames!
The Undead King refused to retreat. He slammed his scepter into the ground, spreading spectral fire across the chamber floor.
Green flames surged outward, consuming everything in their path.
Leon sidestepped effortlessly.
Powerful Fireball!
He retaliated instantly, launching his fireball straight at the Undead King.
Boom!
The explosion engulfed the king’s upper body.
"Gah—"
With his combat power reduced, his constitution had fallen as well. The damage was far greater than before.
Slash!
Leon didn’t give him time to recover. He moved like a blur, cutting down another Undead Knight.
Divine Beam!
Emilia seized the opening and fired her beam, piercing straight through a knight’s chest. It froze for a moment before collapsing.
The remaining knights fell one by one.
Some to Leon’s blade. One to Emilia’s spell.
In less than a minute—
Only the Undead King remained.
The green flames in his eyes flared violently as he stared at Leon.
"A power such as this..." he said coldly. "It should not exist here. You must be the last one."
"Deal with it," Leon grinned. "I’m ending this."
"So be it."
The Undead King struck his scepter against the ground again. Dark flames spread across the floor in a complex pattern.
"I shall eliminate you before you become a threat."
He lifted his staff, necromantic energy surging, preparing to summon more undead—
Powerful Fireball!
Leon didn’t let him finish.
The fireball slammed into the Undead King’s chest, completely disrupting the spell.
Before the king could recover—
Slash!
Leon stepped in and decapitated him cleanly.
The head rolled across the stone floor, the green flames fading instantly. Silence.
Ding!
[You have killed x5 "Undead Knights" and gained 3,500 experience points.]
[You have killed "Undead King (Zone Boss)" and gained 5,000 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered. Items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
Leon exhaled slowly.
Surprisingly, it wasn’t enough to level him up—but he was close.
"Nice!" Emilia said brightly. "But... are we sure we got the king’s heart for the quest?"
Leon didn’t answer right away. Instead, he opened his [Storage Space].
Normally, even after defeating the Undead King, there was only a one-in-three chance to obtain the [Undead King Heart].
Most players had to clear the dungeon multiple times.
But for Leon, the item was already there.
[Undead King Heart (Legendary): Material required for Merek’s S-Level Secret Quest. Bring it to him.]
"Hah," Leon said, showing it to Emilia. "I got it."
Her eyes lit up immediately.
"Yes!"
But Leon wasn’t done.
He continued scrolling through his storage, his grin slowly widening as he checked the rest of the items he had obtained.
