chapters.title: Chapter 43: Basic Necromancy Sub-Talent, Spectral Flames
paragraphs: Leon’s gaze lingered on the list of items floating in front of him, one after another, his grin slowly widening as he took everything in.
[Undead Knight Essence x5: Consuming will increase constitution by 8.]
[Undead King Essence: Consuming will increase spirit by 10 and constitution by 5.]
[Undead King Scepter (Epic): +500 Magic Attack, +500 Spirit, +300 Agility. Requirement: Level 15.]
[Undead Knight Armor x5 (Elite): +600 Defense, +400 Constitution, -100 Agility. Requirement: Level 15.]
[Materials: Undead Core x6, Corrupted Bones x11]
[Sub-Talent Scrolls: Spirit Enhancement (D-Level), Basic Necromancy (E-Level)]
[Skill Book: Spectral Flames (Epic)]
"Pretty good," Leon nodded in approval, a satisfied smile spreading across his face.
For a single dungeon run, especially one taken far earlier than recommended, this haul was absurd.
Any other player would have considered themselves lucky to walk out with half of this.
Yet for Leon, it was simply confirmation that choosing the [Hard] difficulty had been the correct decision.
Then another panel appeared.
Ding!
[25/25 Undead Core, 50/50 Corrupted Bones, 1/1 Undead King Heart.]
[You have acquired all the materials needed for Merek’s quest. Return to him to complete it.]
"Got enough," Leon said, turning toward Emilia with a grin. "We can return."
As if on cue, a teleportation portal formed in the center of the chamber.
Pale blue light swirled quietly, stable and inviting. Stepping through it would immediately send them out of the dungeon.
Emilia stared at the portal, then back at Leon, confusion written all over her face.
"But... we don’t have enough materials for both of us," she said slowly. "There’s only one heart. Won’t only one of us complete the quest?"
"No," Leon shook his head without hesitation. "Trust me. We’ll both get a resurrection stone."
She blinked at him, clearly unsure how that was even possible.
Still, after everything she had seen so far, doubting him felt pointless.
"...Alright," she nodded. "I trust you."
From the fight against the Undead King and his knights, Emilia had leveled up to level 12.
She hadn’t received anywhere near as many items as Leon, but that was expected. Her drop rate was normal. His was anything but.
Leon didn’t waste time. He consumed all the essences immediately.
Ding!
[+40 Strength, +10 Spirit, +5 Constitution.]
The increase was modest compared to some of his other gains, but every point mattered.
At higher levels, even small increases translated into noticeable boosts in combat power.
Next, Leon attempted to fuse the Undead Knight Armor pieces. One attempt failed. The second succeeded.
Ding!
[Undead Knight Armor +2 (Elite): +800 Defense, +500 Constitution, -80 Agility. Requirement: Level 15.]
"Not bad," Leon muttered.
He couldn’t equip it yet due to the level requirement, but the stats were solid.
Heavy armor like this was meant for frontline fighters, and once he reached level 15, it could serve as a temporary upgrade.
Leon then turned toward Emilia and casually tossed two items her way.
"You can take these," he said. "The scepter and the skill book."
Emilia caught them reflexively, then froze when she saw what they were.
The [Undead King Scepter]. And an Epic skill book. Her eyes widened.
"You’re giving these to me?" she asked, clearly shocked.
"I can’t use the scepter," Leon replied calmly. "And while I could learn [Spectral Flames], it’ll benefit us more if you do. You getting stronger helps me too."
For a moment, Emilia just stared at him. Then suddenly, she hugged him.
"Thanks—!"
Realizing what she had done a split second later, she pulled back instantly, her face turning bright red.
"S-Sorry!"
Leon blinked, then chuckled softly. "It’s fine."
Trying to hide her embarrassment, Emilia immediately focused on the skill book. She poured mana into it without hesitation.
Fwoosh!
The book dissolved into motes of light that flowed into her body.
Ding!
[You have learned "Spectral Flames"]
"Yes," Emilia smiled, clearly pleased. She then stored the Undead King Scepter away for later use.
Leon nodded. "Your skills are still underleveled, though. We’ll need a lot of [Skill Stones]."
"I know..." Emilia sighed lightly. "They’re hard to find."
"I already have a place in mind," Leon replied.
A place that could supply skill stones in bulk. A dangerous place, but perfect. It wasn’t time to go there yet. Not now.
Leon shifted his attention to the last items left in his storage: the sub-talent scrolls.
He took out the first one: [Spirit Enhancement (D-Level)]
Without hesitation, he poured mana into it and tore it apart.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have learned the D-Level Sub-Talent: "Spirit Enhancement"]
[Spirit Enhancement (D-Level): Permanently increases spirit by 30%.]
Leon exhaled slowly.
"Amazing."
With this, all four of his core attributes were now enhanced by sub-talents. Strength, agility, constitution, and spirit, each one boosted permanently.
He would need to find ways to evolve them further, but for now, this alone was already monstrous.
Then there was the last scroll: [Basic Necromancy (E-Level)]
Leon paused for a moment. This was rare. Extremely rare.

Necromancy-related monsters were uncommon to begin with. Getting a sub-talent scroll from one was even rarer. And unless your talent or title was tied to necromancy, there were very few ways to acquire something similar.
Even in his past life, Leon had only met a handful of necromancers.
Among them, one stood above the rest. The [UndeadLiege] was her ID.
A player capable of summoning thousands of undead soldiers, wiping out entire armies alone.
Leon shook his head lightly.
"No point thinking about that now."
He poured mana into the scroll and tore it apart.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have learned the E-Level Sub-Talent: "Basic Necromancy"]
Unlike the others, this sub-talent’s panel was larger. Leon immediately opened it.
[Basic Necromancy (E-Level): You become a novice necromancer, able to summon undead skeletons to aid you.]
[Skeleton Summon Limit: 3.]
[Each summoned skeleton has 25% of your base stats.]
"Interesting."
That meant as Leon grew stronger, his summoned skeletons would scale with him.
Right now, each one would only have around four to five hundred points in their main stats.
Enough to distract enemies, maybe help with weaker monsters, but not enough to pose a real threat. Still, the potential was there.
"I’ll have to test it later," Leon murmured. "And find ways to boost them."
For now, he was satisfied.
"Done?" Emilia asked with a grin. "You spent more time on loot than on the actual fight."
"I get a lot," Leon shrugged. "And yeah. It’s related to my talent."
"That just makes me more curious~"
Leon smiled but didn’t answer. He could tell her. He trusted her.
But revealing it now wouldn’t change anything as it didn’t help in battle. His talent only truly mattered after enemies were dead.
Fwoosh!
"Wait," Leon said as they were about to head out, "Grab this."
Leon tossed all of the materials required for the quest to Emilia, who held them all in her hands and...
Ding!
[You have acquired all the materials needed for Merek’s quest...]
She also received the panel.
"Alright."
Leon then took the items once more and stored them in his storage space except for some of the [Corrupted Bones].
The two stepped into the portal, light enveloping them.
In the next instant, they reappeared outside the [Undead Temple].
Without stopping, they headed back toward [Hub City].
Along the way, a stray monster crossed their path. Emilia raised her scepter and activated her newly learned skill.
Spectral Flames!
Ghostly fire surged forward, engulfing the monster and reducing it to ash almost instantly.
Her eyes lit up.
"Nice," she said happily. "I’ve got two attacking spells now."
Leon nodded.
He didn’t even consider going back to farm the Undead King for the skill himself, as that wasn’t possible.
Once a dungeon’s [Hard] difficulty was cleared, it couldn’t be challenged again.
A harsh restriction. Still, there were plenty of other skills out there.
Eventually, they reached [Hub City] and made their way through the streets to Merek’s alchemist shop.
"Oh?" Merek’s eyes widened when he saw them. "Did you...?"
Leon answered by placing the materials on the counter.
"All of them," he said. "And this quest is completed for both of us."
Merek didn’t question it.
He simply laughed, scooped everything up, and immediately got to work, his expression full of excitement.

sentences.text: Leon’s gaze lingered on the list of items floating in front of him, one after another, his grin slowly widening as he took everything in.
[Undead Knight Essence x5: Consuming will increase constitution by 8.]
[Undead King Essence: Consuming will increase spirit by 10 and constitution by 5.]
[Undead King Scepter (Epic): +500 Magic Attack, +500 Spirit, +300 Agility.
Requirement: Level 15.]
[Undead Knight Armor x5 (Elite): +600 Defense, +400 Constitution, -100 Agility.
Requirement: Level 15.]
[Materials: Undead Core x6, Corrupted Bones x11]
[Sub-Talent Scrolls: Spirit Enhancement (D-Level), Basic Necromancy (E-Level)]
[Skill Book: Spectral Flames (Epic)]
"Pretty good," Leon nodded in approval, a satisfied smile spreading across his face.
For a single dungeon run, especially one taken far earlier than recommended, this haul was absurd.
Any other player would have considered themselves lucky to walk out with half of this.
Yet for Leon, it was simply confirmation that choosing the [Hard] difficulty had been the correct decision.
Then another panel appeared.
Ding!
[25/25 Undead Core, 50/50 Corrupted Bones, 1/1 Undead King Heart.]
[You have acquired all the materials needed for Merek’s quest.
Return to him to complete it.]
"Got enough," Leon said, turning toward Emilia with a grin.
"We can return."
As if on cue, a teleportation portal formed in the center of the chamber.
Pale blue light swirled quietly, stable and inviting.
Stepping through it would immediately send them out of the dungeon.
Emilia stared at the portal, then back at Leon, confusion written all over her face.
"But... we don’t have enough materials for both of us," she said slowly.
"There’s only one heart.
Won’t only one of us complete the quest?"
"No," Leon shook his head without hesitation.
"Trust me.
We’ll both get a resurrection stone."
She blinked at him, clearly unsure how that was even possible.
Still, after everything she had seen so far, doubting him felt pointless.
"...Alright," she nodded.
"I trust you."
From the fight against the Undead King and his knights, Emilia had leveled up to level 12.
She hadn’t received anywhere near as many items as Leon, but that was expected.
Her drop rate was normal.
His was anything but.
Leon didn’t waste time.
He consumed all the essences immediately.
Ding!
[+40 Strength, +10 Spirit, +5 Constitution.]
The increase was modest compared to some of his other gains, but every point mattered.
At higher levels, even small increases translated into noticeable boosts in combat power.
Next, Leon attempted to fuse the Undead Knight Armor pieces.
One attempt failed.
The second succeeded.
Ding!
[Undead Knight Armor +2 (Elite): +800 Defense, +500 Constitution, -80 Agility.
Requirement: Level 15.]
"Not bad," Leon muttered.
He couldn’t equip it yet due to the level requirement, but the stats were solid.
Heavy armor like this was meant for frontline fighters, and once he reached level 15, it could serve as a temporary upgrade.
Leon then turned toward Emilia and casually tossed two items her way.
"You can take these," he said.
"The scepter and the skill book."
Emilia caught them reflexively, then froze when she saw what they were.
The [Undead King Scepter].
And an Epic skill book.
Her eyes widened.
"You’re giving these to me?" she asked, clearly shocked.
"I can’t use the scepter," Leon replied calmly.
"And while I could learn [Spectral Flames], it’ll benefit us more if you do.
You getting stronger helps me too."
For a moment, Emilia just stared at him.
Then suddenly, she hugged him.
"Thanks—!"
Realizing what she had done a split second later, she pulled back instantly, her face turning bright red.
"S-Sorry!"
Leon blinked, then chuckled softly.
"It’s fine."
Trying to hide her embarrassment, Emilia immediately focused on the skill book.
She poured mana into it without hesitation.
Fwoosh!
The book dissolved into motes of light that flowed into her body.
Ding!
[You have learned "Spectral Flames"]
"Yes," Emilia smiled, clearly pleased.
She then stored the Undead King Scepter away for later use.
Leon nodded.
"Your skills are still underleveled, though.
We’ll need a lot of [Skill Stones]."
"I know..." Emilia sighed lightly.
"They’re hard to find."
"I already have a place in mind," Leon replied.
A place that could supply skill stones in bulk.
A dangerous place, but perfect.
It wasn’t time to go there yet.
Not now.
Leon shifted his attention to the last items left in his storage: the sub-talent scrolls.
He took out the first one: [Spirit Enhancement (D-Level)]
Without hesitation, he poured mana into it and tore it apart.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have learned the D-Level Sub-Talent: "Spirit Enhancement"]
[Spirit Enhancement (D-Level): Permanently increases spirit by 30%.]
Leon exhaled slowly.
"Amazing."
With this, all four of his core attributes were now enhanced by sub-talents.
Strength, agility, constitution, and spirit, each one boosted permanently.
He would need to find ways to evolve them further, but for now, this alone was already monstrous.
Then there was the last scroll: [Basic Necromancy (E-Level)]
Leon paused for a moment.
This was rare.
Extremely rare.
Necromancy-related monsters were uncommon to begin with.
Getting a sub-talent scroll from one was even rarer.
And unless your talent or title was tied to necromancy, there were very few ways to acquire something similar.
Even in his past life, Leon had only met a handful of necromancers.
Among them, one stood above the rest.
The [UndeadLiege] was her ID.
A player capable of summoning thousands of undead soldiers, wiping out entire armies alone.
Leon shook his head lightly.
"No point thinking about that now."
He poured mana into the scroll and tore it apart.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have learned the E-Level Sub-Talent: "Basic Necromancy"]
Unlike the others, this sub-talent’s panel was larger.
Leon immediately opened it.
[Basic Necromancy (E-Level): You become a novice necromancer, able to summon undead skeletons to aid you.]
[Skeleton Summon Limit: 3.]
[Each summoned skeleton has 25% of your base stats.]
"Interesting."
That meant as Leon grew stronger, his summoned skeletons would scale with him.
Right now, each one would only have around four to five hundred points in their main stats.
Enough to distract enemies, maybe help with weaker monsters, but not enough to pose a real threat.
Still, the potential was there.
"I’ll have to test it later," Leon murmured.
"And find ways to boost them."
For now, he was satisfied.
"Done?" Emilia asked with a grin.
"You spent more time on loot than on the actual fight."
"I get a lot," Leon shrugged.
"And yeah.
It’s related to my talent."
"That just makes me more curious~"
Leon smiled but didn’t answer.
He could tell her.
He trusted her.
But revealing it now wouldn’t change anything as it didn’t help in battle.
His talent only truly mattered after enemies were dead.
Fwoosh!
"Wait," Leon said as they were about to head out, "Grab this."
Leon tossed all of the materials required for the quest to Emilia, who held them all in her hands and...
Ding!
[You have acquired all the materials needed for Merek’s quest...]
She also received the panel.
"Alright."
Leon then took the items once more and stored them in his storage space except for some of the [Corrupted Bones].
The two stepped into the portal, light enveloping them.
In the next instant, they reappeared outside the [Undead Temple].
Without stopping, they headed back toward [Hub City].
Along the way, a stray monster crossed their path.
Emilia raised her scepter and activated her newly learned skill.
Spectral Flames!
Ghostly fire surged forward, engulfing the monster and reducing it to ash almost instantly.
Her eyes lit up.
"Nice," she said happily.
"I’ve got two attacking spells now."
Leon nodded.
He didn’t even consider going back to farm the Undead King for the skill himself, as that wasn’t possible.
Once a dungeon’s [Hard] difficulty was cleared, it couldn’t be challenged again.
A harsh restriction.
Still, there were plenty of other skills out there.
Eventually, they reached [Hub City] and made their way through the streets to Merek’s alchemist shop.
"Oh?" Merek’s eyes widened when he saw them.
"Did you...?"
Leon answered by placing the materials on the counter.
"All of them," he said.
"And this quest is completed for both of us."
Merek didn’t question it.
He simply laughed, scooped everything up, and immediately got to work, his expression full of excitement.

chapters.title: Chapter 44: Completing Merek’s Quest, Two Resurrection Stones!
paragraphs: Since Emilia also held all the required items for the quest and had personally received the system panel confirming it, the system itself judged that she had completed the quest as well.
It was a neat loophole. One that very few players knew about.
As long as all required materials were present in a player’s possession at the moment of turn-in, and the quest panel acknowledged it, the system counted it as valid.
It didn’t matter who had gathered what, or how the materials were split beforehand.
Most people never discovered this simply because secret quests were rare, and even fewer involved shared materials. But Leon knew.
After several minutes of careful work behind the counter, Merek finally returned.
In his clawed hands were not one, but two stones, both faintly glowing with a soft, golden light.
He placed them down gently, one after the other, his grin wide and satisfied.
"Not many manage to complete my quest," Merek said, nodding slowly. "So here you go. Appreciate it."
Ding!
[Your reputation with Merek has improved.]
Leon wasn’t surprised.
Every native of [Eternal Ascension], what players casually called NPCs, had a reputation value tied to each individual player.
Improving it could open doors: better prices, exclusive interactions, rare crafting options, and sometimes even access to hidden quests or locations.
Of course, reputation wasn’t always something to blindly increase.
Some natives sided with the gods. Others answered directly to higher beings. And some were simply dangerous.
Leon would never aim to stay on good terms with everyone. That was a good way to die.
Still, Merek was a valuable ally.
Leon picked up one of the stones from the counter and casually tossed the other toward Emilia.
She barely caught it, instinctively gripping it with both hands.
[Resurrection Stone (Legendary): Will revive someone at the nearest "safe point" upon death. Automatically consumed if the user dies.]
"Oh my god..." Emilia whispered, staring at it. "This is... insane."
"Yeah," Leon nodded calmly. "I don’t plan on dying anytime soon, though. This is just insurance. Don’t let it make you careless."
"I won’t," Emilia said immediately, shaking her head.
Leon had seen it happen too many times.
Players who obtained resurrection items often started taking unnecessary risks, thinking death no longer mattered.
But those stones were rare. Extremely rare. Wasting one was equivalent to throwing away a miracle.
Leon would only rely on it if escape was truly impossible.
"If you have more materials, I can craft more things," Merek said casually. "Or buy them."
"Perfect," Leon replied.
He opened his [Storage Space] and pulled out everything he currently had that wasn’t immediately useful.
[Darkened Star Grass (Special Material)]
[Dark Tree Branch x5 (Uncommon)]
[Howled Wolf Claw x3 (Rare)]
[Elemental Stone x4]
He placed them all on the counter. Merek examined them carefully, his expression thoughtful.
"Hm. The branches, claws, and stones are for a blacksmith," he said. "Not an alchemist. But I can take the grass.
"That’s fine," Leon nodded.
"I’ll give you 500 Eternal Coins for it."
Leon didn’t hesitate. Special materials were rare, but he needed liquidity more than anything right now.
The transaction completed instantly. After that, they exchanged brief farewells and left the shop.
As they walked through the empty, broken streets of [Hub City], Emilia glanced back once.
"Are we going to see him again?"
"Yeah," Leon answered without hesitation. "He’s going to become a major alchemist."
Emilia blinked. "How do you even know that?"
"Feeling," Leon grinned.
The streets around them remained quiet, abandoned, and partially destroyed. Most players didn’t venture this far from the main square unless they had a specific reason.
But just as they were about to re-enter the central area—
Ding!
[30 minutes until the event of "Hub City" starts.]
A global announcement echoed through the city, reaching every eligible player between levels 10 and 15.
Leon’s eyes sharpened. Finally. He had been waiting for this.
Even in his past life, events were unpredictable. Some were remembered. Others were forgotten. And some... changed everything.
This one was new to him. Which made it even more interesting.
Leon and Emilia moved quickly, returning to the main square. Compared to earlier, the difference was night and day.
Players flooded the area from every direction.
"Finally, I’ve been waiting forever."
"I wonder what kind of event it is..."
The air buzzed with excitement and tension.
Most events involved rankings. Performance-based competitions where the best players earned the best rewards.
And sometimes, those rewards were powerful enough to define a player’s future.
Leon wasn’t interested in anything except first place. To him, anything below that barely mattered.
And thankfully, his current combat power gave him a real chance.
Still, events had one unfair aspect: level 15 players were allowed to participate.
That meant someone from a high-level world, blessed with an absurd talent, could appear and dominate everything.
Even so, Leon remained confident.
"Well," he said calmly, "we wait."
Minutes passed.
More and more players arrived. Some rushed in from nearby dungeons. Others sprinted across the wilds the moment they heard the announcement.
Even players from the [Undead Temple] hurried back, abandoning their runs to avoid missing the event.
The crowd kept growing.
Then—
Ding!
[5 minutes left before the event.]
By now, tens of thousands of players filled the square and surrounding streets.
"This feels strange," Emilia muttered, looking around. "There are so many people. Some of them are from intermediate and high-level worlds."
Leon scanned the panels of nearby players.
[World: Anglomera (Intermediate-Level)]
[World: Berid (High-Level)]
Different races. Different worlds. Different backgrounds. Universal Ascension didn’t discriminate.
Even Emilia looked surprised when she noticed elves that clearly weren’t from her world, Verdia.
"I guess it does make you feel small," she said quietly, "knowing how many worlds are involved."
"That’s the power of [Universal Ascension]," Leon replied. "But we’ll rise above them."
She smiled. "Fair."
Then—
Ding!
[Special Event: "Shadow Horde" will now start.]
[Difficulty: Nightmare.]
"...WHAT?"
"Nightmare difficulty?! Are you kidding me?"
"Hell no, I’m out."
A wave of panic spread through the crowd. And it made sense.
Events, like dungeons, had difficulty tiers: Normal, Hard, Hell, Nightmare, Abyss, Eternal.
Nightmare was the fourth tier. For an event limited to level 10-15 players, that was insane.
Ding!
[Objective: Defend "Hub City" from the advancing Shadow Horde.]
[Each monster defeated will grant points based on strength.]
[Players ranked highest on the leaderboard will receive the greatest rewards.]
[Rank 1 Reward: Mythical Treasure Chest.]
[Event Duration: 2 hours.]
[Good luck.]
Leon’s expression hardened. This was it. A Mythical Treasure Chest.
Something that could redefine his build entirely. There was no hesitation.
Leon took a slow breath, his grip tightening around his weapon.
No matter what appeared, no matter who stood in his way—
He was taking first place.

chapters.title: Chapter 45: Start Of The Shadow Horde Event, Killing Shadow Wolves
paragraphs: Fwoosh!
The moment the last event panels vanished, the air around [Hub City] shifted in a way that everyone could feel.
It wasn’t subtle. The temperature dropped slightly, the light dimmed, and a heavy pressure settled over the land like an invisible dome pressing down from above.
Far in the distance, a thick, rolling fog began to form.
It wasn’t normal fog. It was darker, denser, and it moved with intent, spreading outward until it completely surrounded the city from every direction.
Within seconds, the horizon disappeared, replaced by an endless wall of shadow.
This was the event’s boundary.
Once the fog finished closing in, a clear realization struck everyone present: this entire area had become an arena. Anyone inside it was now locked in.
There was no walking out, if you were here, you were participating, whether you wanted to or not.
That was exactly why the system always gave a thirty-minute warning before an event began.
It wasn’t just a courtesy for eager players to gather. But also was a final chance for anyone uncertain to leave while they still could.
Because once the event started, there were no second chances.
During events, death was final.
Emilia stood beside Leon, slowly turning in place as she took in the fog encircling them.
Her earlier excitement faded, replaced by a more cautious expression. Even someone as composed as her could feel how serious this was.
Then another panel appeared.
Ding!
[As the event progresses, the monsters that appear will become stronger and grant more points.]
[They will be unable to enter the city unless too many of them approach the gate.]
[Hub City] was technically a safe zone, but only under specific conditions.
If too many people chose to hide inside, refusing to fight, eventually, sheer pressure would overwhelm the gates, allowing the horde to flood in and slaughter everyone inside.
The event didn’t allow cowards. It punished them.
"We move now," Leon said calmly.
Emilia nodded without hesitation, gripping her scepter more firmly as they left the main square and headed outside the city.
Thousands of players were already gathering there, forming loose lines, small squads, or standing alone with weapons drawn.
No one joked anymore. Everyone stared at the fog.
And then—
Ding!
[The "Shadow Horde" has appeared.]
The fog churned violently, as if something massive was breathing within it.
A second later, shapes began to emerge, one after another, moving faster and faster until the ground itself trembled.
They came in waves.
Shadowy figures sprinted forward on four limbs, their eyes glowing faintly as they burst out of the fog in overwhelming numbers.
Leon activated [Appraisal] instantly.
[Shadow Wolf]
[Level: 10]
[Combat Power: 5,000]
[Details: Born from shadow fog. Highly aggressive and driven by bloodlust.]
At the sight of the panel, fear rippled through the crowd.
For some, it was reassurance. A combat power of 5,000 wasn’t low, but it wasn’t impossible either.
These monsters relied on numbers more than individual strength, and with tens of thousands of players present, the balance could still hold.
For others, though, the sheer volume of wolves pouring out of the fog made their legs feel heavy.
A group of elves near the front suddenly surged forward.
"Charge!" one of them shouted loudly. "We elves will prove our superiority today!"
Emilia watched them go, her expression tightening slightly, "They sound exactly like the people who betrayed me," she muttered. "Same confidence. Same arrogance."
"It’s fine," Leon grinned.
Before anyone else could react—
Fwoosh!
Leon shot forward, becoming a blur as he closed the distance between himself and the advancing horde.
Sword in one hand, staff in the other, he didn’t hesitate for even a moment.
This was an event built around points. And points were earned by killing.
Powerful Fireball!
The air condensed in front of his staff before erupting outward in a blazing sphere of compressed flames.
The fireball slammed into the front of the horde and exploded, instantly incinerating five shadow wolves where they stood.
Their bodies dissolved into black smoke before they even hit the ground.
Leon followed up immediately, channeling energy through his sword.
Crescent Slash!
A wide arc of compressed force tore through the air, cutting through a dozen wolves in a single sweep before dissipating.
Ding!
[You have killed x17 "Shadow Wolves" and gained 340 experience points.]
Leon smiled faintly. Another panel appeared almost immediately.
Ding!
[You have obtained 17 Points.]
"Good, though it seems these wolves don’t have any drops."
He opened the leaderboard without slowing his movements.
[Event Leaderboard:]
[1. Celestial - 17 Points]
"Perfect."
Not only was he in first place, but he had done it before most players had even properly engaged.
The experience gain was mediocre, but that didn’t matter. Events were about rankings, not levels.
Behind him, Emilia raised her scepter.
"My turn."
Divine light gathered at its tip, condensing into a blinding beam.
Divine Beam!
BOOM!
A column of radiant energy shot forward, piercing through the horde and erasing more than a dozen shadow wolves in its path.
Where the light passed, nothing remained. Shadow-type monsters were naturally weak to divine energy, and Emilia exploited that weakness perfectly.
Her name climbed rapidly on the leaderboard.
Seeing Leon and Emilia take the lead snapped the rest of the players out of their hesitation.
"Move!"
"Don’t let them take all the points!"
Skills erupted across the battlefield.
An elf leapt into the air and brought his blade down in a powerful overhead strike, cleaving through several wolves at once.
Mages unleashed spells, though none matched the sheer efficiency of Leon’s attacks.
Leon didn’t slow down. If a wolf closed in, his sword flashed, cutting it down instantly.
If they clustered together, fireballs and crescent slashes tore through them.
He avoided using [Lightning Strike]; single-target skills weren’t ideal when facing a tide like this.
Emilia stayed close, her spells sweeping across wide areas, [Divine Beam] and [Spectral Flames] working together to erase groups of enemies before they could overwhelm nearby players.
Their combat power made the difference obvious. They weren’t just participating. They were dominating.
By the time the last shadow wolf dissolved into smoke, the battlefield was littered with fading remains and exhausted players.
A few corpses lay among them, low-level players who had rushed in without preparation, but casualties were far fewer than expected.
A brief lull followed.
"Is that it? Already?"
"I need more points..."
People began checking the leaderboard.
[Event Leaderboard:]
[1. Celestial - 248 Points]
[2. MightyElf - 196 Points]
[3. ILoveExplosions - 193 Points]
[4. Saintess - 184 Points]
[5. HighUnity - 179 Points]
Whispers spread instantly.
"Who the hell is Celestial?"
"All the others are from high-level worlds. He has to be from one too."
"Maybe even eternal-level."
Leon ignored the murmurs. He was more surprised by Emilia’s ranking than his own.
Her area control and damage were exceptional, far beyond what most support-type players could achieve.
"That wasn’t the whole thing, right?" Emilia asked quietly. "It’s only been thirty minutes."
Leon smirked. "Not even close."
As if responding to his words, the air trembled again.
Ding!
[The Second Wave of the "Shadow Horde" is coming.]
Leon tightened his grip on his weapon.
"Of course," he muttered, "Here it comes."

sentences.text: Fwoosh!
The moment the last event panels vanished, the air around [Hub City] shifted in a way that everyone could feel.
It wasn’t subtle.
The temperature dropped slightly, the light dimmed, and a heavy pressure settled over the land like an invisible dome pressing down from above.
Far in the distance, a thick, rolling fog began to form.
It wasn’t normal fog.
It was darker, denser, and it moved with intent, spreading outward until it completely surrounded the city from every direction.
Within seconds, the horizon disappeared, replaced by an endless wall of shadow.
This was the event’s boundary.
Once the fog finished closing in, a clear realization struck everyone present: this entire area had become an arena.
Anyone inside it was now locked in.
There was no walking out, if you were here, you were participating, whether you wanted to or not.
That was exactly why the system always gave a thirty-minute warning before an event began.
It wasn’t just a courtesy for eager players to gather.
But also was a final chance for anyone uncertain to leave while they still could.
Because once the event started, there were no second chances.
During events, death was final.
Emilia stood beside Leon, slowly turning in place as she took in the fog encircling them.
Her earlier excitement faded, replaced by a more cautious expression.
Even someone as composed as her could feel how serious this was.
Then another panel appeared.
Ding!
[As the event progresses, the monsters that appear will become stronger and grant more points.]
[They will be unable to enter the city unless too many of them approach the gate.]
[Hub City] was technically a safe zone, but only under specific conditions.
If too many people chose to hide inside, refusing to fight, eventually, sheer pressure would overwhelm the gates, allowing the horde to flood in and slaughter everyone inside.
The event didn’t allow cowards.
It punished them.
"We move now," Leon said calmly.
Emilia nodded without hesitation, gripping her scepter more firmly as they left the main square and headed outside the city.
Thousands of players were already gathering there, forming loose lines, small squads, or standing alone with weapons drawn.
No one joked anymore.
Everyone stared at the fog.
And then—
Ding!
[The "Shadow Horde" has appeared.]
The fog churned violently, as if something massive was breathing within it.
A second later, shapes began to emerge, one after another, moving faster and faster until the ground itself trembled.
They came in waves.
Shadowy figures sprinted forward on four limbs, their eyes glowing faintly as they burst out of the fog in overwhelming numbers.
Leon activated [Appraisal] instantly.
[Shadow Wolf]
[Level: 10]
[Combat Power: 5,000]
[Details: Born from shadow fog.
Highly aggressive and driven by bloodlust.]
At the sight of the panel, fear rippled through the crowd.
For some, it was reassurance.
A combat power of 5,000 wasn’t low, but it wasn’t impossible either.
These monsters relied on numbers more than individual strength, and with tens of thousands of players present, the balance could still hold.
For others, though, the sheer volume of wolves pouring out of the fog made their legs feel heavy.
A group of elves near the front suddenly surged forward.
"Charge!" one of them shouted loudly.
"We elves will prove our superiority today!"
Emilia watched them go, her expression tightening slightly, "They sound exactly like the people who betrayed me," she muttered.
"Same confidence.
Same arrogance."
"It’s fine," Leon grinned.
Before anyone else could react—
Fwoosh!
Leon shot forward, becoming a blur as he closed the distance between himself and the advancing horde.
Sword in one hand, staff in the other, he didn’t hesitate for even a moment.
This was an event built around points.
And points were earned by killing.
Powerful Fireball!
The air condensed in front of his staff before erupting outward in a blazing sphere of compressed flames.
The fireball slammed into the front of the horde and exploded, instantly incinerating five shadow wolves where they stood.
Their bodies dissolved into black smoke before they even hit the ground.
Leon followed up immediately, channeling energy through his sword.
Crescent Slash!
A wide arc of compressed force tore through the air, cutting through a dozen wolves in a single sweep before dissipating.
Ding!
[You have killed x17 "Shadow Wolves" and gained 340 experience points.]
Leon smiled faintly.
Another panel appeared almost immediately.
Ding!
[You have obtained 17 Points.]
"Good, though it seems these wolves don’t have any drops."
He opened the leaderboard without slowing his movements.
[Event Leaderboard:]
Celestial - 17 Points]
"Perfect."
Not only was he in first place, but he had done it before most players had even properly engaged.
The experience gain was mediocre, but that didn’t matter.
Events were about rankings, not levels.
Behind him, Emilia raised her scepter.
"My turn."
Divine light gathered at its tip, condensing into a blinding beam.
Divine Beam!
BOOM!
A column of radiant energy shot forward, piercing through the horde and erasing more than a dozen shadow wolves in its path.
Where the light passed, nothing remained.
Shadow-type monsters were naturally weak to divine energy, and Emilia exploited that weakness perfectly.
Her name climbed rapidly on the leaderboard.
Seeing Leon and Emilia take the lead snapped the rest of the players out of their hesitation.
"Move!"
"Don’t let them take all the points!"
Skills erupted across the battlefield.
An elf leapt into the air and brought his blade down in a powerful overhead strike, cleaving through several wolves at once.
Mages unleashed spells, though none matched the sheer efficiency of Leon’s attacks.
Leon didn’t slow down.
If a wolf closed in, his sword flashed, cutting it down instantly.
If they clustered together, fireballs and crescent slashes tore through them.
He avoided using [Lightning Strike]; single-target skills weren’t ideal when facing a tide like this.
Emilia stayed close, her spells sweeping across wide areas, [Divine Beam] and [Spectral Flames] working together to erase groups of enemies before they could overwhelm nearby players.
Their combat power made the difference obvious.
They weren’t just participating.
They were dominating.
By the time the last shadow wolf dissolved into smoke, the battlefield was littered with fading remains and exhausted players.
A few corpses lay among them, low-level players who had rushed in without preparation, but casualties were far fewer than expected.
A brief lull followed.
"Is that it?
Already?"
"I need more points..."
People began checking the leaderboard.
[Event Leaderboard:]
Celestial - 248 Points]
MightyElf - 196 Points]
ILoveExplosions - 193 Points]
Saintess - 184 Points]
HighUnity - 179 Points]
Whispers spread instantly.
"Who the hell is Celestial?"
"All the others are from high-level worlds.
He has to be from one too."
"Maybe even eternal-level."
Leon ignored the murmurs.
He was more surprised by Emilia’s ranking than his own.
Her area control and damage were exceptional, far beyond what most support-type players could achieve.
"That wasn’t the whole thing, right?" Emilia asked quietly.
"It’s only been thirty minutes."
Leon smirked.
"Not even close."
As if responding to his words, the air trembled again.
Ding!
[The Second Wave of the "Shadow Horde" is coming.]
Leon tightened his grip on his weapon.
"Of course," he muttered, "Here it comes."

chapters.title: Chapter 46: The Dark Sentinels, Full Storage Space!
paragraphs: Several monsters began to emerge from the dark fog once more, their silhouettes forming long before their bodies became clear.
The ground trembled as they rushed toward [Hub City] for the second time, their footsteps heavy and synchronized, far more disciplined than the chaotic charge of the shadow wolves from before.
There were thousands of them.
But unlike the first wave, these monsters did not move like beasts driven purely by instinct.
They advanced in loose formations, weapons in hand, eyes glowing with a dull, oppressive light.
Even from a distance, it was obvious that these enemies were on an entirely different level.
Leon immediately activated [Appraisal].
[Dark Sentinel]
[Level: 13]
[Combat Power: 7,000]
[Details: Humanoid soldiers born from darkness and shadow.]
The moment the panel appeared, the mood among the players shifted.
A combat power of 7,000 was no joke. For most of the people who had barely survived the first wave, this was already beyond their limits.
Panic spread quickly, and within seconds, over fifty percent of the players who had fought the shadow wolves began to retreat.
Some ran back toward the city gates. Others simply stopped fighting altogether, choosing to stay far behind the frontline and hope that stronger players would handle everything.
Those who stayed were the confident ones. Talents from intermediate and high-level worlds.
People who understood that this was a [Nightmare] difficulty event and had accepted the risks the moment they decided to stay.
Leon and Emilia were among them. Neither of them moved back even a single step.
"This is more like it," Leon muttered, watching the sentinels approach.
As the first [Dark Sentinel] reached him, its shadow-forged blade swung down with surprising speed. Leon met it head-on.
Slash!
His sword cut cleanly through the sentinel’s torso, the dark body splitting apart before dissolving into smoke.
Leon raised an eyebrow slightly. "...Yeah. That’s about what I expected."
Even without Emilia’s [Strength Buff], his attacks were already more than enough to deal with enemies of this level.
The buff was still appreciated, of course, and it would make a real difference once stronger monsters appeared, but for now, he didn’t need it to dominate.
Beside him, Emilia didn’t waste time either.
Divine energy gathered at her scepter as she fired beams into the advancing ranks, her attacks tearing through multiple sentinels at once.
"Finding more support spells is my priority," she said while fighting, her tone calm despite the chaos. "If I can stack buffs properly, I’ll be able to support you far more efficiently."
Leon nodded as he cleaved through another sentinel. "My talent will make that easier."
He already had several plans forming in his mind.
Certain monsters, certain regions, even specific dungeons were known to drop support-type spells.
And if luck didn’t favor him, he could always buy them.
While cutting down enemies, Leon opened the [Trading House] mid-battle, his movements smooth and practiced. He filtered the listings, searching specifically for support spells.
The results made his eye twitch.
[Speed Buff (Uncommon Lv.1): 50,000 Eternal Coins.]
"...Absolutely not."
The price was absurd. Even for an uncommon spell, the demand was high enough to drive costs through the roof. Leon closed the interface with a faint sigh.
For now, he was broke. Still, that wouldn’t last forever.
The items he was acquiring were in high demand, and once he sold them, he would be swimming in Eternal Coins.
Until then, he’d simply have to work with what he had.
Powerful Fireball!
A blazing explosion erupted in the middle of the sentinel ranks, instantly wiping out a cluster of them.
Their defenses were better than the wolves’, but they still couldn’t withstand Leon’s magic.
After everything he and Emilia had gone through in the [Undead Temple] on [Hard] difficulty, enemies like this were well within expectations.
Ding!
[You have killed x25 "Dark Sentinels" and gained 1,865 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered. Items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
[You have obtained 50 Points.]
Leon glanced at the notifications. "Looks like these ones actually drop items."
He quickly noticed another important detail. The sentinels were worth significantly more points than the shadow wolves. Double, in fact.
That made sense. As monsters became stronger and fewer players were willing to fight, the system compensated by increasing point rewards. High risk, high reward.
Then another familiar chime echoed.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 13!]
[Due to "Heaven’s Blessing", you have gained 100 points in all attributes and 100 free points to distribute.]
"Nice."
Leon could feel the increase immediately. His body felt lighter, stronger, more responsive. Leveling up during an event like this was ideal, especially with his talent amplifying the gains.
Still, he didn’t dwell on it. Instead, he checked the items he had acquired.
[Dark Sentinel Essence x12: Consuming increases Strength by 5.]
[Dark Sentinel Armor x13 (Rare): +350 Defense, +300 Constitution, -50 Agility. Requirement: At least one darkness-based skill, trait, or sub-talent.]
Leon whistled softly. He had obtained a ridiculous number of armors already.
These weren’t items he planned to wear. Instead, they were perfect fuel.
He consumed all twelve essences without hesitation, feeling a surge of power ripple through him as his Strength increased by sixty points.
Then he went back to work.
Slash! Slash!
Another sentinel fell. And another.
The dark soldiers kept advancing, but none of them could stop Leon’s momentum.
Each kill made him stronger, and with Emilia covering his sides, their position remained unbreakable.
Eventually, another system message appeared.
Ding!
[Your "Storage Space" is full. Please free space or pay 10,000 Eternal Coins to add 10 slots.]
"Damn it," Leon muttered.
This was exactly why Eternal Coins were so important.
His talent relied entirely on items being sent to his [Storage Space]. Without space, the effects were interrupted.
And right after that, something else caught his attention.
The next sentinel he killed did not trigger the familiar drop-rate notification. No [100% Drop Rate has triggered].
Leon’s eyes narrowed. ’So that’s the limitation.’
If his storage was full, the talent couldn’t activate properly. It wasn’t a big issue, but it was something he had to manage carefully.
"Cover me for a moment," Leon said.
Emilia immediately nodded. "Got it."
She stepped forward, unleashing [Divine Beam] and waves of [Spectral Flames], holding the sentinels back as Leon focused on his inventory.
He consumed every remaining essence first.
[+75 Strength.]
Then he moved on to the armors. He had fifty-six [Dark Sentinel Armors].
Without hesitation, he began fusing them.
Fwish!
Ding!
[You have consumed two identical equipment... enhancement successful!]
Ding!
[You have consumed two identical equipment... enhancement failed!]
Again. And again.
Most enhancements failed, but Leon didn’t care. He kept going, methodically reducing the pile.
After about a minute, he was left with twelve [Dark Sentinel Armor +2].
He continued.
Ding!
Crack!
Failures stacked up, but eventually, he succeeded. Three [Dark Sentinel Armor +3].
"Done?" Emilia shouted, firing another spell as the pressure increased.
Leon looked up and grinned. "Yeah."
He closed his interface and surged forward again.
Powerful Fireball! Slash!
The sentinels fell once more, unable to regain momentum.
An entire hour passed like this, the battlefield slowly clearing as the remaining players worked together, pushing through exhaustion and danger.
Unlike the shadow wolves, these enemies fought back fiercely. They coordinated, blocked, and counterattacked. Still, one by one, they fell.
Leon continued consuming essences and fusing armors nonstop, keeping his storage manageable while growing stronger at an absurd pace.
And then, the hour ended.
Ding!
[The Third Wave of the "Shadow Horde" is coming.]
Only thirty minutes remained. Leon checked the leaderboard briefly.
[Event Leaderboard:]
[1. Celestial - 660 Points]
[2. MightyElf - 532 Points]
[3. Saintess - 501 Points]
He and Emilia were dominating the event. Even with elites from countless worlds present, they stood above nearly everyone else.
Another notification appeared.
Ding!
[+390 Strength.]
Leon exhaled slowly.
His Strength had skyrocketed.
It had passed the thousand mark long ago and kept climbing.
He could feel it in every movement, every swing of his sword.
An event like this, filled with endless enemies, was the perfect stage for his talent.
Just as he was about to examine the upgraded armor—
ROOOAR!
A thunderous roar shook the battlefield, freezing players in place.
From the depths of the fog, something massive began to emerge.
And Leon knew, without a doubt, that the final wave had arrived.

chapters.title: Chapter 47: The Event Boss, Darkness Wolves Leader
paragraphs: The final wave of the event finally revealed itself, and with it came the most dangerous presence on the battlefield.
"The Event Boss is here," Leon said calmly as he glanced toward Emilia. "Stay sharp."
Much like dungeons and zones that possessed a zone boss, large-scale events also had what players referred to as an event boss.
It was the strongest monster tied to the event itself, the core threat meant to push participants to their limits.
If left unchecked, it could wipe out entire groups, ruin rankings, and turn a promising start into complete failure.
And now, it had arrived.
In the distance, the remaining players watched as a massive figure emerged from the dark fog.
Even before its status panel appeared, its sheer presence alone made the air feel heavier.
The creature stood nearly five meters tall, its body shaped like a colossal wolf standing on powerful limbs.
Its fur flowed unnaturally, rippling like shadows caught in water, while its crimson eyes burned with intelligence and malice.
Long, jagged fangs protruded from its maw, each one gleaming as if forged from darkness itself.
Leon activated appraisal without hesitation.
[Darkness Wolves Leader (Event Boss)]
[Level: 15]
[Talent: Darkness Manipulation (C-Level)]
[Combat Power: 15,000]
[Details: Leader of the darkness wolves.]
A murmur rippled through the battlefield.
Fifteen thousand combat power.
That number alone crushed the morale of many players who were still standing.
For most of them, even reaching half of that would have been considered extraordinary.
Facing something at this level, especially after enduring two exhausting waves, felt impossible.
And the nightmare didn’t end there.
As the leader stepped forward, hundreds of smaller figures emerged beside it.
Though much smaller than their leader, they radiated an oppressive presence of their own, moving with lethal coordination.
[Darkness Wolf]
[Level: 15]
[Exclusive Talent: Kin of Darkness]
[Combat Power: 9,000]
[Details: Wolves born from darkness that follow the will of their leader.]
"Holy shit... there’s no way we can win this."
"Should we fall back? If we die now, it’s over."
"But if we leave, we lose all our points..."
Fear spread quickly. Many players hesitated, torn between survival and ambition.
Some backed away instinctively, while others stood frozen, their confidence shattered by the overwhelming power displayed before them.
Leon, however, didn’t move.
He stood still, sword resting loosely in his hand, his expression calm and unreadable.
Compared to the [Undead King] and the enemies inside the [Undead Temple], these monsters weren’t anything special. Strong, yes, but not beyond him.
Instead of panicking, Leon used the brief window before the wolves closed the distance to check his [Storage Space].
After nonstop fusions during the second wave, something remarkable had happened.
One of the armors had reached its max level.
[Dark Sentinel Armor +4 (Rare): +1,000 Defense, +600 Constitution, -10 Agility. Requirement: At least one darkness-based skill, trait, or sub-talent.]
"...Damn," Leon muttered.
The difference was massive. This piece alone eclipsed anything he had worn so far.
Without hesitation, he removed the [Earth Snake Armor +2] and equipped the new armor.
The moment it settled onto his body, he could feel the defensive boost immediately, like an invisible wall reinforcing his frame.
Then he looked up. The darkness wolves were already close enough to see their distorted reflections in his blade.
’I’ll need to keep consuming drops and managing my storage mid-fight,’ Leon thought calmly. ’This is going to be messy.’
But before the clash truly began—
Fwoosh!
An arrow shot through the air from behind Leon and Emilia, cutting past them with terrifying speed. It slammed directly into the [Darkness Wolves Leader].
For a split second, everything went silent.
Then—
BOOM!
A violent explosion erupted around the leader’s head, sending fragments of shadow flying outward.
The blast staggered the massive beast, tearing through part of its dark fur and drawing an enraged roar from its throat.
It didn’t die. But it was clearly injured.
Leon and Emilia exchanged a sharp look. They both recognized that attack.
It was the same explosive arrow that had targeted them earlier while they were heading toward [Hub City].
"That means..." Emilia muttered.
"The player killers are here," Leon finished, his gaze hardening.
He immediately turned around, scanning the crowd, but found nothing obvious. Dozens of players wielded bows. Pinpointing the attacker in this chaos was nearly impossible.
Still, one thing was certain.
"Be careful," Leon said quietly. "They already tried to kill us once. There’s no reason to believe they won’t try again."
Even if they didn’t act immediately, the fact that they had attacked at all meant they were prepared for confrontation.
Leon didn’t hesitate.
Powerful Fireball!
The blazing sphere shot forward and slammed into the leader’s face, exploding on impact and tearing away more of its shadowy flesh.
Divine Beam!
Emilia followed instantly, her beam of holy light scorching the monster’s side and forcing another roar from its throat.
In less than ten seconds, the Event Boss had taken heavy damage. That alone was shocking.
But what truly caught Leon’s attention was the arrow from before. Anyone capable of dealing that much damage in a single strike was no ordinary player.
’Combat power above ten thousand, at least,’ Leon concluded.
Even so, he wasn’t worried. No matter how strong they were, they wouldn’t stand a chance against him head-on.
The darkness wolves finally closed the distance, leaping toward the frontline players.
"ARGH!"
"Watch out!"
Claws slashed through the air as wolves lunged at anything within reach. Some players were sent flying, others barely managed to block or dodge in time.
Three darkness wolves targeted Leon at once. They never stood a chance.
Slash! Slash! Slash!
Their bodies dissolved into smoke almost instantly.
Ding!
[You have killed x3 "Darkness Wolves" and gained 1,200 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered. Items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
[You have obtained 12 Points.]
Leon’s lips curved into a grin. ’That experience gain is ridiculous, also 4 points per monsters now.’
He spared a quick glance at the drops, already planning how to manage them mid-battle.
[Darkness Wolf Claw x2 (Epic)]
[Darkness Fur Boots (Epic): +250 Agility, +100 Constitution. Requirement: Level 15.]
No essences. That was a slight disappointment, but the materials themselves were valuable.
The claws could be used to craft high-grade weapons, and the boots were solid equipment.
’I’ll either sell these or bring them to a blacksmith,’ Leon decided.
Materials couldn’t be fused, so he’d have to manage storage carefully. Still, everything here had value, and that was good enough.
ROOOAR!
A thunderous roar shook the battlefield.
The leader, enraged by the death of its kin and its own worsening injuries, unleashed its power. A dark aura spread outward from its body, enveloping the remaining wolves.
[Darkness Wolf]
[Combat Power: 10,500]
Their stats surged instantly. Their movements became sharper, their claws deadlier, their presence far more oppressive.
For most players, this was the breaking point.
Slash! Slash!
He cut down every wolf that came too close, his blade moving with brutal efficiency. Bodies piled up around him as minutes passed.
After fifteen minutes, dozens of darkness wolves had fallen at his feet.
The true problem, however, remained the leader.
As its health dropped further, it activated a familiar skill: [Darkness Barrier].
The same skill Leon possessed.
And combined with its C-Level talent [Darkness Manipulation], the barrier was absurdly strong.
Attacks from all directions slammed into it, arrows, spells, sword strikes, but they only managed to crack the surface.
Ding!
[Only 10 minutes remain.]
Most of the darkness wolves were dead now, but the leader and the elite wolves guarding it held their ground stubbornly.
The Event Boss was worth an enormous amount of points.
Whoever landed the killing blow would secure their position at the top.
Leon’s gaze sharpened.
"I’m ending this," he said calmly, stepping forward. "Buff my strength."
Emilia didn’t hesitate.
Strength Buff!
Her magic surged, wrapping Leon in a powerful aura that doubled his strength. Leon felt it instantly.
The power coursed through his body, his grip tightening on his sword as he charged forward.

"The Event Boss is here," Leon said calmly as he glanced toward Emilia.
"Stay sharp."
Much like dungeons and zones that possessed a zone boss, large-scale events also had what players referred to as an event boss.
It was the strongest monster tied to the event itself, the core threat meant to push participants to their limits.
If left unchecked, it could wipe out entire groups, ruin rankings, and turn a promising start into complete failure.
And now, it had arrived.
In the distance, the remaining players watched as a massive figure emerged from the dark fog.
Even before its status panel appeared, its sheer presence alone made the air feel heavier.
The creature stood nearly five meters tall, its body shaped like a colossal wolf standing on powerful limbs.
Its fur flowed unnaturally, rippling like shadows caught in water, while its crimson eyes burned with intelligence and malice.
Long, jagged fangs protruded from its maw, each one gleaming as if forged from darkness itself.
Leon activated appraisal without hesitation.
[Darkness Wolves Leader (Event Boss)]
[Level: 15]
[Talent: Darkness Manipulation (C-Level)]
[Combat Power: 15,000]
[Details: Leader of the darkness wolves.]
A murmur rippled through the battlefield.
Fifteen thousand combat power.
That number alone crushed the morale of many players who were still standing.
For most of them, even reaching half of that would have been considered extraordinary.
Facing something at this level, especially after enduring two exhausting waves, felt impossible.
And the nightmare didn’t end there.
As the leader stepped forward, hundreds of smaller figures emerged beside it.
Though much smaller than their leader, they radiated an oppressive presence of their own, moving with lethal coordination.
[Darkness Wolf]
[Level: 15]
[Exclusive Talent: Kin of Darkness]
[Combat Power: 9,000]
[Details: Wolves born from darkness that follow the will of their leader.]
"Holy shit... there’s no way we can win this."
"Should we fall back?
If we die now, it’s over."
"But if we leave, we lose all our points..."
Fear spread quickly.
Many players hesitated, torn between survival and ambition.
Some backed away instinctively, while others stood frozen, their confidence shattered by the overwhelming power displayed before them.
Leon, however, didn’t move.
He stood still, sword resting loosely in his hand, his expression calm and unreadable.
Compared to the [Undead King] and the enemies inside the [Undead Temple], these monsters weren’t anything special.

Instead of panicking, Leon used the brief window before the wolves closed the distance to check his [Storage Space].
After nonstop fusions during the second wave, something remarkable had happened.
One of the armors had reached its max level.

"...Damn," Leon muttered.
The difference was massive.
This piece alone eclipsed anything he had worn so far.
Without hesitation, he removed the [Earth Snake Armor +2] and equipped the new armor.
The moment it settled onto his body, he could feel the defensive boost immediately, like an invisible wall reinforcing his frame.
Then he looked up.
The darkness wolves were already close enough to see their distorted reflections in his blade.
’I’ll need to keep consuming drops and managing my storage mid-fight,’ Leon thought calmly. ’This is going to be messy.’
But before the clash truly began—
Fwoosh!
An arrow shot through the air from behind Leon and Emilia, cutting past them with terrifying speed.
It slammed directly into the [Darkness Wolves Leader].
For a split second, everything went silent.
Then—
BOOM!
A violent explosion erupted around the leader’s head, sending fragments of shadow flying outward.
The blast staggered the massive beast, tearing through part of its dark fur and drawing an enraged roar from its throat.
It didn’t die.
But it was clearly injured.
Leon and Emilia exchanged a sharp look.
They both recognized that attack.
It was the same explosive arrow that had targeted them earlier while they were heading toward [Hub City].

He immediately turned around, scanning the crowd, but found nothing obvious.
Dozens of players wielded bows.

chapters.title: Chapter 48: Dominating The Event, Mythical Treasure Chest
paragraphs: Fwish!
Leon moved through the battlefield like a streak of light as he engaged the leader of the darkness wolves.
The creature stood at the center of the chaos, towering over the other monsters as if it ruled the entire area.
Its body was larger than the rest, its fur darker, thicker, and constantly releasing waves of shadow that twisted the air around it.
Wherever it stepped, the ground cracked and dimmed, as if light itself refused to linger near it.
Around the leader, players were struggling just to stay alive.
Slash! Slash!
The wolf leader swung its massive claws without hesitation.
Two players who were just a bit too slow were caught in its reach.
The claws passed through them effortlessly, tearing armor apart like paper.
Their bodies split into pieces before they even had time to scream, and their bodies lay there, killed instantly.
Blood hadn’t even touched the ground before the smaller darkness wolves rushed in again.
They moved in packs, circling players, biting at legs, tearing into backs, and forcing everyone to split their attention.
Every time someone tried to focus on the leader, the smaller wolves punished them.
It was chaos. This wasn’t just a strong monster.
It truly deserved to be called an event boss.
But even as players panicked, shouted, and fell one after another, Leon felt none of that fear.
He stood his ground. His eyes were calm as he faced the wolf leader directly.
Darkness Barrier!
A familiar wave of shadow wrapped around Leon’s body, forming a barrier almost identical to the one surrounding the boss. The dark surface rippled slightly, dense and stable.
Without hesitating, Leon rushed forward.
Powerful Fireball! Lightning Strike!
Two spells activated at the same time. The fireball burned with intense heat, its core glowing white-hot as it tore through the air.
Lightning followed immediately after, crackling violently as it descended with terrifying speed.
BOOM!
Both attacks slammed directly into the wolf leader’s barrier.
Most players had already tried something similar. Their spells, skills, and attacks had all hit the barrier before, only to disperse harmlessly, leaving no mark at all.
But Leon was different.
Crack!
A sharp sound echoed across the battlefield.
A massive crack spread across the darkness barrier protecting the wolf leader, splitting the shadow like shattered glass.
For a brief moment, everything froze. Players nearby stared in disbelief.
Leon’s attacks had actually damaged it.
The reason was simple: Leon’s spirit was extremely high.
Spirit didn’t just increase mana or spell control. It directly boosted the damage dealt by magic attacks, stacking on top of skill level and quality.
Against a barrier-based defense, spirit mattered more than anything else. And Leon had plenty of it.
ROOAR!
The shadow wolves leader let out a furious roar, shaking the battlefield.
The moment it noticed the crack, it abandoned everything else.
Its eyes locked onto Leon. All of its killing intent focused on him alone.
The smaller wolves hesitated for a split second, sensing the shift in their leader’s attention. Then the leader charged.
It moved with explosive speed, crossing the distance in an instant. Its claws came down in a brutal strike aimed directly at Leon.
Slash!
The claws collided with Leon’s Darkness Barrier. But nothing happened.
The barrier didn’t even shake. The wolf leader froze mid-motion, its eyes widening slightly.
It attacked again.
Slash!
Still nothing.
The barrier remained perfectly intact, as if the attack had never happened at all.
Leon’s sub-talent was the evolved form of what the shadow wolves leader possessed.
The B-Level [Vessel of Darkness] talent wasn’t just stronger, it completely dominated darkness-based abilities.
Against darkness-element enemies, Leon held an overwhelming advantage.
To them, he was something higher. Something untouchable.
"Roar?"
The wolf leader tilted its head slightly, genuine confusion flickering in its eyes.
But it didn’t get time to think any further.
Slash!
Leon moved.
His sword flashed through the air several times in quick succession. Each strike carried clean precision, cutting through the cracked barrier like it wasn’t there at all.
The darkness barrier shattered completely.
Before the leader could react, Leon stepped in and swung once more.
The blade passed cleanly through the wolf leader’s neck.
Its massive head flew into the air before crashing heavily onto the ground.
The body collapsed a moment later. The battlefield fell silent.
"Nice!" Emilia shouted from afar, her voice filled with excitement.
Ding!
[You have killed 48 "Darkness Wolves" and gained 19,200 experience points!]
[You have killed "Darkness Wolves Leader (Event Boss)" and gained 5,000 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered...]
"Holy hell," Leon muttered, grinning as he saw the experience numbers.
They were massive. And of course, with that much experience...
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 14!]
[Due to "Heaven’s Blessing", you have gained 100 points in all attributes and 100 free points to distribute.]
A warm sensation spread through Leon’s body as his constitution, strength, agility, and spirit surged again.
He felt even sharper than before.
And right at that moment, just as the wolf leader’s head finished rolling across the ground, another announcement rang out.
Ding!
[Player "Celestial" has killed the "Shadow Wolves Leader" and thus gained 300 Points.]
Everyone participating in the event saw the announcement.
No matter where they were on the battlefield, no matter what they were doing, they all saw it.
And the meaning was clear. The event was decided. No one else stood a chance.
The remaining minutes passed calmly.
Without their leader, the darkness wolves were nothing more than experience fodder.
Players worked together, finishing them off one by one. There were no more desperate struggles, no more panic.
Soon enough...
Ding!
[The "Shadow Horde" event is now over.]
[You will receive your rewards based on your ranking in the event leaderboard.]
[May the will of the "Heavenly One" be with you.]
The panels appeared and vanished. Just like that, the first event of Leon’s new life was over.
Leon walked back to Emilia, a wide grin still on his face.
Ding!
[You have ranked first in the event.]
[Reward: Mythical Treasure Chest.]
The chest was instantly placed into his storage space along with everything else he had obtained.
"I was third overall," Emilia said as she checked the [Event Leaderboard]. "So I got a [Legendary Treasure Chest] and 50 free attribute points."
"That’s decent," Leon replied with a nod.
Around them, many players sat down on the ground, exhausted. Others returned to [Hub City] immediately, their expressions still tense as they checked their panels.
Even though Leon felt the event hadn’t been that difficult, for most of them, it had been a true life-or-death battle.
Emilia pulled her chest out of her inventory, and it dropped onto the ground with a heavy thud. It glowed with a bright golden light.
"Wow!" Her eyes sparkled. "This is insane...!"
Leon calmly pulled out his own chest from his [Storage Space].
Bam!
The [Mythical Treasure Chest] appeared in front of him, resting on the ground. Its golden glow was purer, brighter, and far more intense than the legendary one beside it.
Some might have wondered why Leon didn’t simply open Emilia’s chest for her: with his talent, he would receive all the items inside anyway.
But Leon didn’t even try.
[Eternal Ascension] clearly recorded ownership. A treasure chest could only be opened by its rightful owner.
So Leon focused on his own. He extended his hand and opened it.
Ding!
[100% Drop Rate has triggered, all items inside of the treasure chest have been placed into storage space.]
"Haha..." Leon chuckled softly as he checked his [Storage Space].
[Darkness Wolf Claw x20 (Epic)]
[Darkness Fur Boots +4 (Epic): +750 Agility, +400 Constitution. Requirement: Level 15.]
[Darkness Fur Boots +3 (x3)]
He had been fusing boots throughout the battle, so having several upgraded pairs made sense. The extras would sell well, and he wasn’t willing to risk fusing them further.
Then he checked the drops from the boss itself.
[Skill Book: Darkness Barrier (Epic)]
[Sub-Talent Scroll: Darkness Manipulation (C-Level)]
[Skill Stones x3]
[Shadow Gloves (Epic): +500 Attack, +300 Strength, +150 Agility. Requirement: Level 15.]
"Pretty good," Leon said quietly.
Finally, he turned his attention to the contents of the [Mythical Treasure Chest].
[Void Staff (Mythical): +1,000 Spirit. Requirement: Level 15.]
[Sub-Talent Scrolls: Constitution Enhancement (E-Level), Strength Enhancement (F-Level).]
[Skill Stones x15]
[Enhancement Stones x15]
[Elemental Necklace (Mythical): Boosts the power of elemental attacks by 25%.]
[Skills Books: Shadow Arrows (Legendary), Shadow Slash (Legendary).]
[Advanced All-Attributes Pill: Increases all attributes by 75.]
Every single item was powerful. But at the very bottom of the list, Leon noticed one final item.
And it read:
[Farlands Token (Mythical): Allows the user to enter the "Farlands", the most difficult dungeon of the "Lower Domain"].

chapters.title: Chapter 49: Farlands Token, Selling Items
paragraphs: "The Farlands?" Leon muttered quietly as he summoned the small [Farlands Token] into his palm.
The token floated just above his hand. It was a dull green color, slightly translucent, with a strange distorted symbol carved into its surface.
The symbol didn’t resemble any rune or language Leon recognized.
It twisted unnaturally, almost as if it didn’t belong in the same space as everything else.
Leon stared at it for a moment. Of course, he knew what [Tokens] and [Keys] were.
In [Eternal Ascension], items like these often granted access to secret zones, hidden dungeons, or special instances that couldn’t be reached through normal means.
Some were tied to quests, others to events, and a few were so rare that most players would never even see one.
But the [Farlands]? That was new.
Leon searched his memory carefully. In his past life, he had learned about countless dungeons, ruins, and forbidden zones within the [Lower Domain].
Yet no matter how hard he tried, the name didn’t ring any bells. That alone was unsettling.
The system itself had clearly stated that the [Farlands] was the most difficult dungeon in the entire [Lower Domain].
That wasn’t just a casual description. If it labeled something as the hardest, then it truly was at the absolute peak of danger.
Which meant one thing: Leon wasn’t touching it anytime soon.
At the very least, he would need to reach level 50. And even then, it wouldn’t be something he entered lightly.
He would need perfect preparation, top-tier equipment, and absolute confidence in his strength.
Leon clenched his fingers and dismissed the token, storing it safely back into his inventory.
That thing would wait. For now.
He turned his head slightly and glanced to the side.
Emilia was standing nearby, her focus completely locked onto her [Storage Space].
Her expression kept shifting between excitement and surprise as she scrolled through the items she had received from her treasure chest.
They weren’t the only ones. All around them, players who had survived the event were doing the same.
Some looked relieved. Others looked stunned. A few were laughing quietly to themselves, while many simply sat on the ground, too exhausted to even stand properly.
Almost everyone had received some form of reward.
Treasure chests of different grades had appeared for those who ranked decently, and even players who barely contributed still got something small.

He started using his items immediately.
First, he pulled out the [Advanced All-Attributes Pill]. Without hesitation, he consumed it.
The pill dissolved the moment it entered his mouth, releasing a powerful surge of energy that rushed through his entire body.
Leon felt heat spread through his limbs, his muscles tightening as his bones and veins strengthened.
Every single attribute increased by 75. The boost was immediate and noticeable.
Leon exhaled slowly, steadying himself as the sensation faded.
Next, he moved on to the sub-talent scrolls. He had already planned this part carefully.
He summoned the two new sub-talents he had acquired and brought them together with the ones he already possessed.
"Fuse," Leon said calmly.
The system responded instantly.
[Fusion successful.]
Leon’s eyes narrowed slightly.
Then—
[Fusion successful.]
Both worked.
Ding!
[You have evolved "Constitution Enhancement (E-Level)" to "Constitution Enhancement (D-Level)"]
Ding!
[You have evolved "Strength Enhancement (F-Level)" to "Strength Enhancement (E-Level)"]
Leon immediately checked the updated descriptions.
[Constitution Enhancement (D-Level): Permanently increases constitution by 30%.]
[Strength Enhancement (E-Level): Permanently increases strength by 20%.]
A slow smile formed on his face. This was a massive improvement.
His strength attribute was already his highest stat, and boosting it by another 20% pushed his physical power even further ahead.
Combined with the constitution increase, his survivability and damage output both jumped significantly.
He was becoming more unbalanced, in the best way possible.
After that, Leon took out the [Shadow Slash] skill book.
He inspected it carefully.
[Shadow Slash (Legendary): Blend into the shadows for 30 seconds then strike at an enemy with a powerful darkness-based attack. Requirement: Level 15.]
Leon nodded slightly.
"I’ll use it later," he thought.
It was a powerful skill, but without meeting the level requirement, there was no point rushing it.
Next came equipment.
Most of the items he had obtained, both from the monsters and the treasure chest, had a level 15 requirement. He was close, but not there yet.
Still, there were a few pieces he could use immediately.
Leon equipped the [Elemental Necklace (Mythical)] first.
To do that, he had to remove his [Purple Jade Necklace (Rare)].
The defensive effect of the jade necklace had served him well until now, but with [Darkness Barrier] at his disposal, he no longer relied on passive defense as much as before.
The offensive boost from the mythical necklace was far more valuable.
Then he turned his attention to his weapon. He pulled out the [Undead Sword +3 (Uncommon)].
[Undead Sword +3 (Uncommon): +1,100 Attack, +700 Strength, +200 Agility. Requirement: Level 14.]
Leon didn’t hesitate.
This sword was significantly better than the [Sword of Darkness +4] he had been using. The increase in attack and strength alone made the choice obvious.
He equipped it immediately.
A familiar weight settled into his hand, but the balance felt even better than before.
As for the remaining items, Leon planned to equip them all the moment he reached level 15. That wouldn’t take long.

"I’m done," Emilia said with a grin as she finally looked up. "I got a few [Stamina Potions], some skill stones and enhancement stones, an [Intermediate All-Attributes Pill], and... a new support-type skill!"
"A support skill?" Leon raised an eyebrow.
"Yeah," Emilia said, clearly pleased. "It’s called [Speed Buff]. It boosts agility."
Leon was genuinely surprised.
Support skills were extremely valuable, especially ones that enhanced movement and attack speed. The fact that Emilia had gotten one so early was a big advantage.
"That’s good," Leon said honestly.
Emilia hadn’t reached level 14 yet, but she was extremely close. With just a bit more grinding, she’d get there.
"Should we head back?" she asked. "Or do you need more time to sort things out? You probably got way more items than I did."
"I’m done," Leon replied calmly. "I still need to use the [Skill Stones] and [Enhancement Stones], but I’ll do that later."
Then he remembered something else: he still had free attribute points.
Leon opened his status panel.
[Free Points to Allocate: 200.]
Without hesitation, he spoke his choice aloud.
"100 in Spirit and 100 in Agility."
The points distributed instantly. Leon then checked his [Combat Power]. His eyes widened.
Leon’s mouth fell open slightly. He had already surpassed 20,000 combat power. And he wasn’t stopping there.
These were numbers that even level 20 to 25 players struggled to reach.
Yet Leon was only level 14. Still, he knew this wasn’t enough. Not for the future he was aiming for.
’I’ll need to help Emilia get stronger,’ Leon thought. ’And the others too, once they arrive.’
That was precisely why he had kept many of the valuable items in his storage instead of selling everything immediately.
Strength wasn’t something he wanted to monopolize alone.
Together, Leon and Emilia returned to [Hub City].
The city was filled with exhausted players. Some leaned against walls. Others sat on the ground. Complaints and discussions echoed everywhere.
"Damn it, that event was brutal."
"I almost died three times..."
"That [Celestial] guy completely dominated everything..."
As Leon entered the city, many heads turned. Players recognized him instantly. Whispers spread.
Some rushed toward him, excitement and greed clear in their eyes, asking him to join their party or guild.
Leon declined all of them with a simple shake of his head. He didn’t plan on joining any group.
Still, Leon wasn’t about to waste this opportunity.
"I’m putting a lot of items up for sale in the [Trading House]!" he shouted, his voice carrying across the area. "Check my ID if you’re interested!"
People froze for a moment. Then curiosity kicked in.
Leon immediately listed multiple items for sale, including several [Darkness Fur Boots +3], [Undead Knight Armor], [Sword of Darkness +4], and even a [Sub-Talent Scroll: Darkness Control (D-Level)].
At first, players didn’t expect much.
But the moment they opened the [Trading House] and saw what "Celestial" was selling... Their jaws dropped wide.
